definition_zh: n. 痛经；经期疼痛；原发性痛经；继发性痛经
definition_en: pain in the lower abdomen during menstruation, from mild cramps to pain severe enough to stop daily activity
core_image: 床头柜上热水袋与止痛药盒并排放着，日历上那几天被红笔圈出；诊室问卷的疼痛评分从 1 到 10 被圈到 8；超声屏上卵巢旁一个小囊肿横着测量线；女生蜷在沙发一角膝盖抵着小腹

sceneCN: 这里 dysmenorrhoea 指「经期出现的下腹疼痛」（第 1 个义项：痛经）；句意是她因为痛经两次没去上班。图中可辨识物件：热水袋、止痛药盒、被红笔圈出的日历。

senses.title: Pain during menstruation
senses.definition: pain in the lower abdomen during menstruation
senses.definitionCN: （名词）经期出现的下腹疼痛
senses.example: She was absent from work twice because of dysmenorrhoea.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为痛经两次没去上班。
senses.why: A hot water bag pressed against a lower belly while a calendar shows three days ringed in red.
senses.whyCN: 热水袋压在小腹上，日历上那三天被红笔圈了出来。

senses.title: The primary form
senses.definition: cramping pain with no underlying disease, common in the first years after periods begin
senses.definitionCN: （名词）没有器质性病变的痉挛性疼痛，多见于初潮后头几年
senses.example: Primary dysmenorrhoea usually begins within a year or two of the first period.
senses.exampleCN: 原发性痛经通常在初潮后一两年内开始。
senses.why: A school nurse log with the same three dates marked every month for one young student.
senses.whyCN: 校医记录本上，同一个年轻学生每个月都标着同样的那三天。

senses.title: The secondary form
senses.definition: pain caused by a condition such as endometriosis, often starting later in life
senses.definitionCN: （名词）由子宫内膜异位症等病症引起、往往较晚出现的疼痛
senses.example: Secondary dysmenorrhoea led the doctor to look for endometriosis.
senses.exampleCN: 继发性痛经促使医生去排查子宫内膜异位症。
senses.why: An ultrasound screen showing a small cyst beside the ovary with a measuring line across it.
senses.whyCN: 超声屏上卵巢旁有一个小囊肿，一条测量线横穿而过。

intro.en: Dysmenorrhoea is dys- meaning difficult, men- meaning month and -rrhoea meaning flow; put together the word names a monthly flow that comes with difficulty and pain.
intro.cn: dysmenorrhoea 由 dys-（困难）、men-（月）与 -rrhoea（流）组成；合起来这个词指称「来得艰难而疼痛的每月血流」。

items.en: The Greek prefix dys- means bad or difficult.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 dys- 意为坏、困难。

items.en: Greek men means month, the same root behind menstrual.
items.cn: 希腊语 men 意为月，与 menstrual 同一词根。

items.en: Greek rhoia means a flow, giving the ending -rrhoea.
items.cn: 希腊语 rhoia 意为流，给出后缀 -rrhoea。

items.en: Medical Latin assembled the parts into a term for painful periods.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语把各部分拼成表示经期疼痛的术语。

items.en: Medicine split the term into a primary and a secondary form.
items.cn: 医学把这个术语分为原发性与继发性两型。

items.en: American writing drops one letter and spells it dysmenorrhea.
items.cn: 美式拼写省去一个字母，写作 dysmenorrhea。

note.en: Dysmenorrhoea shares dys- with dysentery and -rrhoea with diarrhoea, while amenorrhoea and menorrhagia change the prefix to name too little or too much flow.
note.cn: dysmenorrhoea 与 dysentery 共用 dys-，与 diarrhoea 共用 -rrhoea；而 amenorrhoea 与 menorrhagia 换了前缀，分别指经血过少与过多。

dict_mnemonic.text: dysmenorrhoea ＝ dys-（困难、坏）＋ men-（月，希腊语 men）＋ -rrhoea（流，希腊语 rhoia）＝「艰难的每月血流」＝痛经。记住 men- 就记住一串：menstrual 月经的、menstruation 月经、amenorrhoea 闭经（a- 无）、menorrhagia 经血过多。-rrhoea 家族还有 diarrhoea 腹泻（dia- 穿过）。临床分两型：primary 原发性（无器质病变，初潮后一两年起，痉挛样），secondary 继发性（由 endometriosis 子宫内膜异位症等引起，出现较晚）。美式拼写省一个 o：dysmenorrhea。

definition_zh: 障碍物；阻碍；障碍；绊脚石；壁垒
definition_en: something that stands in the way and must be removed, crossed or gone around before progress can continue
core_image: 一条小径正中横着一块大石，行人提着包从旁边的窄缝侧身挤过
scene: 山道正中倒着一棵大树，骑车的人只好下车，抬着车从路旁的草坡绕过去。 A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
sceneCN: 这里指挡在路上的实物（第 1 个义项：物理障碍物）；句意为倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。图中可辨识物件：横倒的树干、单车、草坡、被堵住的路面；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 障碍物；阻碍；绊脚石

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示路线的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛道」；本词没有常见的派生词族
由本词加表示比赛的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛」
本词的复数形式，义为「多处障碍」

senses.title: A physical thing blocking the way
senses.definition: an object that physically prevents passage along a route
senses.definitionCN: 物理上阻止人沿路线通行的物体
senses.example: A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stand against; the noun first names a thing that literally stands in front of you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「站在对面」；这个名词最初指一件字面意义上立在你面前的东西。

senses.title: A hindrance to progress
senses.definition: a condition, rule or shortage that slows or prevents an intended outcome
senses.definitionCN: 减缓或阻止预期结果的条件、规则或短缺
senses.example: Lack of funding is the main obstacle to the research.
senses.exampleCN: 资金不足是这项研究的主要障碍。
senses.why: Once the thing standing in the way is no longer physical, the word keeps the same geometry: something is in front of the goal.
senses.whyCN: 当挡路之物不再有形，这个词仍保留同样的几何关系：有东西横在目标前面。

senses.title: A hurdle in sport
senses.titleCN: 体育比赛中的栏架与障碍
senses.definition: a fence, hurdle or water jump that a competitor must clear
senses.definitionCN: 选手必须越过的栏架、栅栏或水沟
senses.example: She cleared every obstacle in the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一圈越过了每一个障碍。
senses.why: Sport turns the blocking object into a designed test that must be jumped rather than removed.
senses.whyCN: 体育把挡路的物体变成设计好的考验：必须跳过，而不是搬走。

senses.title: A defensive barrier in warfare
senses.definition: a barricade, wire or ditch built to slow an advancing force
senses.definitionCN: 为迟滞对方推进而设置的路障、铁丝网或壕沟
senses.example: Engineers laid an obstacle belt before the position.
senses.exampleCN: 工兵在阵地前布设了一条障碍带。
senses.why: Here the obstacle is deliberately placed by the defender, so blocking becomes a tactic.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍由防守方故意设置，阻挡因此成为一种战术。

senses.title: A barrier to communication
senses.definition: a difference of language, culture or channel that keeps a message from arriving
senses.definitionCN: 语言、文化或渠道差异使信息无法抵达
senses.example: Poor translation created an obstacle between the two delegations.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的翻译在两个代表团之间造成了障碍。
senses.why: The thing in the way is now a gap in understanding rather than a stone.
senses.whyCN: 此时挡路的不再是石头，而是理解上的缺口。

senses.title: A mental barrier
senses.definition: an inner fear or belief that stops a person from acting
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人行动的内在恐惧或信念
senses.example: Fear of failure was the real obstacle, not the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 真正的障碍是对失败的恐惧，而不是考试。
senses.why: The stone moves inside the mind; the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 石头移进了心里；这个词也跟着去了那里。

senses.title: An economic or trade barrier
senses.definition: a tariff, quota or regulation that restricts the movement of goods
senses.definitionCN: 限制商品流动的关税、配额或法规
senses.example: The new tariff became an obstacle to exports.
senses.exampleCN: 新关税成了出口的障碍。
senses.why: Policy builds invisible walls, and the old stone word still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 政策筑起看不见的墙，这个古老的石头词依然适用。

senses.title: The sticking point in a negotiation
senses.definition: the one issue on which talks cannot move forward
senses.definitionCN: 使谈判无法推进的那一个议题
senses.example: Payment terms remained the chief obstacle to the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 付款条件仍是这笔交易的主要症结。
senses.why: In a room of words, one unresolved point can stand in the road like a boulder.
senses.whyCN: 在一屋子言辞里，一个未解决的议题也能像巨石一样横在路上。

senses.title: An object a machine must avoid
senses.titleCN: 机器必须避开的障碍物
senses.definition: an object detected by a vehicle or robot that must be routed around
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或机器人检测到、必须绕开的物体
senses.example: The robot stopped when its sensor detected an obstacle.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器检测到障碍物时，机器人停了下来。
senses.why: Robotics borrowed the plain physical sense and gave it a detection routine.
senses.whyCN: 机器人学借用了最朴素的物理义，并给它配上一套检测程序。

intro.en: Obstacle is a Latin verb for standing against, turned into a noun for the thing that stands in the way; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「站在对面」的动词，转为指「挡在路上的东西」的名词；英语经法语借入。

items.en: stare meant to stand, to remain in place; it is the root of a large family of standing words.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立、留在原地」，是一大类「站立」词的词根。

items.en: ob- meant against, in front of, or towards, and it fixes the direction of the standing.
items.cn: ob- 意为「对着、在前面、朝向」，它规定了「站」的方向。

items.en: obstare was to stand in front of a person or thing, hence to hinder.
items.cn: obstare 意为「站在某人或某物前面」，因此引申为「阻碍」。

items.en: The noun obstaculum named the thing that stands in the way, not the act of standing.
items.cn: 名词 obstaculum 指挡在路上的那个东西，而不是「站」这个动作。

items.en: Old French obstacle carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century; the first date is approximate but the line is clear.
items.cn: 古法语 obstacle 在十四世纪把这个名词带进英语；首见年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: Sport, trade, psychology and robotics each reused the stone-in-the-road image for a barrier of their own kind.
items.cn: 体育、贸易、心理学与机器人学各自把「路上的石头」这一意象用于本领域的壁垒。

note.en: The first group shares the standing root or looks close; the second group names nearby barriers and distinguishes how each one blocks.
note.cn: 第一组共享「站立」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的阻碍类词，说明中区分各自的阻挡方式。

entries.definition: Stubbornly refusing to change; it uses the same standing-against root for a person's will.
entries.definitionCN: 指固执地拒绝改变；用同一「站着对抗」词根来描述人的意志。

entries.definition: The medical field of childbirth; its Latin source named a midwife as one who stands before the mother.
entries.definitionCN: 指产科医学；其拉丁来源把助产士称为「站在母亲前面的人」。

entries.definition: To block or get in the way; it looks related but is built on a root meaning to pile up, not to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻塞或挡路；形近，但其词根意为「堆起」，而非「站立」。

entries.definition: Several things standing in the way at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时挡在路上的多件东西。

entries.definition: A structure or rule that keeps things apart; it separates rather than merely blocking a route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事物隔开的结构或规则；它重在分隔，而不只是挡住路线。

entries.definition: A small barrier to jump over, or a difficulty to pass; it suggests a sequence of tests.
entries.definitionCN: 指需跳过的矮栏，或需通过的难关；暗示一连串考验。

entries.definition: Something that slows progress, often a defect or burden carried along.
entries.definitionCN: 指拖慢进展的东西，常是随身带着的缺陷或负担。

entries.definition: An outside force crossing into a process and disturbing it; it acts on the process, not on the road.
entries.definitionCN: 指外部力量横插进一个过程并加以扰乱；它作用于过程，而非挡在路上。

entries.definition: A brake applied from inside a person or system; it restrains rather than stands in front.
entries.definitionCN: 指从人或系统内部施加的刹车；它重在拉住，而非立在前面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stand-against image, the real sport and trade phrases, and the real sister roots.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「站着对抗」意象、真实的体育与贸易搭配，以及真实的同根词。

normal.en: ob- is against and stare is stand: an obstacle is something standing against your path.
normal.cn: ob- 是对着，stare 是站立：障碍就是立在路对面挡住你的东西。

normal.en: The word is a noun for the stone, not for the walking; remove the object and the road reopens.
normal.cn: 这个词是那块石头的名词，不是走路的名词；搬走物体，路就重新打开。

normal.en: Obstacle course and obstacle race are two real sporting phrases.
normal.cn: 障碍赛道与障碍赛是两个真实的体育说法。

normal.en: A trade tariff is an invisible obstacle, but the geometry is the same.
normal.cn: 贸易关税是一道看不见的障碍，但几何关系完全相同。

normal.en: A robot detects an obstacle and routes around it, which is the plain sense in a machine.
normal.cn: 机器人检测到障碍物并绕行，这就是这个词在机器里的朴素用法。

abstract.en: An obstacle is defined by the direction you want to go; the same stone is scenery to a walker heading elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 障碍是由你想去的方向定义的；同一块石头，对朝别处走的行人只是风景。

abstract.en: Some obstacles are placed on purpose, and some are only feared; both stop the feet.
abstract.cn: 有些障碍是故意设置的，有些只存在于恐惧中；两者都能让脚停住。

abstract.en: The word is not an enemy but a test of route: every path proves itself by what it goes around.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是敌人，而是对路线的检验：每条路都用它绕开的东西证明自己。

examples.en: The fallen bridge was the last obstacle between the village and the hospital.
examples.cn: 断桥是村庄与医院之间的最后一道障碍。

examples.en: High interest rates remain an obstacle to small businesses.
examples.cn: 高利率仍是小企业的障碍。

examples.en: The negotiators cleared the main obstacle with a single compromise.
examples.cn: 谈判者用一次妥协清除了主要症结。

root: 来自拉丁语 obstaculum「阻碍物」← obstare「站在前面阻挡」← ob-「对着、在前」+ stare「站立」；经古法语 obstacle 于十四世纪进入英语。词源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a stone in the road through abstract hindrance, sport, warfare, language, mind, trade and negotiation to a robot's detected object.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从路上的一块石头，经过抽象阻碍、体育、战争、语言、心智、贸易与谈判，最后落到机器人检测到的物体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boulder sits across a narrow path, and every walker must squeeze past its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块巨石横在窄路上，每个行人都要从它边缘挤过去。

branches.en: THE STONE AND THE WIRE: a physical object, whether natural or built for defence.
branches.cn: 石头与铁丝：自然存在的实物，或为防御而设的实物。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE TARIFF: an abstract condition or a policy wall in the way.
branches.cn: 规则与关税：抽象条件或政策之墙挡在路上。

branches.en: THE HURDLE AND THE SENSOR: an obstacle designed for sport or detected by a machine.
branches.cn: 栏架与传感器：为体育设计的障碍，或被机器检测到的障碍。

branches.en: THE WORD AND THE FEAR: a gap in understanding or a belief that stops the feet.
branches.cn: 话语与恐惧：理解上的缺口，或阻止脚步的信念。

branches.en: THE STICKING POINT: one unresolved issue that holds a whole deal in place.
branches.cn: 症结：一个未解决的议题把整笔交易卡住。

intro.en: Obstacle is a prepositional prefix plus a verb of standing plus a noun ending for a thing.

definition_zh: 多样化；分散投资；业务多元化
definition_en: the process of adding variety, especially by spreading investments or activities
core_image: 一只篮子里的鸡蛋被分装到许多只篮子，每只篮子走向不同的方向
scene: 理财顾问把客户的资金分到不同行业与地区，以避免单一市场崩盘带来的冲击。 Diversification reduced the fund's loss when one sector collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里指「分散投资」，对应第 2 个义项：把资金分散到不同资产以降低风险；句意为一个行业崩盘时，分散化降低了基金的损失。画面要点：多只篮子、行业标签、下跌曲线。

senses.title: The general process of adding variety
senses.definition: the act of making something include a wider range of types
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物包含更广泛类型的行为
senses.example: Diversification of the curriculum widened student choice.
senses.exampleCN: 课程多样化扩大了学生的选择。
senses.why: The noun names the act of turning one kind into many, the most general reading of the verb behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指把一种变成多种的动作，是背后动词最一般的读法。

senses.title: Spreading investments
senses.definition: the practice of spreading money across assets so that one failure does not sink the whole
senses.definitionCN: 把资金分散到不同资产，使单一失败不至于拖垮整体
senses.example: Diversification cannot remove risk, only redistribute it.
senses.exampleCN: 分散投资不能消除风险，只能重新分配风险。
senses.why: In finance the many kinds are many holdings; the purpose is not variety for its own sake but spreading the chance of loss.
senses.whyCN: 在金融中，多种类就是多项持有；目的不是为多样而多样，而是分散损失的可能性。

senses.title: Entering new lines of business
senses.definition: a company's expansion into products or markets different from its original one
senses.definitionCN: 公司扩展到与原业务不同的产品或市场
senses.example: Diversification into software saved the publisher.
senses.exampleCN: 向软件业务多元化拯救了这家出版商。
senses.why: A firm with one product is a basket with one egg, so the word describes adding other baskets of revenue.
senses.whyCN: 只有一种产品的公司就像只放一枚鸡蛋的篮子，这个词因此指增添其他收入篮子。

senses.title: Spreading across regions
senses.definition: the expansion of activity into different countries or regions
senses.definitionCN: 把活动扩展到不同国家或地区
senses.example: Geographic diversification protected sales during the home slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 地域分散化在本国放缓期间保住了销售。
senses.why: The many kinds here are many places: a collapse in one region is offset by activity elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这里的多种类是多个地方：一个地区的崩塌可由别处的活动来抵消。

senses.title: Crop diversification
senses.definition: the practice of growing several crops instead of relying on one
senses.definitionCN: 种植多种作物而不是依赖单一作物的做法
senses.example: Crop diversification improved the soil and the farmer's income.
senses.exampleCN: 作物多样化改善了土壤，也提高了农民收入。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the financial logic to the field: several crops hedge against weather and price swings.
senses.whyCN: 农业把金融逻辑搬到田里：几种作物共同对冲天气与价格波动。

senses.title: Economic diversification
senses.definition: the broadening of a regional or national economy beyond one industry
senses.definitionCN: 把地区或国家经济扩展到单一产业之外
senses.example: Oil revenue funded the country's economic diversification.
senses.exampleCN: 石油收入资助了这个国家的经济多元化。
senses.why: A whole economy can be a single basket, so the word scales up from a firm to a state.
senses.whyCN: 整个经济体也可以是一只单一的篮子，于是这个词从公司放大到国家。

senses.title: Biological diversification
senses.definition: the increase of variety among species or genes over time
senses.definitionCN: 物种或基因随时间增加多样性
senses.example: Island isolation drove rapid diversification of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿隔离推动了这些鸟类的快速分化。
senses.why: Biology uses the same shape without human choice: one ancestral form branches into many forms.
senses.whyCN: 生物学使用同样的形状，却没有人为选择：一个祖型分化为许多类型。

senses.title: The resulting mixed state
senses.titleCN: 分散之后形成的混合状态
senses.definition: the condition of being made up of varied parts rather than one
senses.definitionCN: 由多种成分而非单一成分构成的状态
senses.example: The portfolio's diversification made its returns smoother.
senses.exampleCN: 这个组合的分散状态使其回报更平稳。
senses.why: The word can name not only the act but the result: a whole that is now visibly made of many parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅能指动作，也能指结果：一个如今明显由许多部分构成的整体。

intro.en: Diversification is an English noun built on Latin roots meaning to turn apart and to make. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: diversification 是英语名词，建立在表示「转向别处」与「制造」的拉丁词根上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and it underlies divertere, convertere and a large family of English words about turning.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动，是 divertere、convertere 以及一大批表示「转」的英语词的底层。

items.en: Diversus meant turned in different directions, hence various or separate, the source of diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 意为被转向不同方向，因此指多样或分开，是 diverse 与 diversity 的来源。

items.en: The verb joined diversus with facere 'to make', literally to make things turn apart, that is, to make them varied.
items.cn: 这个动词把 diversus 与 facere「制造」结合，字面是使事物转向不同方向，也就是使之多样。

items.en: French carried the verb into ordinary use, and English borrowed the verb in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词带入日常使用，英语在十七世纪借入了该动词。

items.en: The noun ending -ification names the process of making, so diversification is literally the making of variety.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ification 表示「使……的过程」，所以 diversification 字面上就是「使多样」。

items.en: Twentieth-century finance and management gave the noun its specialized readings: spreading holdings, markets and products.
items.cn: 二十世纪的金融与管理学赋予这个名词专门含义：分散持有、市场与产品。

note.en: The first group is built from the same turning root; the second group names the result or a neighboring strategy.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「转」的词根上；第二组指结果或相邻策略。

entries.definition: The state of having many different kinds; diversification is the act of producing that state.
entries.definitionCN: 具有许多不同种类的状态；diversification 是产生这种状态的动作。

entries.definition: Varied or different; it describes the parts, while diversification names the change that creates them.
entries.definitionCN: 多样的、不同的；它描述各个部分，而 diversification 指创造这些部分的变化。

entries.definition: To turn something aside or to entertain; it shares the turning image but has no sense of adding variety.
entries.definitionCN: 使转向一旁，或使娱乐；共享「转」的意象，但没有增加多样的意思。

entries.definition: A change of route or an amusement; it turns one thing away rather than multiplying kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改道或消遣；它是把一样东西转开，而不是增加种类。

entries.definition: Distributing something over a wider area; in finance it is the practical effect of diversification.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物分布到更广的范围；在金融中它是分散化的实际效果。

entries.definition: Making a range wider; it stresses extent, while diversification stresses the addition of different types.
entries.definitionCN: 使范围更宽；强调广度，而分散化强调加入不同类型。

entries.definition: Growth in size or reach; expansion can stay in one line, while diversification must cross into another.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或范围的扩大；扩张可以停留在同一业务线，而多元化必须跨到另一条。

entries.definition: Taking an offsetting position to reduce risk; hedging is one reason to diversify, not the same action.
entries.definitionCN: 建立对冲头寸以降低风险；对冲是分散化的一个理由，而不是同一动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real turning root, the real making suffix and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「转动」词根、真实的「制造」后缀与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The first half means turned apart, the second half means making, so the word is making things turn apart.
normal.cn: 前半意为转向不同方向，后半意为制造，所以这个词就是使事物分向多处。

normal.en: Finance applies it to eggs and baskets: many holdings instead of one.
normal.cn: 金融把它用到鸡蛋与篮子上：多项持有而不是只有一项。

normal.en: Business applies it to products and regions; agriculture applies it to crops.
normal.cn: 企业把它用到产品与地区；农业把它用到作物。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: portfolio, product, geographic, economic, crop.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出尺度：组合、产品、地域、经济、作物。

normal.en: Diversity is the state; diversification is the act that produces it.
normal.cn: diversity 是状态，diversification 是产生该状态的动作。

abstract.en: Picture one egg in one basket, then the same egg copied into many baskets walking in different directions.
abstract.cn: 想象一只篮子里放一枚鸡蛋，随后同一枚蛋被分装到许多只走向不同方向的篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a single road splitting into many roads, so no closure can stop all travel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成许多条，任何一处封闭都无法阻断全部通行。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree branching outward, the same shape as a portfolio spreading outward.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树向外分枝，与投资组合向外分散是同一个形状。

examples.en: Diversification is the first rule taught to new investors.
examples.cn: 分散投资是教给新投资者的第一条规则。

examples.en: The region's diversification away from mining took a decade.
examples.cn: 该地区摆脱对矿业的依赖、走向多元化花了十年。

examples.en: Genetic diversification helps a species survive a new disease.
examples.cn: 遗传多样化帮助物种挺过新的疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分成许多样」——把鸡蛋分到许多篮子里 → 分散投资、多样化

root: 由拉丁语 diversus「转向不同方向的、多样的」与 facere「制造」结合，经法语进入英语；名词后缀表示「使……的过程」，故字面义为「使多样」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general act of adding variety to its financial, business, regional, agricultural, economic and biological applications, and finally to the mixed state it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的「增加多样」动作，转到金融、企业、地域、农业、经济与生物上的应用，最后落在它所产生的混合状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eggs from one basket distributed among many baskets heading in different directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子里的鸡蛋被分到许多只走向不同方向的篮子。

branches.en: GENERAL ACT: one kind is deliberately turned into many kinds.
branches.cn: 一般动作：一种被有意变成多种。

branches.en: INVESTMENT AND RESULT: money is spread across assets, and the portfolio ends up visibly mixed.
branches.cn: 投资与结果：资金分散到各种资产，组合最终呈现为可见的混合体。

branches.en: BUSINESS AND PLACE: a firm adds new lines and new regions so no single market decides its fate.
branches.cn: 企业与地点：公司增添新业务线与新地区，使单一市场无法决定其命运。

branches.en: FIELD AND STATE: crops and whole economies are diversified for the same hedge against one failure.
branches.cn: 田地与国家：作物与整个经济体为同样的「防单一失败」而对冲。

branches.en: NATURAL BRANCHING: evolution produces variety without a human planner.
branches.cn: 自然分枝：演化在没有人类规划者的情况下产生多样性。

intro.en: Diversification is built from Latin pieces that still work productively in English: a turning root, a making suffix and a process ending.
intro.cn: diversification 由仍在英语中能产的拉丁成分构成：一个「转」的词根、一个「制造」的后缀与一个表过程的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere 'to turn' gives divert, convert and reverse; diversus adds the idea of turning apart, and facere supplies the making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere「转」衍生 divert、convert 与 reverse；diversus 增添「转向别处」的意思，facere 提供「制造」。

items.example: The prefix pushes the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作推向外侧。

items.example: The root appears in convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在转变与反转等词里。

items.example: To simplify is to make simple.
items.exampleCN: 简化就是使某物变简单。

items.example: Beautification is the process of making beautiful.
items.exampleCN: 美化就是使某物变美的过程。

items.example: Farmers diversify their crops.
items.exampleCN: 农民使作物多样化。

items.example: The firm is now diversified.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司如今已多元化。

items.example: Diversification took three years.
items.exampleCN: 多元化用了三年。

items.example: The forest has great diversity.
items.exampleCN: 这片森林多样性很高。

items.example: The city has a diverse population.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市人口多样。

items.example: They diverted traffic around the works.
items.exampleCN: 他们让车流绕开施工路段。

definition_zh: 潮汐的；与潮汐有关的；受潮水涨落支配的
definition_en: relating to the tide, the regular rise and fall of sea level caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun
core_image: 海水沿着同一道岸坡一天两次爬上来，又顺着同一个坡退回去，像有人在极慢地呼吸
scene: 沿海公路旁，测量员把潮汐表摊在引擎盖上，对照岸边的刻度说， Records of tidal water levels from this bay go back two centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 tidal 指「与潮汐这一自然现象有关的」（第 1 个义项：潮汐的、潮汐观测的）；句意为：这个海湾的潮位记录可以追溯到两百年前。

pos.zh: 潮汐的；与潮汐有关的
受潮水涨落支配的；随潮汐节律的（多作定语，比较级罕用）

forms.label: 比较级（关系形容词，罕用）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成：以潮汐的方式；随潮汐节律地
由「潮」加「陆地」构成的复合词：受潮水淹没的滩地
由「潮」加「线」构成的复合词：高潮退去后留下的杂物线、潮线
由「潮」加「水」构成的复合词：受潮水推动的水；潮水灌溉的低地
由「潮」加「闸门」构成的复合词：挡潮闸，退潮时放水、涨潮时挡住海水

senses.title: Of the tide as a phenomenon
senses.definition: relating to the tide as a physical phenomenon, including its timing, its height and the study of it
senses.definitionCN: 与潮汐这一物理现象有关的，包括其时刻、高度以及相关研究
senses.example: Records of tidal water levels from this bay go back two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个海湾的潮位记录可以追溯到两百年前。
senses.why: tide began as a word for 'time', and -al means 'of or belonging to'; tidal therefore says 'of the tide' before it narrows to any particular place.
senses.whyCN: tide 最初是「时间」之词，-al 表示「属于……的」；因此 tidal 首先只是「潮汐的」，之后才收窄到具体场合。

senses.title: A place the tide governs
senses.definition: of a harbour, bay or stretch of shore that is open to the tide and whose water level changes with it
senses.definitionCN: 指敞开迎潮、水位随潮水升降的港口、海湾或河岸
senses.example: The harbour is tidal, so boats leave before the water drops.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口受潮水支配，所以船只要在水位退下前离港。
senses.why: a place described by what controls it takes the relational adjective; a tidal harbour is one where the tide, not the harbour, sets the water level.
senses.whyCN: 用支配它的力量来描写一个地点时就用这个关系形容词；受潮港口的意思是潮水而非港口本身决定水位。

senses.title: Driven by the tide
senses.definition: using the rise and fall of the tide as a source of motion or electric power
senses.definitionCN: 把潮水的涨落当作动力或电力来源的
senses.example: A tidal scheme could light the island twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一套潮汐发电方案能一天两次为这座岛供电。
senses.why: the adjective of origin also marks the source of power: what belongs to the tide can be turned into what runs on the tide.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示来源的形容词也能标出动力来源：属于潮汐的东西，可以被改造成靠潮汐运转的东西。

senses.title: Of the intertidal strip
senses.definition: of the zone between the high and low water marks, covered at high tide and bare at low tide
senses.definitionCN: 指高水位线与低水位线之间、涨潮被淹、退潮露出的地带
senses.example: Crabs wait out the low water in tidal pools.
senses.exampleCN: 螃蟹在潮池里熬过退潮的那段时间。
senses.why: that strip has no everyday name of its own, so the adjective does the work: it is the part of the shore the tide owns.
senses.whyCN: 那条地带在日常生活里没有专门名称，于是由形容词承担：它是岸上归潮水所有的那一段。

senses.title: Reversing with the tide
senses.definition: of a current or stream whose direction turns with the flood and the ebb
senses.definitionCN: 指方向随涨潮与退潮而反转的水流
senses.example: Pilots time their entry to a favourable tidal stream.
senses.exampleCN: 引航员会掐着顺向的潮流水势进港。
senses.why: a stream that turns is 'of the tide' in direction as well as in schedule, and the adjective covers both at once.
senses.whyCN: 会掉头的水流在方向上和时间上都「属于潮汐」，一个形容词同时覆盖这两层。

senses.title: Keeping tidal time
senses.definition: of a rhythm in a living thing that is set by the tide rather than by daylight
senses.definitionCN: 指生物体内由潮汐而非日照设定的节律
senses.example: Shorebirds feed on a tidal clock rather than on the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 滨鸟按潮汐的钟点觅食，而不是按太阳的钟点。
senses.why: biology needed a word for clocks the moon winds, and the existing adjective supplied it without any new coinage.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要为「月亮上弦的钟」找一个词，现成的形容词直接顶上，不必再造新词。

senses.title: Reached by the tide upstream
senses.definition: of the lower course of a river that salt water enters and pushes back twice a day
senses.definitionCN: 指海水每天两次灌入并顶托的河流下游段
senses.example: The lower river is tidal as far as the weir.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的下游一直到拦河堰都是感潮的。
senses.why: the tide does not stop at the coast; where it forces its way up a river, that reach becomes literally of the tide.
senses.whyCN: 潮水并不止于海岸；它顶进河流的那一段，字面上就成了「潮汐的」地盘。

senses.title: Of a gravitational tide
senses.definition: of the bulge or force raised in one body by another body's gravity, with or without water
senses.definitionCN: 指一个天体被另一个天体的引力拉出的隆起或作用力，无论表面有没有水
senses.example: The moon lifts a tidal bulge in the solid rock.
senses.exampleCN: 月球在坚硬的岩层里也拉起一个潮汐隆起。
senses.why: physics kept the water image and moved it to rock: what the moon raises in the earth is of the same nature as the sea's tide.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留水的意象又把它挪到岩石上：月球在地球里拉出的隆起，与海潮在性质上相同。

senses.title: Of one breath's volume
senses.definition: of the volume of air moved in or out in a single ordinary breath
senses.definitionCN: 指一次平静呼吸进出肺部的空气体积
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's tidal volume every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每小时记录一次病人的潮气量。
senses.why: breathing repeats like the water's rise and fall, so respiratory physiology borrowed the adjective for the air moved in one cycle.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸像水的涨落一样往复，呼吸生理学于是借这个形容词，指一个周期里进出的空气量。

intro.en: Tidal is a native Germanic noun fitted with a borrowed suffix: Old English tīd 'time' became tide, and English added -al to make an adjective from it. The word is recorded in tide-related writing from the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tidal 是一个日耳曼本族名词加外来后缀的构造：古英语 tīd「时间」演变为 tide，英语再加 -al 构成形容词。这个词从 18 世纪的潮汐类写作中开始见于书证，年代均为约数。

items.en: Tīd meant 'time, hour, season, appointed time' and survives in eventide and Yuletide; the Germanic noun behind it is reconstructed as *tīdiz, the same word as German Zeit, so the sea sense grew out of the fixed hours at which high water was expected.
items.cn: tīd 意为「时间、时辰、季节、约定的时刻」，今仍存于若干表示时令的旧词中；其背后的日耳曼名词重构为 *tīdiz，与德语 Zeit 同词，海潮义正是从「高潮到来的固定时刻」长出来的。

items.en: By the fourteenth century tide named the rise and fall of the sea itself, and high tide and low tide had become fixed phrases.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，tide 已指海水本身的涨落，「高潮」与「低潮」成为固定说法。

items.en: The adjective suffix -al goes back to Latin -alis by way of Norman French; English attaches it freely to nouns (tidal, coastal, legal) to mean 'of or belonging to'.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -al 经诺曼法语上溯到拉丁 -alis；英语把它自由地加在名词后，表示「属于……的」。

items.en: Tidal appears in eighteenth-century writing on harbours and tide tables, where an adjective was needed for the phenomenon itself rather than for a particular tide.
items.cn: tidal 见于 18 世纪关于港口与潮汐表的写作，当时需要一个形容词来指这一现象本身，而不是某一次具体的潮。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective spread to tidal power, tidal force in astronomy and tidal volume in physiology, each time keeping the core relation 'of the tide'.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪，这个形容词扩展到潮汐发电、天文学中的引潮力、生理学中的潮气量，每次都保留「属于潮汐」这一核心关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest citation of tidal is generally placed in the eighteenth century but is not precisely dated; *tīdiz is a reconstruction, while the cognacy of tide and German Zeit is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：tidal 的最早书证一般定在 18 世纪，但没有确切年份；*tīdiz 是重构形式，而 tide 与德语 Zeit 同源这一点并无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like tidal or are built on the same stem, including two that end alike but come from different roots; group two holds words used about the same coastal setting.
note.cn: 第一组是与 tidal 形近或同出同一词干的词，其中两个结尾相同但词根不同；第二组是用于同一海岸情境的词。

entries.definition: the rise and fall of the sea itself; tidal only describes what belongs to it, so the noun cannot stand in for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 海水本身的涨落；tidal 只描写属于它的东西，因此这个名词不能替代形容词。

entries.definition: tidal plus -ly, describing how something is done or driven, as in a tidally flushed lagoon.
entries.definitionCN: tidal 加 -ly，描写某事以何种方式发生或被驱动，如「靠潮水冲刷的潟湖」。

entries.definition: from Latin titulus 'inscription, label'; the shared ending is accidental and there is no tide in it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 titulus「铭文、标签」；相同的词尾纯属巧合，与潮汐无关。

entries.definition: from bride plus -al, meaning 'of a wedding'; it rhymes with tidal but is built on a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 由「新娘」一词加 -al 构成，意为「婚礼的」；它与 tidal 押韵，却建立在另一个名词上。

entries.definition: between the high and low water marks; it names one zone, while tidal can qualify anything connected with the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 位于高低潮线之间；它只指一个地带，而 tidal 可修饰任何与潮汐有关的事物。

entries.definition: of the shore, whether or not tides reach it; it is a wider term than tidal.
entries.definitionCN: 海岸的，无论潮水是否到达；它比 tidal 范围更宽。

entries.definition: of an estuary, the place where a river meets the tide; it names the setting rather than the tide's influence.
entries.definitionCN: 河口湾的，即河流与潮水相遇之处；它指这类地点，而非潮汐的影响。

entries.definition: recurring at regular intervals; tidal behaviour is one kind of periodic behaviour, so the general word is wider.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔重复的；潮汐行为是周期性行为的一种，因此这个一般词的范围更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English tīd meant 'time', and the tide keeps its own clock: high water arrives at fixed hours.
normal.cn: 古英语 tīd 意为「时间」，潮水也自带时钟：高潮总在固定的时刻到来。

normal.en: The family runs tide, tidal, tidally, tideland, tideline, tidewater, tidegate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tide、tidal、tidally、tideland、tideline、tidewater、tidegate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the coastal sense: tidal flat, tidal pool, tidal current, tidal bore.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出海岸义：潮滩、潮池、潮流、涌潮。

normal.en: German Zeit 'time' is the cousin of tide; the two words split long before English existed.
normal.cn: 德语 Zeit「时间」是 tide 的表亲，两词在英语形成之前就已分开。

normal.en: A relational adjective rarely takes more or most: the comparative sounds awkward in ordinary use.
normal.cn: 关系形容词很少用比较级：在普通用法里，比较级听起来很别扭。

abstract.en: Picture the sea climbing a stone stair, one step every six hours.
abstract.cn: 想象海水在爬石阶，每六个小时上一级。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands are moved by the moon instead of by a spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针不靠发条，而由月亮推动。

abstract.en: Picture a river that briefly turns salty and flows backwards twice a day.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河一天两次短暂变咸，并倒着流。

examples.en: Tidal water reached the lower streets before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前，潮水已经漫到低处的街道。

examples.en: The tidal flat teems with worms and shells at low water.
examples.cn: 退潮时，潮滩上尽是沙蚕与贝壳。

examples.en: Engineers survey tidal currents before anchoring the turbine.
examples.cn: 工程师在固定涡轮之前先勘测潮流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬陡」——潮水抬得又陡又快，一转眼漫上滩面 → 潮汐的、受潮水支配的

root: 古英语 tīd「时间、时辰」（日耳曼语重构 *tīdiz，与德语 Zeit 同源）→ 中古英语 tide 兼指海水的定时涨落 → tide + 形容词后缀 -al → tidal；*tīdiz 属构拟形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one relation, 'of the tide': the phenomenon and its records, the places it governs, the power drawn from it, the strip it owns, the currents it turns, the clocks it winds, the rivers it pushes up, the rock it bulges, and finally the breath it resembles.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都守着同一个关系「属于潮汐」：现象及其记录、受它支配的地点、从它取用的动力、它拥有的地带、它反转的水流、它上弦的钟、它顶进的河流、它拉起的岩层，最后是它所比拟的一次呼吸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sea climbing and retreating along the same shore twice a day, on a schedule set by the moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：海水沿着同一道岸坡一天涨落两次，时刻由月亮定下。

branches.en: THE BASIC RELATION: first the phenomenon and its records, then the places and waters it governs.
branches.cn: 基本关系：先是现象及其记录，然后是受它支配的地点与水域。

branches.en: TIDE AS FORCE: the water that spins a turbine is the same water that reverses a channel.
branches.cn: 潮汐作为力：转动涡轮的水，与让水道掉头的水是同一股。

branches.en: THE STRIP THE TIDE OWNS: between the marks, the tide decides what may live and when.
branches.cn: 潮水拥有的地带：在两条水位线之间，潮汐决定谁能生存、何时生存。

branches.en: TIDE AS CLOCK AND AS INTRUSION: organisms keep its rhythm, and rivers feel its push upstream.
branches.cn: 潮汐作为时钟与侵入者：生物守着它的节律，河流感到它向上游的顶托。

branches.en: THE IMAGE EXTENDED: gravity raises rock, and breathing repeats like water.
branches.cn: 意象的延伸：引力拉起岩石，呼吸像水一样往复。

intro.en: Tidal is a native Germanic noun with a borrowed suffix: tide comes from Old English, while -al reached English through Latin and French and then became fully productive.
intro.cn: tidal 是日耳曼本族名词加外来后缀：tide 来自古英语，而 -al 经拉丁语与法语进入英语，随后成为能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin (-alis); tide itself has no Latin cognate, since it descends from Germanic *tīdiz. The Latin entries are therefore empty by design, and Latin-based look-alikes such as title belong to other roots.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁的（-alis）；tide 本身来自日耳曼 *tīdiz，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁条目按实情留空；像 title 这类拉丁系形近词属于别的词根。

items.example: High water came at the appointed tīd.
items.exampleCN: 高潮在约定的时辰到来。

items.example: The same suffix builds tidal from tide.
items.exampleCN: 同一个后缀把 tide 构成 tidal。

items.meaning: the rise and fall of the sea
items.example: The tide turned before noon.
items.exampleCN: 中午之前潮水转向了。

items.meaning: of or relating to the tide
items.example: Tidal water covered the road.
items.exampleCN: 潮水淹了这条路。

items.meaning: in a manner driven by the tide
items.example: The lagoon is flushed tidally.
items.exampleCN: 这片潟湖靠潮水冲刷。

items.example: Eelgrass grows on the tideland.
items.exampleCN: 大叶藻长在潮间地上。

items.meaning: the line of debris left by high water
items.meaningCN: 高潮退去后留下的杂物线
items.example: A tideline of plastic marked the beach.
items.exampleCN: 一道塑料垃圾的潮线划在海滩上。

items.meaning: water moved by the tide; low coastal land
items.meaningCN: 受潮水推动的水；沿海低地
items.example: Tidewater reaches the old mill pond.
items.exampleCN: 潮水能涨到那座旧磨坊的水塘。

items.meaning: a gate that keeps the tide out
items.example: The tidegate protects the low fields.
items.exampleCN: 挡潮闸保护低处的田地。

items.example: Intertidal rocks are bare at low water.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时潮间带的礁石裸露出来。

definition_zh: 热浪；持续多日的异常酷热天气；突然集中爆发的热潮
definition_en: a spell of unusually hot weather lasting several days, or a sudden widespread surge of something
core_image: 暑气在城市上空积成一层厚盖，柏油路面整夜不凉，墙外的空调外机不停滴水
scene: 入夏第三个星期，柏油路面整夜不凉，气象站连续多日测到异常高温。 The heat wave held the city for twelve days without a storm.
sceneCN: 这里指连续多日不散的异常高温（第 1 个义项：持续多日高温）；句意为这场热浪围住城市十二天，一场雷雨也没来。图中可辨识物件：柏油路、温度计、空调外机、稀疏树荫。

pos.zh: 热浪；持续高温期；集中的热潮

derivatives.zh: 由「热」与「浪」两个成分合写成一词构成，义为「热浪」
由「热」加已然词尾构成，义为「加热的；激烈的」
由「热」的动词加名词尾构成，义为「供暖；加热」
由同一名词转作动词构成，义为「加热」
由「热」与「一段时期」组合成的同义说法，义为「酷热期」

senses.title: A spell of lasting heat
senses.definition: a period of abnormally hot weather that lasts several days and nights
senses.definitionCN: 连续数日数夜异常炎热的天气时段
senses.example: The heat wave lasted ten days and broke the July record.
senses.exampleCN: 这场热浪持续十天，打破了七月的纪录。
senses.why: The two halves of the compound simply name heat and a rolling swell, so the phrase begins as weather seen as something rolling in.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词的两半只是「热」与「涌动的浪」，所以它最初把天气看成一波涌来的东西。

senses.title: A recorded heat event
senses.definition: a heat wave that has been measured, dated and entered in climate records
senses.definitionCN: 已被测量、标注日期并录入气候记录的热浪
senses.example: The nineteen thirty-six heat wave is still the benchmark for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 一九三六年的那场热浪至今仍是该地区的基准。
senses.why: Once weather stations keep daily logs, a spell of heat becomes an event with dates and numbers.
senses.whyCN: 气象站一旦逐日记录，一段高温就变成有日期、有数字的事件。

senses.title: An official heat alert
senses.definition: a public warning issued when a heat wave is expected to endanger health
senses.definitionCN: 预计热浪将危害健康时发布的公共警报
senses.example: The weather service issued a heat wave alert for the whole province.
senses.exampleCN: 气象部门向全省发布了热浪警报。
senses.why: Forecasting made the phrase a trigger for action, so it now names the warning as well as the weather.
senses.whyCN: 预报使这个说法成为行动的信号，于是它既指天气，也指那条警报。

senses.title: Heat trapped in a city
senses.definition: the intensified heat that a city experiences because concrete, asphalt and traffic hold the day's warmth
senses.definitionCN: 城市因混凝土、柏油与车流存住白天的热量而承受的更强炎热
senses.example: The city heat wave kept night-time temperatures above thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 城市热浪使夜间气温一直高于三十度。
senses.why: The same phrase shifts from the air above a region to the air inside a built-up area, where surfaces store heat.
senses.whyCN: 同一个说法从区域上空转到建成区内部，那里的地表把热量存了下来。

senses.title: A warm spell in the sea
senses.definition: a prolonged period when sea surface temperatures stay far above the long-term average
senses.definitionCN: 海表温度长时间远高于长期平均值的时段
senses.example: A marine heat wave bleached the reef in a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 一场海洋热浪在一个季节里就使珊瑚礁白化。
senses.why: Oceanographers borrowed the weather phrase because warm water spreads and lingers like a dome of hot air.
senses.whyCN: 海洋学家借用了这个天气说法，因为暖水扩散、滞留的样子像一顶热空气罩。

senses.title: A sudden surge of anything
senses.definition: a short period in which an activity, feeling or rumour spreads widely and fast
senses.definitionCN: 某种活动、情绪或传闻在短时间内广泛迅速扩散的时期
senses.example: A heat wave of rumours swept the office before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之前，一阵传闻的热潮扫过办公室。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century usage let wave mean any surging movement, and the compound followed it into figurative weather.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的用法让「浪」可以指任何涌动的势头，这个复合词便跟着进入比喻性的天气。

senses.title: A summer remembered by its deaths
senses.definition: a heat wave so severe that a city or country names it and remembers its death toll
senses.definitionCN: 严重到被城市或国家命名、并被记住死亡人数的热浪
senses.example: The named heat wave killed hundreds of elderly residents.
senses.exampleCN: 那场被命名的热浪夺走了数百名老年居民的生命。
senses.why: Extreme events enter public memory with a name, the way storms do, so a deadly summer becomes a proper event.
senses.whyCN: 极端事件会像风暴一样带着名字进入公共记忆，于是致命的盛夏成了一个专名事件。

senses.title: A public health crisis period
senses.definition: a stretch of heat during which hospitals, power grids and emergency services are strained
senses.definitionCN: 医院、电网与急救系统都承受压力的一段高温时期
senses.example: During the heat wave hospitals admitted twice the usual number of patients.
senses.exampleCN: 热浪期间，医院收治的病人是平常的两倍。
senses.why: The phrase ends up naming not the temperature but the burden it places on a whole society.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法最终指的不是温度本身，而是它压在整个社会身上的负担。

intro.en: Heat wave is a native English compound. Its first half comes from Old English hǣtu, heat, and its second half from Old English wǣg, a moving swell of water. The compound itself is a mid-nineteenth-century formation; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这是英语本族复合词。前一半来自古英语「hǣtu」「热」，后一半来自古英语「wǣg」「移动的水浪」。复合词本身是十九世纪中叶的构造，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Old English hǣtu named heat itself, a native Germanic word with no Latin ancestor.
items.cn: 古英语「hǣtu」指热本身，是日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Old English wǣg first meant a moving swell of water, the ridge that rolls and lifts.
items.cn: 古英语「wǣg」最初指移动的水浪，即起伏涌起的那道浪脊。

items.en: In the nineteenth century wave extended from water to any surging movement, including a spell of weather.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个「浪」词从水面扩展到任何涌动的势头，包括一段天气。

items.en: Heat wave appeared as a compound in the mid-nineteenth century; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 「热浪」这个复合词在十九世纪中叶出现，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Weather services later turned the phrase into an official category with thresholds, forecasts and warnings.
items.cn: 气象部门后来把这个说法变成带有阈值、预报与警报的官方类别。

items.en: Climate research extended it to ocean heat waves, and everyday speech lent it to any sudden surge.
items.cn: 气候研究把它扩展到海洋热浪，日常说法又把它借给任何突然的涌潮。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like heat wave; the second group names neighbouring ideas of hot spells and heat warnings.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「heat wave」相近；第二组是与「酷热期、高温警报」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The same weather event written as one word, a spelling that became common in the twentieth century.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个天气事件的合写形式，这种拼法在二十世纪变得常见。

entries.definition: High temperature itself, the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指高温本身，是复合词的前一半。

entries.definition: A raised ridge moving across water, and by extension any surging movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指在水面移动的浪脊，引申指任何涌动的势头。

entries.definition: Made warm, or made intense and angry, as in a heated argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指被加热的，也指激烈愤怒的，如激烈的争论。

entries.definition: A stretch of hot weather, usually shorter and less technical than a heat wave.
entries.definitionCN: 指一段炎热天气，通常比热浪短，也更口语。

entries.definition: A persistent high-pressure system that traps hot air beneath it and causes a heat wave.
entries.definitionCN: 指滞留的高压系统把热空气压在下方，从而造成热浪。

entries.definition: An informal word for an extremely hot day.
entries.definitionCN: 指极热一天的口语说法。

entries.definition: A public notice that dangerous heat is expected, close to the official sense of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指预报危险高温的公共通告，接近这个词的官方义。

entries.definition: The ocean version of the phenomenon, with water instead of air as the hot medium.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一现象的海洋版本，热的介质是水而不是空气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two native halves of the compound, its real records and its real weather phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个复合词两个本族成分、真实记录与真实气象搭配。

normal.en: Heat plus wave: hot air arriving like a swell that rolls over a city and will not retreat.
normal.cn: 热加浪：热空气像一道涌浪压过城市，迟迟不退。

normal.en: Both halves are Old English, so the phrase is native rather than borrowed from Latin.
normal.cn: 两个成分都来自古英语，所以这个说法是本族的，不是从拉丁语借来的。

normal.en: A heat wave warning is the fixed phrase you hear on the radio before a dangerous summer day.
normal.cn: 热浪警报是危险夏日来临前收音机里会出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Marine heat wave is the scientific use, measuring warm ocean water rather than hot air.
normal.cn: 海洋热浪是科学用法，量的是温暖海水而不是热空气。

normal.en: The compound is only a mid-nineteenth-century formation, younger than the two words inside it.
normal.cn: 这个复合词只是十九世纪中叶才形成的，比它里面的两个词年轻得多。

abstract.en: A heat wave is weather with a lid on it: the air cannot rise and cannot leave.
abstract.cn: 热浪是被盖住的天气：空气既升不上去，也走不掉。

abstract.en: A city in a heat wave becomes an oven that keeps its own warmth after sunset.
abstract.cn: 热浪中的城市成了一口日落后仍存着自己热量的烤箱。

abstract.en: Any rumour can arrive as a heat wave: brief, wide, and impossible to escape while it lasts.
abstract.cn: 任何传闻都可能像热浪一样到来：短暂、广泛，在它持续时无处可躲。

examples.en: The heat wave forced the city to open cooling centres.
examples.cn: 这场热浪迫使城市开放避暑中心。

examples.en: Scientists counted a marine heat wave off the coast last summer.
examples.cn: 科学家去年夏天记录了近岸的一场海洋热浪。

examples.en: A heat wave of protest followed the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布之后，一阵抗议的热潮随之而来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「希特 威夫」——热到空气都翻起了浪：热浪，也用来说一阵突然涌来的热潮。

root: 英语本族复合词：前一半来自古英语「hǣtu」「热」，后一半来自古英语「wǣg」「移动的水浪」；「wave」在十九世纪扩展为「一阵涌动」，复合词于十九世纪中叶出现，确切首见年代不确定。两个成分皆属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a plain weather spell to the official alert, the city and the ocean, a figurative surge, a named deadly summer, and a period of public health strain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的天气时段走向官方警报、城市与海洋、比喻性的涌潮、被命名的致命盛夏，以及公共卫生承压的时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broad dome of hot air sits over a city for days while the pavement never cools.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶宽大的热空气罩连日压在城上，路面始终不凉。

branches.en: THE SPELL: hot air arrives and stays, day and night, until records fall.
branches.cn: 高温时段：热空气来了就留下，日夜不退，直到纪录被打破。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE WARNING: the spell is measured, dated and then announced to the public.
branches.cn: 记录与警报：这段高温被测量、标注日期，随后向公众发布。

branches.en: THE BUILT AND THE WATERY: surfaces store heat in a city, and warm water spreads across a reef.
branches.cn: 建成区与水域：城市地表存住热量，暖水则铺过珊瑚礁。

branches.en: THE FIGURATIVE SURGE: rumour or feeling spreads like hot air, wide and fast.
branches.cn: 比喻涌潮：传闻或情绪像热空气一样广而快地散开。

branches.en: THE DEADLY SUMMER: a named event, its death toll, and the hospitals and grids under strain.
branches.cn: 致命盛夏：被命名的事件、它的死亡人数，以及承压的医院与电网。

intro.en: Heat wave is a Germanic compound, so its parts are native English words rather than Latin stems.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼语复合词，各部分是本族英语词，而不是拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Both components are inherited Germanic words, so there is no Latin counterpart to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都是日耳曼语继承下来的本族词，因此这里没有可列的拉丁同族。

items.example: The word named the feeling of fire and summer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指火与夏天带来的那种感觉。

items.example: It described water lifting and rolling forward.
items.exampleCN: 它描述水面抬升、向前翻卷的样子。

items.example: The first half of the compound is this everyday noun.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前一半就是这个日常名词。

items.meaning: a raised ridge on water; a surge
items.meaningCN: 水面上的浪脊；一阵涌动
items.example: The second half carries the idea of rolling movement.
items.exampleCN: 后一半带着翻滚移动的意思。

items.meaning: a lasting spell of hot weather
items.example: The compound is the ordinary name for the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是这一事件的日常名称。

items.meaning: the same event written as one word
items.meaningCN: 同一事件写成一词的形式
items.example: Newspapers often close the compound up.
items.exampleCN: 报纸常把这个复合词合写。

items.example: It marks the plural of the whole phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它标出整个词组里的复数。

items.structure: English adjective from Old English hāt
items.example: The adjective supplies the family word for hot days.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供了表示炎热日子的同族词。

items.example: It names the period that the heat fills.
items.exampleCN: 它指被高温填满的那段时期。

definition_zh: 成熟；成熟期；（金融票据、合同等的）到期；到期日
definition_en: the state of being fully developed; the point at which a financial instrument or contract falls due
core_image: 果园里，技术员切开一颗果子查看糖度，记录板上画着逐周上升的曲线
scene: 果园里，技术员每隔一周测一次果实的糖度，直到整片园子的果子都达到采收标准。 The orchard was picked only after the fruit reached full maturity.
sceneCN: 这里指果实发育完成（第 1 个义项：生理或发育意义上的成熟）；句意为直到果实完全成熟，果园才开始采摘。图中可辨识物件：果树、糖度计、记录板、采果篮。

senses.title: Biological maturity
senses.definition: the stage at which an organism can reproduce and its body has finished growing
senses.definitionCN: 生物能够繁殖、身体完成生长的阶段
senses.example: The seals reach sexual maturity at about four years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这些海豹大约四岁达到性成熟。
senses.why: Development has a natural end point, and the word names the moment when growth and reproduction are both available.
senses.whyCN: 发育有天然的终点，这个词命名的正是生长与繁殖都已具备的时刻。

senses.title: Emotional and judgemental maturity
senses.definition: the capacity to weigh consequences and act responsibly rather than impulsively
senses.definitionCN: 能权衡后果、负责任地行动而不凭冲动的能力
senses.example: The negotiations demanded patience and a certain maturity from both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判要求双方都有耐心与一定的成熟度。
senses.why: The same word for ripening is applied to character, because both describe something that has stopped being unripe.
senses.whyCN: 表示「成熟」的同一个词被用到性格上，因为两者都描述某物不再青涩。

senses.title: Ripeness of fruit or crops
senses.definition: the point at which a crop is ready to harvest, judged by colour, sugar or texture
senses.definitionCN: 作物达到可采收的程度，常以颜色、糖度或质地判断
senses.example: Growers test sugar levels to decide when the grapes reach maturity.
senses.exampleCN: 种植者测试糖度来决定葡萄何时成熟。
senses.why: Harvest timing needs a threshold, and the word names the stage where the fruit is fully formed and ready.
senses.whyCN: 采收时机需要一个阈值，这个词命名的就是果实完全成形且可用的阶段。

senses.title: A financial instrument falling due
senses.definition: the date on which a bond, note or loan must be repaid, or the state of having reached that date
senses.definitionCN: 债券、票据或贷款必须偿还的日期，或已到达该日期的状态
senses.example: The bond has a maturity of ten years from issue.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券自发行起十年到期。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the language of ripening: a debt is mature when it has reached the point of payment.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了「成熟」的说法：债务到了该偿付的时刻，就说它到期。

senses.title: The maturity date
senses.definition: the specific calendar day on which the principal of an instrument must be repaid
senses.definitionCN: 票据本金必须偿还的具体日期
senses.example: Investors marked the maturity date in their calendars.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者把到期日标在日历上。
senses.why: Once a date had to be written down, the abstract state became a fixed appointment.
senses.whyCN: 一旦必须写下一个日期，抽象状态就变成了固定的约定。

senses.title: Yield to maturity
senses.definition: the total return an investor receives if a bond is held until it matures
senses.definitionCN: 债券持有至到期时投资者获得的总回报率
senses.example: The bond's yield to maturity was higher than its coupon rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券的到期收益率高于票面利率。
senses.why: The measure exists because the value of a bond depends on everything received up to and including the final day.
senses.whyCN: 这一指标之所以存在，是因为债券价值取决于到期日及之前收到的全部现金流。

senses.title: Expiry of a contract or policy
senses.definition: the end of the term for which an insurance policy or agreement runs
senses.definitionCN: 保险单或协议的有效期限结束
senses.example: The policy reached maturity and paid out a lump sum.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单到期并支付了一笔一次性款项。
senses.why: Contracts also have a ripening point, after which the obligations are settled or renewed.
senses.whyCN: 合同同样有一个「熟透」的时点，此后义务结清或续约。

senses.title: Cellular and tissue maturation
senses.definition: the process by which unspecialised cells acquire their adult structure and function
senses.definitionCN: 未特化细胞获得成年结构与功能的过程
senses.example: The culture took three weeks to reach full maturity.
senses.exampleCN: 这组培养物用了三周才完全成熟。
senses.why: In cell biology maturity means differentiation is complete, so the word shifts from the whole body to a single lineage.
senses.whyCN: 在细胞生物学中，成熟意味着分化完成，这个词于是从整个身体转到单一细胞谱系。

senses.title: Soil and ecological maturity
senses.definition: the developed state of a soil profile or an ecosystem that has reached a stable community
senses.definitionCN: 土壤剖面发育完善，或生态系统达到稳定群落的状态
senses.example: The forest had reached maturity after a century without disturbance.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林在百年无干扰之后达到成熟。
senses.why: Ecology applies the same arc from young to developed, treating a climax community as the mature end point.
senses.whyCN: 生态学套用同样的由幼到熟的弧线，把顶极群落视为成熟的终点。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin maturus, ripe or timely, and its noun maturitas. The Latin origin is clear; the exact date of the English noun's first use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「成熟的、适时的」形容词及其名词形式。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Maturus described fruit that had ripened and, by extension, anything that had come at the right time.
items.cn: 这个词先形容果实已经成熟，引申指任何「来得正是时候」的事物。

items.en: The same old root is thought to lie behind matutinus, of the morning, so ripeness and early hour share an idea of the right moment.
items.cn: 一般认为同一个古老词根也藏在表示「早晨的」形容词背后，因此「成熟」与「清晨」共享「恰当时刻」这一观念。

items.en: The abstract noun named the state of being ripe or timely, which English took over almost unchanged.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词指成熟或适时的状态，英语几乎原样借入。

items.en: English used the word first for physical ripeness and later for the due date of a debt.
items.cn: 英语先用它指生理成熟，后来才用于债务的到期。

items.en: As bills and bonds became standard instruments, maturity moved from the ripening of fruit to the day a payment falls due.
items.cn: 当票据与债券成为标准工具，「成熟」便从果实成熟转到付款到期的日子。

items.en: The financial use is dated to the modern banking era, but the precise first attestation of the noun is uncertain.
items.cn: 金融用法可系于现代银行时代，但该名词的确切首见时间不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stem or the finance compounds; the second group names related states of completion.
note.cn: 第一组共享词干或金融搭配；第二组是表示「完成」的相关状态。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb meaning fully developed or to become so.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「成熟的」或「使成熟」的形容词与动词。

entries.definition: The process of becoming mature, especially in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 变为成熟的过程，尤用于生物学。

entries.definition: The state of not yet being mature.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未成熟的状态。

entries.definition: The day on which a financial instrument falls due.
entries.definitionCN: 金融工具到期的那一天。

entries.definition: The return earned by holding a bond to its due date.
entries.definitionCN: 持有债券至到期所获得的回报率。

entries.definition: The state of fruit being ready to eat or harvest.
entries.definitionCN: 果实可以食用或采收的状态。

entries.definition: The stage of being a fully grown person.
entries.definitionCN: 成为完全成年人的阶段。

entries.definition: The completion of growth or formation.
entries.definitionCN: 生长或形成的完成。

entries.definition: The date by which a payment or obligation must be met.
entries.definitionCN: 付款或义务必须履行的日期。

entries.definition: The end of the period for which something is valid.
entries.definitionCN: 某物有效的期限结束。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the arc from fruit to character to finance; abstract ones treat maturity as a threshold rather than a feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着从果实到性格再到金融的弧线展开；抽象联想把成熟看作阈值而非感受。

normal.en: Maturity begins as a fruit word: colour, sugar, texture, ready to pick.
normal.cn: 成熟最初是果实词：颜色、糖度、质地，到了可采摘的程度。

normal.en: The same word then describes a person who can wait and weigh consequences.
normal.cn: 同一个词随后形容能等待、能权衡后果的人。

normal.en: In finance the fruit becomes a bond, and ripe means payable.
normal.cn: 在金融里，果实变成债券，「熟」就是「该付了」。

normal.en: A maturity date is the day the ripening is written into a calendar.
normal.cn: 到期日就是把「成熟」写进日历的那一天。

normal.en: Cells and soils mature too, because every system has a developed end state.
normal.cn: 细胞与土壤也会成熟，因为每个系统都有发育完成的状态。

abstract.en: Maturity is not an age, it is the point where something stops needing to be finished.
abstract.cn: 成熟不是年龄，而是某物不再需要被完成的那一刻。

abstract.en: Every field keeps the same fruit metaphor: unripe, ripening, due.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都保留同一个果实隐喻：未熟、将熟、到期。

abstract.en: A threshold can be crossed quietly, which is why maturity is often noticed only afterwards.
abstract.cn: 阈值可以悄无声息地被跨过，所以成熟往往事后才被察觉。

examples.en: The grapes reach maturity in late September.
examples.cn: 葡萄在九月下旬成熟。

examples.en: The bond has a maturity of five years.
examples.cn: 这只债券期限五年。

examples.en: Emotional maturity matters more than age in this role.
examples.cn: 在这个岗位上，情感成熟比年龄更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「马球里提」——果子熟了才敢办「马球赛」，晚了就到期了：成熟、到期

root: 来自拉丁语 maturus「成熟的、适时的」及其名词 maturitas，经法语进入英语。一般认为表示「早晨的」拉丁形容词也出自同一古老词根，因此「成熟」与「恰当时刻」共享一个观念。金融「到期」义属现代银行时代的引申，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses grow from one image of ripening: the body, the character, the crop, the debt, the date, the return, the contract, the cell and the soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从一个「成熟」意象长出来：身体、性格、作物、债务、日期、回报、合同、细胞与土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar meter, a rising curve, a crate waiting at the end of the row.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖度计、上升的曲线、地头等着的果筐。

branches.en: THE RIPENING CORE: body and crop both arrive at the point of being fully formed.
branches.cn: 成熟内核：身体与作物都到达完全成形的时点。

branches.en: THE CHARACTER: the same threshold applied to judgement and patience.
branches.cn: 性格层面：同一阈值被用到判断力与耐心上。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL ARC: due, the date of due, and the return earned by waiting for it.
branches.cn: 金融弧线：到期、到期日，以及等到期所获的回报。

branches.en: THE OTHER COMPLETIONS: a contract's term ends, a cell's differentiation finishes.
branches.cn: 其他完成形态：合同期限结束，细胞分化完成。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL END: a soil profile or a community reaches its developed state.
branches.cn: 生态终点：土壤剖面或群落达到发育完成的状态。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective plus an abstract noun ending, with English relatives built by negation and by prefixes of time.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁形容词加抽象名词词尾，英语亲属词由否定与时间前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the adjective of ripeness, its abstract noun and the verb of ripening; English adds the ending -ity and the negative and anticipatory prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示成熟的形容词、抽象名词与使成熟的动词；英语加上表示性质的词尾，以及否定与提前的前缀。

items.example: It described fruit at the right moment and then any timely thing.
items.exampleCN: 它先形容恰当时刻的果实，后指任何适时之物。

items.example: The abstract noun passed into English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词几乎原样进入英语。

items.example: The verb supplies the English process noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语的过程名词与动词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成状态名称。

items.example: The shorter form drops the abstract ending.
items.exampleCN: 较短的形容词形式去掉了抽象词尾。

items.example: The ending marks an ongoing process rather than a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记进行中的过程而非状态。

items.example: It forms the adjective and noun for what has not ripened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「尚未成熟」的形容词与名词。

items.example: It marks a birth or event that comes before the due time.
items.exampleCN: 它标记早于应有时刻的出生或事件。

intro.en: Eloquence is Latin eloquentia, from eloqui, which joins ex- meaning out to loqui meaning to speak; it is the power of speaking out well.

items.en: Adding ex- gives eloqui, to speak out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 eloqui，意为说出来。

items.en: The noun eloquentia names the power of speaking out well.

items.en: Old French eloquence carried the sense of fluent persuasive speech.

note.en: Eloquence, elocution and loquacious all carry loqui, the Latin root for speak; eloquence persuades, elocution trains the voice, loquacious simply talks a lot.

dict_mnemonic.text: eloquence ＝ e-（向外）＋ loqu（说话，拉丁 loqui）＋ -ence（名词后缀，表性质）＝「把话说出来的能力」。形容词 eloquent（-ent），副词 eloquently。loqui 这一家按前缀分：e-（外）→ eloquent 雄辩的、elocution 演说术；loquacious 话多的（-acious 爱…的）；soliloquy 独白（solus 独自 ＋ loqui）；colloquial 口语的（col- 一起 ＋ loqui＝一起说话）；ventriloquist 腹语者（venter 肚子 ＋ loqui＝用肚子说话）；circumlocution 迂回说法（circum 绕圈）。注意 eloquence 不只是「说得流利」，fluency 才是流利；eloquence 强调打动与说服。the eloquence of silence 是常见修辞，指沉默比话更有力量。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ loqui（说话）→ eloqui → eloquentia（善言的能力）→ eloquence（口才）

definition_zh: 基因流；基因流动（通过个体迁移、花粉或种子扩散在群体之间传递等位基因）
definition_en: the transfer of alleles from one population to another through migration, dispersal of seeds or pollen, or human movement
core_image: 山脊隘口的风把一片兰花的花粉吹到另一片兰花上，两种花色在两侧渐渐混匀
scene: 山脊两侧各有一片兰花，花色深浅原本不同，风把花粉送过隘口之后，两边花色的比例渐渐接近。 Pollen carried across the ridge produced gene flow between the two orchid populations.
sceneCN: 这里指群体之间的等位基因传递（第 1 个义项：通过迁移或繁殖体扩散把等位基因带入另一群体）；句意为被风送过山脊的花粉在两个兰花群体之间形成了基因流。图中可辨识物件：山脊、隘口、两片花丛、飘散的花粉。

pos.zh: 名词短语：不可数，指群体间的等位基因传递过程

collocations.zh: 来自野生近缘种的基因流

forms.label: 介词搭配
forms.form: gene flow between A and B

derivatives.zh: 短语的第一个成分，义为「基因」，一九零九年由约翰森定名
短语的中心词，义为「流动」，本指液体的连续移动
同一领域的概念，义为「基因库」，指一个群体携带的全部等位基因
同一领域的量，义为「基因频率」，即某等位基因在群体中的比例
由本短语加「速率」构成，义为「基因流速率」，常以每代迁入个体比例表示

senses.title: The process itself
senses.definition: the movement of alleles between populations when individuals or gametes cross a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 个体或配子跨越边界时等位基因在群体之间的移动
senses.example: Gene flow between the two valleys kept their colour patterns similar.
senses.exampleCN: 两个山谷之间的基因流使它们的花色格局保持相似。
senses.why: A boundary that individuals can cross is also a boundary that genes can cross, so the movement of bodies carries the movement of alleles.
senses.whyCN: 个体能越过的边界，基因也能越过；因此身体的移动同时携带了等位基因的移动。

senses.title: Contrast with genetic drift
senses.definition: a gain of variation from outside, whereas drift is a random loss or fixation inside a closed group
senses.definitionCN: 从外部获得变异，而漂变是在封闭群体内部随机丢失或固定
senses.example: Drift eroded the island's variation while gene flow from the mainland restored it.
senses.exampleCN: 漂变侵蚀了岛上的变异，而来自大陆的基因流又把它补回。
senses.why: Drift only reshuffles what is already present; gene flow is the one force that adds new alleles to a population.
senses.whyCN: 漂变只重排已有的东西；基因流则是唯一能给群体添入新等位基因的力量。

senses.title: Distinction from migration
senses.definition: the genetic consequence of movement, not the movement itself; an individual can migrate without breeding successfully
senses.definitionCN: 移动带来的遗传后果，而非移动本身；个体可以迁移却没有成功繁殖
senses.example: The birds migrated, but gene flow occurred only where they nested and raised chicks.
senses.exampleCN: 候鸟确实迁徙了，但只有它们筑巢育雏的地方才发生基因流。
senses.why: Migration is an ecological event; gene flow is its genetic ledger, and a ledger stays empty when no offspring are produced.
senses.whyCN: 迁移是生态事件，基因流是它的遗传账本；没有产生后代，账本上就是空的。

senses.title: Reducing divergence between populations
senses.definition: the homogenising effect that keeps neighbouring populations genetically similar
senses.definitionCN: 使相邻群体在遗传上保持相似的同质化作用
senses.example: Strong gene flow prevented the two colonies from splitting into distinct subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 强大的基因流阻止了两个群体分化为不同的亚种。
senses.why: Differences accumulate only when gene flow is weak; constant exchange keeps pulling the two gene pools back together.
senses.whyCN: 只有在基因流微弱时差异才会累积；持续的交换不断把两个基因库拉回同一状态。

senses.title: Barriers and connectivity
senses.definition: geographic features, distance or human construction that reduce the probability of successful exchange
senses.definitionCN: 地形、距离或人造设施降低成功交换概率的情形
senses.example: A new motorway became a barrier to gene flow for the forest frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 新建的高速公路成了林蛙基因流的屏障。
senses.why: Gene flow needs a path; when a barrier makes crossing rare, drift and local selection begin to separate the groups.
senses.whyCN: 基因流需要通路；当屏障使跨越变得罕见，漂变与局部选择就开始把两群分开。

senses.title: Plant-mediated flow
senses.definition: pollen and seed dispersal, which move genes without moving whole plants
senses.definitionCN: 花粉与种子的扩散，在不移动整株植物的情况下搬运基因
senses.example: Wind-borne pollen carried gene flow across the whole meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 风媒花粉把基因流带遍了整片草甸。
senses.why: A plant cannot walk, but its pollen and seeds can travel, so dispersal replaces migration as the vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 植物不会走路，但花粉与种子能旅行，于是扩散取代迁移成为载体。

senses.title: Animal-mediated flow
senses.definition: gene movement carried by migrating herds, birds, fish or insects
senses.definitionCN: 由迁徙的兽群、鸟、鱼或昆虫携带的基因移动
senses.example: Migrating salmon brought gene flow from the sea back to their home streams.
senses.exampleCN: 洄游的鲑鱼把基因流从海洋带回故乡的溪流。
senses.why: Animals that return to breed link distant sites in a single lifetime, making them extremely effective vectors.
senses.whyCN: 返回繁殖地的动物在一个生命周期内就把相距遥远的地点连起来，因此是极高效的载体。

senses.title: Human-mediated flow
senses.titleCN: 人类活动介导的基因流
senses.definition: translocation, stocking, shipping and trade that move organisms far beyond their natural range
senses.definitionCN: 引种、放养、船运与贸易把生物带到远超自然分布范围的地方
senses.example: Ballast water created gene flow between ports that had never exchanged shellfish.
senses.exampleCN: 压舱水在从未交换过贝类的港口之间造成了基因流。
senses.why: Modern transport compresses distance to nearly zero, so gene flow can occur between places with no natural corridor.
senses.whyCN: 现代运输把距离压缩到近乎为零，于是没有天然走廊的地点之间也能发生基因流。

senses.title: Conservation and corridor design
senses.definition: the management use of gene flow to counter inbreeding while avoiding the introduction of maladapted genes
senses.definitionCN: 用基因流缓解近交、同时避免引入不适应当地基因的管理应用
senses.example: Managers allowed limited gene flow to rescue the isolated herd without swamping local adaptation.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者允许有限的基因流来挽救隔离兽群，又不至于淹没本地适应。
senses.why: Too little flow means inbreeding; too much can erase local adaptation, so the useful concept is a controlled rate rather than a maximum.
senses.whyCN: 流得太少会近交，流得太多会抹掉本地适应，因此有用的概念是受控的速率而非越大越好。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a word coined in 1909 for the unit of inheritance with an Old English verb of flowing. Its modern genetic sense belongs to the twentieth century; the exact first printed use of the pair is not fixed.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一九零九年为遗传单位造出的词与一个古英语「流动」动词配在一起。其现代遗传学含义属于二十世纪；两词首次印在一起的准确时间并不确定。

items.en: Genos meant race, stock or kind; Johannsen took it through German to name the gene in 1909.
items.cn: 这个词意为族、种、类；约翰森经德语把它引入，于一九零九年为「基因」命名。

items.en: The new noun named the unit of heredity before anyone knew what it was made of.
items.cn: 这个新名词在人们知道遗传单位由什么构成之前就已为它命名。

items.en: Flowan meant to flow or to run as water does; its noun flow named the continuous movement itself.
items.cn: 这个古英语动词意为像水一样流动；其名词形式指这种连续运动本身。

items.en: Once heredity was counted in populations, the movement of genes between groups needed a name of its own.
items.cn: 当遗传开始在群体中计数，群体之间基因的移动就需要一个自己的名字。

items.en: The fixed phrase spread in the middle of the twentieth century with the rise of population genetics; its first attestation is uncertain in date but not in origin.
items.cn: 这个固定短语随群体遗传学的兴起在二十世纪中叶流行；其首见年代不确定，来源却清楚。

note.en: The first group shares the word gene or the flow frame; the second group names other ways alleles travel or mix.
note.cn: 第一组共享「基因」一词或「流动」框架；第二组是等位基因传播与混合的其他说法。

entries.definition: All the alleles carried by one population at a given time.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻一个群体所携带的全部等位基因。

entries.definition: The proportion of a particular allele within a population.
entries.definitionCN: 某个特定等位基因在群体中所占的比例。

entries.definition: A genetic construct that spreads a trait faster than ordinary inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 一种让某性状传播得比普通遗传更快的遗传构造。

entries.definition: An informal term for the rate at which genes enter or leave a group.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式说法，指基因进出群体的速率。

entries.definition: A looser wording sometimes used for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 有时用于同一含义的较宽松说法。

entries.definition: The ecological movement of individuals, which may or may not carry genes into the breeding pool.
entries.definitionCN: 个体的生态性移动，未必能把基因带入繁殖群体。

entries.definition: The spreading of seeds, spores or young away from the parent.
entries.definitionCN: 种子、孢子或幼体离开亲体向外扩散。

entries.definition: The permanent incorporation of genes from one species into another through hybridisation.
entries.definitionCN: 通过杂交把一个物种的基因永久并入另一个物种。

entries.definition: The mixing of two previously separated gene pools.
entries.definitionCN: 两个先前隔离的基因库发生混合。

entries.definition: Crossing between distinct groups, often the route by which gene flow becomes introgression.
entries.definitionCN: 不同群体间的杂交，常是基因流变成渐渗的途径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the vehicles of flow; abstract ones treat gene flow as a door in a wall.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着基因流的各种载体展开；抽象联想把它看作墙上的一扇门。

normal.en: Genes travel in bodies, in pollen and in seeds; the traveller is the vehicle.
normal.cn: 基因随身体、花粉与种子旅行；旅行者就是载体。

normal.en: Migration is the walk; gene flow is the birth that follows it.
normal.cn: 迁移是走路，基因流是走路之后发生的繁殖。

normal.en: Drift closes the room, gene flow opens a window.
normal.cn: 漂变关上房间，基因流打开一扇窗。

normal.en: Barriers make flow rare, and rarity lets drift and selection pull the two sides apart.
normal.cn: 屏障让流动变少，稀少又让漂变与选择把两侧拉开。

normal.en: In conservation the useful setting is a controlled trickle, not a flood.
normal.cn: 在保护实践中，有用的设定是受控的细流，而不是洪水。

abstract.en: Gene flow is the only force that adds new letters to a population's alphabet.
abstract.cn: 基因流是唯一能给群体的字母表添入新字母的力量。

abstract.en: A corridor is a sentence spoken between two populations that could not otherwise talk.
abstract.cn: 走廊是两个本无法交谈的群体之间说出的一句话。

abstract.en: Distance is a resistor, and each migrant is a small current.
abstract.cn: 距离是电阻，每个迁入者都是一小股电流。

examples.en: Gene flow from the mainland restored variation the island had lost.
examples.cn: 来自大陆的基因流恢复了岛屿已经丢失的变异。

examples.en: A motorway reduced gene flow between the two frog populations.
examples.cn: 一条高速公路降低了两群林蛙之间的基因流。

examples.en: Pollen dispersal is the main route of gene flow in wind-pollinated grasses.
examples.cn: 花粉扩散是风媒禾草中基因流的主要途径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「基因 弗楼」——基因像水一样「流」过山谷，把两边的库连起来：基因流

root: 第一个成分由希腊语 genos「族、种」经德语于一九零九年定为「基因」；第二个成分来自古英语 flowan「流动」。整个短语在二十世纪中叶随群体遗传学兴起而通行，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the bare process to its contrast with drift, its difference from migration, its effects, its vehicles and its management.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从过程本身出发，依次到与漂变的对比、与迁移的区别、效应、各种载体，最后到管理应用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wind over a ridge pass, pollen crossing from one orchid patch to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：风越过山口，花粉从一片兰花飘到另一片。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: bodies or gametes cross a boundary, and alleles cross with them.
branches.cn: 过程本身：个体或配子越过边界，等位基因随之越界。

branches.en: THE TWO DISTINCTIONS: drift only reshuffles inside, and migration matters only when offspring are produced.
branches.cn: 两组区分：漂变只在内部重排，迁移只有产生后代才有效。

branches.en: THE EFFECT AND ITS BRAKE: exchange homogenises neighbours until a barrier makes crossing rare.
branches.cn: 效应与刹车：交换使邻群同质化，直到屏障让跨越变少。

branches.en: THE VEHICLES: pollen, animals and human transport each carry genes by a different route.
branches.cn: 三类载体：花粉、动物与人类运输各以不同路径搬运基因。

branches.en: THE MANAGEMENT: conservation wants a controlled trickle that fights inbreeding without erasing local adaptation.
branches.cn: 管理应用：保护实践要的是受控细流，既抗近交又不抹掉本地适应。

intro.en: The phrase is two free words; its only bound pieces are the old adjective ending on the first word and the noun endings on both.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个自由词构成；黏着成分只有第一个词上的古老形容词词尾与两个词的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek gives the root for kind or stock; Old English gives the verb of flowing. No Latin noun underlies either half, so the Latin entry list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供「族、种」的词根；古英语提供「流动」动词。两半背后都没有拉丁名词，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

items.example: The root names a line of descent rather than a single trait.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指一条血统，而非单个性状。

items.example: Johannsen created the short form for the unit.
items.exampleCN: 约翰森为这个单位造出这个短词。

items.example: The adjective links the unit to the whole science.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把单位与整门科学连起来。

items.example: It attaches the Greek root to English syntax.
items.exampleCN: 它把希腊词根接入英语句法。

items.example: The verb described water moving without a fixed shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述水在没有固定形状的情况下移动。

items.example: The noun names movement as a process rather than an event.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把移动看作过程而非事件。

items.example: The prefix marks direction toward the centre.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标记朝向中心的运动。

items.example: The prefix marks direction away from the centre.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标记离开中心的运动。

derivatives.zh: 短语的第一个成分，义为「基因」，一九零九年由约翰森定名
短语的中心词，义为「流动」，本指液体的连续移动
同一领域的概念，义为「基因库」，指一个群体携带的全部等位基因
同一领域的量，义为「基因频率」，即某等位基因在群体中的比例
由本短语加「速率」构成，义为「基因流速率」，常以每代迁入个体比例表示

definition_zh: 珊瑚；珊瑚虫群体；珊瑚色；珊瑚制品
definition_en: a stony material built by tiny sea polyps, the animal colony itself, or the pink-orange colour of the precious kind
core_image: 海底一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，枝端还伸着细小的白色触手
scene: 浅海潜水时，向导指着一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，说明那些细小的触手是仍在取食的珊瑚虫。 The guide pointed to a branching pink-orange coral whose tiny polyps were still feeding.
sceneCN: 这里 coral 指「由珊瑚虫群体建造的活体珊瑚」（第 1 个义项：活着的珊瑚虫群体）；句意为向导指向一丛仍在取食的粉橙色枝状珊瑚。

pos.zh: 珊瑚；珊瑚虫群体
珊瑚（材料、制品）
珊瑚色的；珊瑚制的

derivatives.zh: 多种珊瑚（复数）
珊瑚的；珊瑚色的；珊瑚藻
珊瑚状的
