senses.title: The living colony of polyps
senses.definition: a colony of small sea animals that build a shared skeleton around themselves
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细小海生动物构成的群体，它们在自己周围建造共同的骨骼
senses.example: The guide pointed to a branching coral whose polyps were still feeding.
senses.exampleCN: 向导指着一丛仍在取食的枝状珊瑚。
senses.why: Naturalists first took coral for a plant; once it was shown to be an animal, the same word came to name the living colony.
senses.whyCN: 博物学家最初把珊瑚当作植物；一旦证明它是动物，同一个词就开始指活的群体。

senses.title: The hard stony skeleton
senses.definition: the limy skeleton left by a coral colony, often branching or dome-shaped
senses.definitionCN: 珊瑚群体留下的钙质骨骼，常呈枝状或穹顶状
senses.example: The beach was made of broken coral and shell.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩由碎珊瑚和贝壳构成。
senses.why: The skeleton outlasts the animal, so the word transferred from the builder to the built thing.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼比动物活得久，于是这个词从建造者转到了被建造物上。

senses.title: The framework of a reef
senses.definition: coral as the main builder that raises a reef structure in shallow tropical seas
senses.definitionCN: 在浅热带海域抬升出礁体结构的主要造礁珊瑚
senses.example: Coral slowly raised a barrier along the edge of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚沿海岛边缘慢慢筑起一道堡礁。
senses.why: In geology coral names the construction material of the reef, not the animal that made it.
senses.whyCN: 在地质语境里，coral 指礁体的建筑材料，而不是造它的动物。

senses.title: Polished coral as a material
senses.definition: the hard red or pink coral cut and polished for use in objects
senses.definitionCN: 被切割打磨、用于制作器物的红色或粉色硬珊瑚
senses.example: The workshop set a piece of coral into a silver ring.
senses.exampleCN: 工坊把一块珊瑚嵌进银戒指。
senses.why: Once cut and polished, the skeleton becomes a gem-like material, and the word follows the trade.
senses.whyCN: 一旦切割打磨，骨骼就成了类宝石的材料，词义也随行业走。

senses.title: The orange-pink colour
senses.definition: a soft orange-pink colour like precious red coral
senses.definitionCN: 像贵重红珊瑚那样的柔和橙粉色
senses.example: The walls were painted a warm coral.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面被刷成温暖的珊瑚色。
senses.why: The colour name is a straightforward transfer: the hue is named after the object that supplied the dye-like shade.
senses.whyCN: 颜色名是直接的转喻：这种色调以提供它的物件命名。

senses.title: Coral as ornament
senses.definition: beads, carvings or jewellery made from coral
senses.definitionCN: 用珊瑚制成的珠子、雕件或首饰
senses.example: A string of coral hung at her throat.
senses.exampleCN: 她颈间挂着一串珊瑚。
senses.why: The material is metonymy for the finished object, a common path from stuff to ornament.
senses.whyCN: 材料转指成品，这是从「材质」到「饰物」的常见路径。

senses.title: Fossil coral in rock
senses.definition: the remains of ancient coral preserved in limestone or shale
senses.definitionCN: 保存在石灰岩或页岩中的古代珊瑚遗骸
senses.example: Fossil coral in the cliff shows that this desert was once a sea.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁里的珊瑚化石说明这片沙漠曾是海洋。
senses.why: Palaeontology keeps the name because the fossil keeps the shape, even though the animal is long gone.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学沿用这个名字，因为化石保留了形态，尽管动物早已消失。

senses.title: A protective talisman
senses.definition: red coral worn or hung as a charm against misfortune, especially for children
senses.definitionCN: 被佩戴或悬挂以避邪的红珊瑚，尤用于儿童
senses.example: The grandmother tied a small coral to the child's wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母把一小块珊瑚系在孩子手腕上。
senses.why: Traditional belief gave the red material a protective power, so coral also names a charm rather than a substance.
senses.whyCN: 传统信仰赋予红色材料护佑之力，因此 coral 也指护身符，而不只是物质。

intro.en: Coral reached English through Old French from Latin, which had borrowed the word from Greek; the Greek source is not fully settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coral 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，拉丁语又是从希腊语借来的；希腊语的来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Korallion was the name of the red coral of the Mediterranean. Its deeper origin is not established; a Semitic loan is a common hypothesis, not a proven fact.
items.cn: korallion 是地中海红珊瑚的名称。其更深来源没有定论；源自闪米特语是一种常见假说，并非已证事实。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as corallium and used it for the red skeletal material, which Romans carved into beads and charms.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 corallium，指红色的骨骼材料，罗马人把它雕成珠子和护符。

items.en: Old French coral carried the word into English in the twelfth century, at first for the precious red material rather than for a living animal.
items.cn: 古法语 coral 在 12 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指贵重的红色材料，而非活体动物。

items.en: For centuries coral was classed as a sea plant; eighteenth-century naturalists showed that the polyps are animals, and the zoological sense followed.
items.cn: 数百年来珊瑚被归为海生植物；18 世纪的博物学家证明珊瑚虫是动物，动物学义随之出现。

items.en: The colour name coral, for the soft orange-pink of the precious material, became common in English dress and decoration writing.
items.cn: 指贵重材料那种柔和橙粉色的颜色名 coral，在英语服饰与装饰文字中逐渐通行。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Greek korallion has no agreed etymology, and the Semitic Origin hypothesis is one proposal among several, so no single source is asserted here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：希腊 korallion 没有公认的词源，闪米特语来源只是若干假说之一，此处不武断选定一种。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same coral stock that are easily interchanged; group two holds reef and shell words with neighbouring meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 coral 词族、容易互换的词；第二组是意义相邻的礁与壳类词。

entries.definition: The plural counts colonies or kinds; coral as a mass material stays singular.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式计数群体或种类；作物质材料时仍用单数 coral。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of or like coral; as a noun it also names red coralline algae, a different organism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为珊瑚的或似珊瑚的；作名词时还指珊瑚藻，那是另一种生物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', so it describes a branching shape without claiming the material is coral.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，描述枝状形态，并不表示材料真是珊瑚。

entries.definition: A reef is the whole wave-resistant structure; coral is one builder within it, alongside algae and other organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 礁指整座抗浪结构；珊瑚只是其中的建造者之一，还有藻类及其他生物参与。

entries.definition: One coral animal is a polyp; coral names the colony and its skeleton, not the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 单个珊瑚动物叫 polyp；coral 指群体及其骨骼，而非单个个体。

entries.definition: A ridge of rock, sand or coral near the surface; it may be built by coral but need not be.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近水面的一道岩石、沙或珊瑚脊；它可以由珊瑚建造，但并非必然。

entries.definition: The hard outer case of a mollusc or other animal; coral is an internal skeleton built by a colony, not a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 软体动物等的外壳；珊瑚是群体建造的骨骼，不是外壳。

entries.definition: A rock made largely of calcium carbonate, often from coral and shell debris; it is the stone, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 主要由碳酸钙构成的岩石，常来自珊瑚与贝壳碎屑；它指岩石，不指动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Coral names both the animal colony and the stone it leaves behind, so context decides which is meant.
normal.cn: coral 既指活体群体，也指它留下的石头，靠上下文判断指哪一个。

normal.en: The colour coral is simply the colour of red coral, not a separate root.
normal.cn: 颜色义 coral 就是红珊瑚的颜色，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Coral reef and coral island are fixed compounds; reef alone can be rock or sand.
normal.cn: coral reef 与 coral island 是固定复合词；单说 reef 则可能是岩礁或沙洲。

normal.en: Coralline and coralloid both start with coral but point to 'of coral' and 'like coral' respectively.
normal.cn: coralline 与 coralloid 都以 coral 开头，但分别指「珊瑚的」与「像珊瑚的」。

normal.en: Coral bleaching is the fixed phrase for the whitening that follows the loss of algal partners.
normal.cn: 珊瑚失去共生藻后变白，固定说法是 coral bleaching。

abstract.en: Picture a city built by animals that never leave home, each adding a room of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由从不离家的动物建起的城市，每只都添一间石屋。

abstract.en: Picture a pink branch that is soft while alive and becomes jewellery when dead.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粉色的枝，活着时柔软，死后变成首饰。

abstract.en: Picture a desert cliff holding the shape of a sea that vanished.
abstract.cn: 想象一面沙漠崖壁里留着早已消失的海洋的形状。

examples.en: Coral grows only where the water stays warm and clear.
examples.cn: 珊瑚只在水温温暖、水质清澈的地方生长。

examples.en: The island is a ring of coral around a drowned crater.
examples.cn: 这座岛是一圈环绕着沉没火山口的珊瑚。

examples.en: She chose a coral dress for the summer wedding.
examples.cn: 她为夏季婚礼选了一条珊瑚色的裙子。

dict_mnemonic.text: coral 读起来像「口若」——珊瑚枝一条条张开小口，像在不停地开口吃东西

root: 希腊 korallion「红珊瑚」→ 拉丁 corallium → 古法语 coral；korallion 的更深来源不确定，闪米特语来源只是一种假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object from life to stone to symbol: the living colony, its skeleton, the reef it raises, the polished material, the colour, the ornament, the fossil, and the charm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一物件从生命走到石头再走到象征：活体群体、骨骼、抬升的礁、打磨的材料、颜色、饰品、化石与护符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pink branching stone with tiny white tentacles at the tips.
core.cn: 核心意象：粉色的枝状石头，枝端伸出细小的白色触手。

branches.en: BUILDER AND BUILT: the colony makes the stone, then the stone outlasts the colony.
branches.cn: 建造者与被建造物：群体造出石头，石头又比群体活得久。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION: in geology the material is the reef itself.
branches.cn: 建筑：在地质语境中，这种材料就是礁体。

branches.en: MATERIAL TO ORNAMENT: cutting and polishing turn skeleton into gem and then into jewellery.
branches.cn: 从材料到饰品：切割打磨把骨骼变成宝石，再变成首饰。

branches.en: COLOUR BY METONYMY: the hue is named directly after the precious red kind.
branches.cn: 转喻得色：色调直接以贵重的红珊瑚命名。

branches.en: FROM STONE TO SYMBOL: the fossil proves an ancient sea, the charm promises protection.
branches.cn: 从石到象征：化石证明古海，护符许诺护佑。

intro.en: Coral is a borrowed noun with no productive English prefix; its family is built by compounding and by the suffixes -ine and -oid.
intro.cn: coral 是借入名词，没有能产的英语前缀；其词族靠复合与后缀 -ine、-oid 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin corallium and Greek korallion are the source forms; corallum is the Latin noun used in natural history for a coral colony.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 corallium 与希腊 korallion 是来源形式；corallum 是博物学中用于指珊瑚群体的拉丁名词。

items.meaning: red coral, and later any coral
items.meaningCN: 红珊瑚；后泛指各类珊瑚
items.example: Coral was once classed as a plant.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚曾被归为植物。

items.example: The reef holds hundreds of corals.
items.exampleCN: 这座礁有数百种珊瑚。

items.example: Coralline means belonging to coral.
items.exampleCN: coralline 意为属于珊瑚的。

items.meaning: of coral; also a red coralline alga
items.example: Coralline algae cement the reef frame.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚藻把礁体胶结起来。

items.example: The suffix marks resemblance, not identity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记相似，而非同一。

items.example: The mineral forms coralloid branches.
items.exampleCN: 这种矿物形成珊瑚状的枝。

items.meaning: a reef built chiefly by coral
items.example: The coral reef shelters the lagoon.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁护住了潟湖。

items.meaning: an island made largely of coral
items.example: Coral islands rise only a few metres above the sea.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚岛只高出海面几米。

items.example: The corallum is the whole skeletal frame.
items.exampleCN: corallum 指整个骨骼框架。

definition_zh: 歧义；含糊；模棱两可；犹豫不决；（意图的）不确定
definition_en: the quality of having more than one possible meaning, of being unclear, or of a state of doubt in which the mind cannot settle
core_image: 一句话被同时驱向两条路：两种读法都站得住，谁也没被甩开
scene: 审稿人读到「他们给旧船刷了漆和发动机」这一句，先笑出声，随后在页边写下批注。 The reviewer reads the sentence 'they painted the old boat and the engine', laughs, and notes the structural ambiguity in the margin.
sceneCN: 这里 ambiguity 是「句法歧义」（第 4 个义项：句子结构可作两种切分）；句意：审稿人读到这句话先笑出声，随后在页边记下它的句法歧义。场景要点：稿纸页边的批注、被圈出的 and、两种颜色的修改笔、停住的笔尖。

pos.zh: 歧义；含糊；模棱两可；犹豫不决

collocations.zh: 道德上的含混（人物或结局难以简单评判）

derivatives.zh: 有歧义的；含糊不清的；模棱两可的
含糊地；模棱两可地
歧义性；含糊
不含糊的；明确无误的
明确无误地

senses.title: Doubting, unable to decide
senses.titleCN: 犹疑不决：心智停不下来
senses.definition: the state of being unable to decide or of hesitating between possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 无法作出决定、在几种可能之间犹豫不定的状态
senses.example: His ambiguity about the job offer showed in the way he kept changing the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这份工作邀请的犹豫，表现在他总把话题岔开。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, recorded c.1400. Latin ambigere meant 'to be driven around', so the mind here is not empty of meaning; it is pulled first one way and then the other.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早的义项，约记录于 1400 年。拉丁语 ambigere 意为“被驱赶着转来转去”，所以这里并非“没有意思”，而是心智先被拉向一边、又被拉向另一边。

senses.title: Two meanings in one word
senses.titleCN: 一词两义：同一个词被读出两种意思
senses.definition: the quality of a word or phrase that can be understood in two or more different ways
senses.definitionCN: 一个词或短语可以被理解成两种或多种不同意思的性质
senses.example: The ambiguity of 'bank' made the joke work.
senses.exampleCN: bank 一词的歧义让这个笑话成立了。
senses.why: Once ambiguity names the word rather than the mind, the two directions of ambigere become two readings of one form. The word itself is the crossroads where both roads stay open.
senses.whyCN: 当 ambiguity 指的不是心智而是词语时，ambigere 的两个方向就变成同一个词形的两种读法。词本身就是那个两条路都敞开的十字路口。

senses.title: The meaning is left unclear
senses.titleCN: 表述含混：意义没有被说清
senses.definition: the quality of a statement or description that is not precise enough to be understood clearly
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或描述不够精确、因而无法被清楚理解的性质
senses.example: Critics attacked the ambiguity of the policy statement.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击那份政策声明的含混不清。
senses.why: Here the two readings are not both useful; the text simply fails to close the gap. The same fork remains, but it is now a defect of description, recorded from the early 15th century.
senses.whyCN: 这里两种读法并非都有用，文本只是没能把缺口合上。同一个分叉仍在，但此时它是表述上的缺陷；这一用法记录于 15 世纪早期。

senses.title: Two parses of one sentence
senses.titleCN: 同一句话的两种句法切分
senses.definition: in linguistics, the property of a sentence whose grammatical structure can be analysed in more than one way
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，指句子的语法结构可以被分析成不止一种形式
senses.example: The sentence 'old men and women' is famous for its structural ambiguity.
senses.exampleCN: “old men and women”这句话以结构歧义著称。
senses.why: The fork is no longer in the dictionary but in the brackets: [old men] and women assigns old to men only, while old [men and women] assigns it to both. One string of words supports two trees.
senses.whyCN: 分叉不在词典里，而在括号里：[old men] and women 把 old 只给 men，而 old [men and women] 把 old 同时给了 men 和 women。同一串词支撑起两棵句法树。

senses.title: Deliberate ambiguity in negotiation
senses.definition: the intentional use of unclear wording so that different parties can each read what they want into it
senses.definitionCN: 故意使用不清楚的措辞，让不同各方都能从中读出自己想要的意思
senses.example: The agreement preserved a deliberate ambiguity over the status of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议在该地区的地位问题上保留了一种有意的含糊。
senses.why: Both readings are kept alive on purpose. Instead of driving the mind to a decision, the wording lets each side drive it in its own direction, so ambiguity becomes a diplomatic tool rather than a fault.
senses.whyCN: 两种读法被有意地同时保留。措辞不把心智驱向某个决定，而是让每一方把它驱向自己的方向，于是含糊从缺陷变成了外交工具。

senses.title: One picture, two figures
senses.definition: the quality of an image or sound that can be perceived in two different ways, as in an ambiguous figure
senses.definitionCN: 图像或声音可以被感知为两种不同样式的性质，如双义图形
senses.example: The duck-rabbit drawing is a classic case of perceptual ambiguity.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭兔图是知觉歧义的经典例子。
senses.why: The eye, like the mind in the earliest sense, is driven to two gestalts and can flip between them. Both readings are fully present in the same stimulus, so neither can be dismissed.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛就像最早义项里的心智，被驱向两种完形，并在两者之间翻转。两种读法都完整地存在于同一个刺激中，因此哪一种都无法被排除。

senses.title: An unclear position or role
senses.definition: the state of having a role or status that is not clearly defined, so that expectations remain unsettled
senses.definitionCN: 所担任的角色或地位没有被清楚界定、因而期待始终悬而未决的状态
senses.example: The ambiguity of her position as adviser and friend caused friction.
senses.exampleCN: 她既是顾问又是朋友，这种身份的模糊引发了摩擦。
senses.why: A person can occupy two categories at once. Neither label wins, so the social situation wavers like the original verb: the same person is legitimately read two ways.
senses.whyCN: 一个人可以同时占据两个类别。两个标签都不占上风，于是社会处境像原动词一样摇摆：同一个人被两种方式合理地解读。

senses.title: Meaning left open in a work
senses.titleCN: 作品中保留的开放意义
senses.definition: in literature and art, the quality of a work that invites several readings without settling on one
senses.definitionCN: 在文学与艺术中，作品邀请多种读法而不落定于其一的品质
senses.example: The ambiguity of the ending is what makes the novel memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 结局的开放含混正是这部小说令人难忘的原因。
senses.why: Here the fork is valued rather than repaired. The work holds two readings in suspension and leaves the reader to waver, turning the old defect into an aesthetic effect.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分叉是被珍视的，而不是被修复的。作品把两种读法悬置起来，让读者自己去摇摆，把旧的缺陷转成了审美效果。

senses.title: Unclear intention behind an act
senses.definition: the quality of an action or gesture whose underlying intention cannot be determined, even when the words or act themselves are clear
senses.definitionCN: 行为或姿态背后的意图无法确定，即使言语或动作本身很清楚
senses.example: There was an ambiguity in his kindness that made her distrust it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的善意里有某种说不清的意味，让她反而起了疑心。
senses.why: Two possible motives are driven at once, so the fork moves from wording to intention. The act is plain, but why it was done remains double, which is why the word can describe motives as well as sentences.
senses.whyCN: 两种可能的动机同时被驱动，分叉就从措辞移到了意图。行为本身很清楚，但“为什么这样做”仍然是双重的；因此这个词既能描述句子，也能描述动机。

intro.en: Ambiguity comes from Latin ambiguitas, a noun of state from ambiguus 'having double meaning'. The verb behind it is ambigere 'to dispute, wander, waver', literally ambi- 'about, both ways' + agere 'to drive'. The second element is therefore agere, not a piece that sounds like 'guity'; the core image is a mind driven in two directions at once.
intro.cn: ambiguity 来自拉丁语 ambiguitas，是由 ambiguus“有两种意思的”构成的状态名词。其背后的动词是 ambigere“争执、徘徊、犹豫”，字面为 ambi-“两边、周围”+ agere“驱动”。因此第二成分是 agere，而不是某个听起来像“guity”的部分；核心意象是心智同时被驱向两个方向。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'uncertainty, doubt, indecision, hesitation', from Old French ambiguite and directly from Latin ambiguitatem (nominative ambiguitas). The earliest sense is about the doubting mind, not about a double-meaning word.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“不确定、怀疑、犹豫不决”，来自古法语 ambiguite，并直接来自拉丁语 ambiguitatem（主格 ambiguitas）。最早的义项说的是犹豫的心智，而不是一词两义。

items.en: Ambiguitas was a noun of state from ambiguus 'having double meaning, doubtful'. That adjective already contains the fork: a thing can be taken in two ways, and therefore the person facing it does not know which way to go.
items.cn: ambiguitas 是由 ambiguus“有两种意思的、可疑的”构成的状态名词。那个形容词本身已经含有分叉：一件事可以被两种方式理解，因此面对它的人不知道该往哪边走。

items.en: Ambigere meant 'to dispute about, contend, debate', but literally 'to wander, go about, go around', and figuratively 'to hesitate, waver, be in doubt'. The physical image is being driven around in circles rather than arriving at a point.
items.cn: ambigere 意为“就……争执、辩论”，但字面是“游荡、四处走、绕圈”，引申为“犹豫、摇摆、存疑”。其身体意象是被驱赶着绕圈，而不是抵达某一点。

items.en: Ambi- 'about' is from PIE *ambhi- 'around'; agere 'drive, lead, act' is from PIE *ag- 'to drive, draw out or forth, move'. So the word is built on driving, not on any root meaning 'doubt' or 'two-faced'. Ambiguity is what happens when something is driven both ways at once.
items.cn: ambi-“周围”来自原始印欧语 *ambhi-“环绕”；agere“驱动、引领、行动”来自 *ag-“驱赶、拉出、移动”。因此这个词建立在“驱动”上，而不是任何意为“怀疑”或“两面”的词根上。ambiguity 就是某物被同时驱向两边的结果。

items.en: The sense 'obscurity in description' is recorded from the early 15th century. The adjective ambiguous follows later, first attested in Sir Thomas More in 1528, so the abstract noun was in English before its adjective became common.
items.cn: “描述含混”这一义项记录于 15 世纪早期。形容词 ambiguous 出现更晚，最早见于 1528 年的托马斯·莫尔；也就是说，这个抽象名词先进入英语，其形容词后来才通行。

items.en: Modern English extends the same fork to syntax, perception, diplomacy, social roles, art and motive. Two look-alikes must be kept apart: ambivalent is ambi- + valere 'to be worth, be strong', and ambition is ambi- + ire 'to go'. Neither shares the agere element of ambiguity.
items.cn: 现代英语把同一个分叉扩展到句法、知觉、外交、社会角色、艺术与动机。两个形似词必须分开：ambivalent 是 ambi- + valere“有价值、有力量”，ambition 是 ambi- + ire“走”。两者都不含 ambiguity 的 agere 成分。

note.en: The first group separates words that look or sound like ambiguity but are built from different Latin verbs; the second compares words learners often use in its place. The key test is whether the trouble lies in two readings or in missing knowledge.
note.cn: 第一组区分那些形似或音似 ambiguity、却由不同拉丁动词构成的词；第二组比较学习者常用来替换它的词。关键区别是：麻烦究竟来自“两种读法”，还是来自“知识缺失”。

entries.definition: having more than one possible meaning. It is the adjective from ambiguity and names the thing that carries two readings, not the state of doubt itself.
entries.definitionCN: 具有不止一种可能意思的。它是 ambiguity 派生的形容词，指承载两种读法的那个东西，而不是犹疑状态本身。

entries.definition: having mixed or conflicting feelings about someone or something. It is ambi- plus Latin valere 'to be strong, be worth', so it is about two pulls of feeling, not two meanings.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某事怀有混合、矛盾的情感。它是 ambi- 加拉丁语 valere“有力量、有价值”，说的是两种情感拉力，而不是两种意思。

entries.definition: a strong desire to achieve something. It goes back to Latin ambire 'to go around', originally canvassing for votes: ambi- + ire 'to go', with no agere.
entries.definitionCN: 实现某事的强烈愿望。它上溯拉丁语 ambire“四处走”，原指为拉票而奔走：ambi- + ire“走”，不含 agere。

entries.definition: relating to walking, or able to walk. It comes from Latin ambulare 'to walk', which merely happens to begin with amb-. There is no ambi- prefix at all.
entries.definitionCN: 与行走有关的，或能行走的。它来自拉丁语 ambulare“行走”，只是碰巧以 amb- 开头，根本没有 ambi- 前缀。

entries.definition: the quality of being imprecise or lacking a clear boundary. Vagueness says the edges are fuzzy; ambiguity says two or more distinct readings are actually available.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确或缺少清晰边界的性质。vagueness 说边界模糊；ambiguity 说确实存在两种或更多彼此不同的读法。

entries.definition: the use of a word with more than one meaning in order to mislead. Equivocation adds the intent to deceive, while ambiguity can be innocent or even useful.
entries.definitionCN: 利用一词多义来误导他人。equivocation 多了一层欺骗意图，而 ambiguity 可以是无意的，甚至是有用的。

entries.definition: the state of not knowing what will happen or what is true. Uncertainty is about the observer's ignorance; ambiguity is about the object supporting several readings.
entries.definitionCN: 不知道会发生什么或什么是真的。uncertainty 说的是观察者的无知；ambiguity 说的是对象本身支持多种读法。

entries.definition: the quality of being hard to understand because it is hidden or unfamiliar. Obscurity hides one meaning; ambiguity displays two.
entries.definitionCN: 因隐蔽或陌生而难以理解的性质。obscurity 把一种意思藏起来；ambiguity 则把两种意思摆出来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ambi- 'both ways' plus agere 'to drive', the ambiguity family, and the three look-alikes built from valere, ire and ambulare.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ambi-“两边”加 agere“驱动”、ambiguity 词族，以及由 valere、ire、ambulare 构成的三个形似词。

normal.en: ambi- means 'both ways' and agere means 'to drive'. Ambiguity is literally a thing driven in two directions at once.
normal.cn: ambi- 意为“两边”，agere 意为“驱动”。ambiguity 字面上就是“被同时驱向两边的状态”。

normal.en: The same agere root gives agent, act, agenda and agile, so ambiguity belongs with 'driving and doing', not with any word for 'two-faced'.
normal.cn: 同一 agere 词根给出 agent、act、agenda、agile，所以 ambiguity 属于“驱动与行动”这一族，与任何“两面”词无关。

normal.en: Three look-alikes use three different second elements: ambivalent has valere 'be worth', ambition has ire 'go', ambulatory has ambulare 'walk'.
normal.cn: 三个形似词用了三个不同的第二成分：ambivalent 是 valere“有价值”，ambition 是 ire“走”，ambulatory 是 ambulare“行走”。

normal.en: The earliest sense was 'hesitation', not 'double meaning'. The mind wavered first; the word's double meaning was named later.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“犹豫”，不是“一词两义”。先有摇摆的心智，后来才用它命名词语的双重意思。

normal.en: Structural ambiguity lives in brackets: [old men] and women versus old [men and women].
normal.cn: 结构歧义活在括号里：[old men] and women 对 old [men and women]。

abstract.en: Picture a road that splits at a fork. The driver is not lost for lack of a map; both roads are real, and the car is pulled down each one in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一条在岔口分开的路。司机并非因为没有地图而迷路；两条路都真实存在，车子被先后拉向每一条。

abstract.en: The same fork can sit in a word, a sentence, a drawing, a treaty, a job title or a gesture. What stays constant is that two readings remain standing at once.
abstract.cn: 同一个分叉可以藏在单词、句子、图画、条约、职位名称或一个姿态里。不变的是：两种读法同时立着。

abstract.en: Sometimes the fork is a fault to be repaired; sometimes it is deliberately preserved. Ambiguity can therefore be either a problem or a resource.
abstract.cn: 有时这个分叉是要修掉的缺陷，有时它被有意保留。因此 ambiguity 既可能是问题，也可能是资源。

examples.en: Please rewrite the sentence to remove its ambiguity.
examples.cn: 请改写这句话，消除它的歧义。

examples.en: The play ends in ambiguity, and each audience member decides what happened.
examples.cn: 这部剧以含糊收场，每位观众都自己判断到底发生了什么。

examples.en: There was an ambiguity in her tone that made him unsure whether she was joking.
examples.cn: 她的语气里有某种含混，让他拿不准她是不是在开玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必鬼题」——俺必答的那道鬼题，两个答案都说得通 → ambiguity 歧义、模棱两可

root: 来自拉丁语 ambiguitas，上溯 ambiguus“有两种意思的”与 ambigere“徘徊、争执”，字面是 ambi-“两边”加 agere“驱动”，核心是“心智被同时驱向两边”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ambiguity, all one fork: a form, a situation or a mind is driven in two directions at once. Sometimes both readings are legitimate, sometimes the split is a defect, and sometimes it is deliberately preserved.
sensesIntro.cn: ambiguity 的九个义项都源于同一个分叉：一个词形、一种处境或一颗心智被同时驱向两个方向。有时两种读法都合法，有时分裂是缺陷，有时它被有意保留。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one form or situation driven down two roads at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个词形或处境被同时驱上两条路。

branches.en: INNER FORK: hesitation and unclear motive. The mind is pulled both ways before any wording is fixed.
branches.cn: 内在分叉：犹豫与动机不明。措辞尚未固定，心智先被拉向两边。

branches.en: CODE: one word or one sentence carries two readings, whether in the dictionary or in the brackets.
branches.cn: 代码层：一个词或一句话承载两种读法，无论在词典里还是在句法括号里。

branches.en: TEXT: vagueness is a fault and open-endedness is a virtue, but both leave meaning unresolved.
branches.cn: 文本层：含混是缺陷，开放是美德，但两者都让意义悬而未决。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: negotiators and social roles keep two readings alive, sometimes on purpose and sometimes by accident.
branches.cn: 制度层：谈判者与社会角色让两种读法同时存活，有时出于有意，有时出于无意。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: the eye flips between two figures held in one drawing.
branches.cn: 知觉层：眼睛在一张图里所持的两个形象之间翻转。

intro.en: Ambiguity is a Latin-derived noun whose parts are frozen: ambi- 'both ways' + agere 'to drive' + -ity. English adds only ordinary suffixes to the finished family. The -ity is not a meaning-bearing 'guity' chunk, and the whole word never meant 'two-faced'.
intro.cn: ambiguity 是拉丁来源的名词，其成分已经凝固：ambi-“两边”+ agere“驱动”+ -ity。英语只是在成品词族后加普通后缀。-ity 并不是一个带意义的“guity”部件，整个词也从来不是“两面派”的意思。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is ambigere 'to dispute, wander, waver', its adjective ambiguus 'double-meaning, doubtful', and agere 'to drive, lead, act'. The same agere yields agent, act, agenda and agile, while ambivalent and ambition belong to valere and ire respectively.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 ambigere“争执、徘徊、犹豫”、其形容词 ambiguus“有两种意思的、可疑的”，以及 agere“驱动、引领、行动”。同一 agere 给出 agent、act、agenda、agile，而 ambivalent 与 ambition 分别属于 valere 和 ire。

items.structure: ambi- (both ways) + agere (to drive) + -ity (noun of state)
items.meaning: the state of being driven two ways, hence double meaning or doubt
items.meaningCN: 被驱向两边的状态，因而指歧义或犹疑（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The ambiguity of the clause delayed the signing.
items.exampleCN: 条款的歧义推迟了签署。

items.meaning: open to more than one interpretation
items.meaningCN: 可作不止一种解释的；有歧义的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave an ambiguous answer and left the room.
items.exampleCN: 他给了个模棱两可的回答，然后离开了房间。

items.meaning: in a way that can be understood in more than one sense
items.meaningCN: 以含糊、可作多种理解的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She smiled ambiguously and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 她含义不明地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.meaningCN: 有歧义性；含糊（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The ambiguousness of the title was intentional.
items.exampleCN: 标题的含混是有意为之。

items.meaningCN: 不含糊的；只有一种清楚意思的（un- 否定）
items.example: The instructions were short and unambiguous.
items.exampleCN: 说明简短而明确。

items.meaning: in a way that leaves no doubt
items.meaningCN: 毫不含糊地；明确无误地
items.example: The court ruled unambiguously in her favour.
items.exampleCN: 法院明确无误地判她胜诉。

items.structure: ambi- (both) + valere (to be worth, be strong) — a different root
items.meaning: having mixed feelings; not the same as having two meanings
items.meaningCN: 有矛盾情感的；与“两种意思”不同源（valere 有价值、有力量）
items.example: She felt ambivalent about moving abroad.
items.exampleCN: 她对移居国外心情矛盾。

items.meaning: the state of having conflicting feelings
items.meaningCN: 矛盾情感；正反情绪并存（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: His ambivalence made the decision harder.
items.exampleCN: 他的矛盾心理让决定更难做。

items.structure: ambi- (around) + ire (to go) — a different root
items.meaning: a strong drive to achieve something, originally 'going around' to canvass
items.meaningCN: 雄心；抱负（原指四处奔走拉票，与 agere 无关）
items.example: Her ambition was to lead the research team.
items.exampleCN: 她的抱负是领导这个研究团队。

items.structure: ambi- (around) + ire (to go) — a different root
items.meaning: the scope or boundary of something
items.meaningCN: 范围；界限（同 ambire 一族，与 agere 无关）
items.example: That question lies outside the ambit of the inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 那个问题不在调查范围之内。

latinEntries.meaning: to dispute, wander, waver, be in doubt

definition_zh: 大气环流；大气中热量与水汽的大尺度输送与循环
definition_en: the large-scale movement of air that carries heat and moisture around a planet
core_image: 一张挂在墙上的全球地图，上面画满从赤道升起、向两极弯曲的箭头
scene: 气象台的屏幕上，一圈圈箭头从赤道升起、向两极偏转，值班员在图上标出雨带。 The map showed atmospheric circulation lifting warm air at the equator and turning it poleward.
sceneCN: 这里指全球尺度的大气环流（第 1 个义项：大气热量与水汽的大范围输送）；句意为图上显示大气环流在赤道抬起暖空气，并使其向极地方向偏转。图中可辨识物件：气象屏、箭头流线、雨带标记、全球地图。

pos.zh: 名词短语：多作不可数，指大气的大尺度环流；强调某一具体环流时可加修饰语

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语表示「蒸汽」与「球体」的成分构成，义为「大气；气氛」
由本短语第一成分构成，义为「大气的」
由拉丁语表示「小环」的名词构成的动词，义为「循环；流通」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「循环；流通」
由本短语第二成分加形容词词尾构成，义为「循环的」

senses.title: Global circulation
senses.definition: the planet-wide system of winds that moves heat from warm regions to cold ones
senses.definitionCN: 把热量从温暖区域输送到寒冷区域的行星尺度风系
senses.example: Atmospheric circulation carries heat from the tropics toward the poles.
senses.exampleCN: 大气环流把热量从热带输送到两极。
senses.why: Without a moving atmosphere the tropics would keep their heat and the poles would keep their cold.
senses.whyCN: 若没有运动的大气，热带会一直保有热量，两极则一直寒冷。

senses.title: The three-cell model
senses.definition: the textbook division of global circulation into polar, mid-latitude and tropical cells
senses.definitionCN: 教科书把全球环流分为极地、中纬度与热带三个环流圈
senses.example: The three-cell model simplifies atmospheric circulation into polar, mid-latitude and tropical cells.
senses.exampleCN: 三圈环流模型把大气环流简化为极地、中纬度与热带三个环流圈。
senses.why: A single cell cannot span a rotating planet, so the flow breaks into three bands per hemisphere.
senses.whyCN: 单个环流圈无法覆盖一颗自转的行星，因此每个半球分裂为三段。

senses.title: The Hadley cell
senses.definition: the tropical overturning in which air rises at the equator, flows poleward aloft and sinks near thirty degrees
senses.definitionCN: 热带地区的翻转环流：空气在赤道上升，高空向极地流动，在纬度约三十度处下沉
senses.example: The Hadley cell is the tropical part of atmospheric circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 哈得来环流是大气环流中热带的那一部分。
senses.why: A named cell makes the tropics a single machine with a rising and a sinking side.
senses.whyCN: 一个被命名的环流圈把热带变成一台只有上升侧与下沉侧的机器。

senses.title: The Walker circulation
senses.definition: the east-west overturning over the equatorial Pacific that links sea temperature to rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 赤道太平洋上东西方向的翻转环流，把海温与降水联系起来
senses.example: The Walker circulation is a key part of atmospheric circulation over the Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 沃克环流是太平洋上空大气环流的关键部分。
senses.why: The tropics also overturn along the equator, not only across latitudes.
senses.whyCN: 热带不仅在纬向翻转，也沿赤道方向翻转。

senses.title: The jet stream
senses.definition: a narrow fast current of air in the upper troposphere that steers weather systems
senses.definitionCN: 对流层上部狭窄而快速的气流，引导天气系统移动
senses.example: Jet streams are fast ribbons within the upper atmospheric circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 急流是上层大气环流中快速的气带。
senses.why: Concentrating the flow into a narrow band makes it far faster than the surrounding air.
senses.whyCN: 把流动集中于狭窄的一条，使它远快于周围空气。

senses.title: Monsoon circulation
senses.definition: a seasonal reversal of winds between land and sea caused by uneven heating
senses.definitionCN: 海陆受热不均导致风向随季节反向的环流
senses.example: Monsoon circulation is the seasonal part of atmospheric circulation that reverses with the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 季风环流是大气环流中随季节反向的那一部分。
senses.why: Land heats faster than water, so the pressure pattern flips and the wind follows.
senses.whyCN: 陆地升温快于水面，气压格局翻转，风便随之转向。

senses.title: Circulation and climate zones
senses.definition: the link between patterns of rising and sinking air and the wet or dry zones they produce
senses.definitionCN: 空气上升与下沉的格局同其所造成的湿润或干旱地带之间的联系
senses.example: Regions with weak atmospheric circulation receive little rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 大气环流较弱的地区降水很少。
senses.why: Rising air rains and sinking air dries, so the map of circulation becomes a map of climates.
senses.whyCN: 上升的空气下雨，下沉的空气致旱，环流图因此成了气候图。

senses.title: Circulation on other planets
senses.definition: the wind systems of other atmospheres, shaped by their own rotation, heating and composition
senses.definitionCN: 其他天体大气的风系，由其自转、受热与成分塑形
senses.example: Venus has an atmospheric circulation that turns far faster than the planet itself.
senses.exampleCN: 金星的大气环流旋转得远比行星本身快。
senses.why: The same physics applied elsewhere produces circulation patterns that no earthly textbook predicts.
senses.whyCN: 同一套物理用到别处，会产生地球教科书无法预言的运动格局。

senses.title: Indoor air circulation
senses.definition: the movement of air within a room that keeps temperature and freshness even
senses.definitionCN: 房间内使温度与新鲜度保持均匀的空气流动
senses.example: Good atmospheric circulation in a room keeps the air from going stale.
senses.exampleCN: 房间内良好的空气循环能防止空气变得沉闷。
senses.why: The same words scale down from a planet to a room, because both depend on air being moved rather than still.
senses.whyCN: 同一组词从行星缩小到房间仍可用，因为两者都依赖空气被移动而非静止。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective for the vapour sphere around a world to a Latin-derived noun for movement in a ring. Both elements are well documented; the phrase took its meteorological sense in the nineteenth century, so its first use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个源自希腊语、表示环绕世界的蒸汽层的形容词，与一个源自拉丁语、表示环状运动的名词组合起来。两个成分来源有据；短语在十九世纪取得气象学含义，确切首见为约数。

items.en: Atmos meant vapour or steam, the invisible envelope of a world.
items.cn: 这个词表示蒸汽或雾气，即环绕世界的那层看不见的东西。

items.en: Sphaira meant a ball or sphere, and the two together named the vapour sphere.
items.cn: 这个词表示球体，两者合起来命名了「蒸汽之球」。

items.en: Circulus was a small ring, the diminutive of the word for a circle.
items.cn: 这个词是表示圆的名词的小称，意为小环。

items.en: The verb meant to make round or to move in a circle.
items.cn: 这个动词意为做成圆形或在环中运动。

items.en: English first applied the noun to blood, then to any fluid moving in a circuit.
items.cn: 英语先用这个名词指血液循环，后指任何沿回路流动的流体。

items.en: Nineteenth-century meteorology needed a term for planetary-scale wind systems, and the two words were joined.
items.cn: 十九世纪的气象学需要一个指行星尺度风系的术语，两个词于是被组合起来。

note.en: The first group shares the adjective atmospheric or the noun circulation; the second group names the motion of air in plainer terms.
note.cn: 第一组共享形容词「大气的」或名词「环流」；第二组用更朴素的说法指空气的运动。

entries.definition: The weight of the air column at a point.
entries.definitionCN: 某点上空气柱的重量。

entries.definition: One of the stacked shells of a planet's air.
entries.definitionCN: 行星大气层叠结构中的一层。

entries.definition: A numerical representation of the state of the air.
entries.definitionCN: 对大气状态的数值表示。

entries.definition: Movement of a fluid around a closed path.
entries.definitionCN: 流体沿闭合路径的运动。

entries.definition: The envelope of gas around a planet.
entries.definitionCN: 行星周围的气体外壳。

entries.definition: The movement of air from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 空气从一处到另一处的运动。

entries.definition: The recurring shape of winds over a region.
entries.definitionCN: 某一地区风的反复出现的形态。

entries.definition: Vertical motion driven by heating from below.
entries.definitionCN: 由下方加热驱动的垂直运动。

entries.definition: The whole set of prevailing winds on a planet.
entries.definitionCN: 一颗行星上全部盛行风的总和。

entries.definition: A moving pattern of pressure, cloud and rain.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的气压、云与降水格局。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations start at the equator and follow the arrows outward and back; abstract ones treat circulation as a way of evening out what the sun makes uneven.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想从赤道出发，沿着箭头向外再返回；抽象联想把环流看作把太阳造成的不均匀重新摊平的方式。

normal.en: Warm air rises at the equator and turns poleward.
normal.cn: 暖空气在赤道上升，并向极地方向偏转。

normal.en: It sinks near thirty degrees, which is why deserts sit there.
normal.cn: 它在纬度约三十度处下沉，沙漠因此分布在那里。

normal.en: Each hemisphere splits into three cells because the planet spins.
normal.cn: 由于行星自转，每个半球分成三个环流圈。

normal.en: A jet stream is the fast core of the upper flow.
normal.cn: 急流是上层气流中速度快的那条核心。

normal.en: Over the Pacific the flow also turns east to west, and that is the Walker cell.
normal.cn: 在太平洋上空气流还东西向翻转，那就是沃克环流。

abstract.en: Circulation is the atmosphere refusing to let heat stay where it landed.
abstract.cn: 环流是大气拒绝让热量留在原地。

abstract.en: Every rising column must have somewhere to sink.
abstract.cn: 每一处上升的气柱都必须在某处下沉。

abstract.en: Wind is not weather's decoration; it is its accounting system.
abstract.cn: 风不是天气的装饰，而是天气的记账系统。

examples.en: Atmospheric circulation redistributes heat from low to high latitudes.
examples.cn: 大气环流把热量从低纬重新分配到高纬。

examples.en: The study linked weaker atmospheric circulation to drier summers.
examples.cn: 这项研究把减弱的大气环流与更干旱的夏季联系起来。

examples.en: Climate models resolve atmospheric circulation at ever finer scales.
examples.cn: 气候模式以越来越精细的尺度解析大气环流。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmospheric（大气的）+ circulation（循环）——大气的循环，即大气环流

root: 由 atmospheric 与 circulation 组合。前者源自希腊语 atmos「蒸汽」与 sphaira「球体」；后者源自拉丁语 circulus「小环」及其动词 circulare「使成环状」。短语在十九世纪气象学中取得现代含义，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move outward from the planet-wide flow to its cells, its jet, its seasonal reversal, its climates, other worlds and finally a single room.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从行星尺度的流动向外展开，走向各个环流圈、急流、季节反转、气候带、其他天体，最后收束到一个房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arrows rising at the equator and bending toward the poles on a wall map.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙图上从赤道升起、向两极弯曲的箭头。

branches.en: THE CORE: the whole moving envelope and the three-cell shorthand used to teach it.
branches.cn: 核心：整个运动的大气层，以及用于教学的「三圈」简写。

branches.en: THE NAMED CELLS: one overturning across latitudes, one across the equatorial Pacific.
branches.cn: 被命名的环流圈：一个跨纬度翻转，一个沿赤道太平洋翻转。

branches.en: THE FAST AND SEASONAL: a narrow upper jet and a wind that reverses with the seasons.
branches.cn: 快速与季节性的两种：狭窄的高空急流，以及随季节反向的风。

branches.en: THE SCALES: wet and dry climate zones, other planets, and a single room.
branches.cn: 尺度变化：干湿气候带、其他行星，以及单个房间。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: circulation on a world that spins differently.
branches.cn: 比较对象：自转方式不同的世界上的环流。

intro.en: A Greek noun of vapour plus a Greek noun of sphere give the first element; a Latin ring gives the second.
intro.cn: 一个希腊语「蒸汽」名词加一个希腊语「球体」名词构成第一成分；一个拉丁语「环」构成第二成分。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies atmos and sphaira; Latin supplies circulus, its verb and the noun of motion.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「蒸汽」与「球体」；拉丁语提供了「小环」、其动词以及表示运动的名词。

items.example: It named the invisible envelope rather than the air itself.
items.exampleCN: 它命名的是看不见的外壳，而非空气本身。

items.example: It supplied the second half of atmosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了「大气」一词的后半部分。

items.example: It turns atmosphere into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「大气」变成形容词。

items.example: The diminutive sense survives in the idea of a closed loop.
items.exampleCN: 小称含义残留在「闭合回路」这一观念中。

items.meaning: to make round, to move in a circle
items.example: The verb yields the English verb circulate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词产生英语动词「循环」。

items.example: It names movement around a circuit.
items.exampleCN: 它命名沿回路的运动。

items.example: The noun first described blood and later air.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指血液，后指空气。

items.example: The adjective makes the phrase specific to a planet's air.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词使短语专门指行星的大气。

definition_zh: 熔化的；（金属、岩石）熔融的；浇铸成的
definition_en: made liquid by great heat, especially metal or rock; shaped by being poured while melted
core_image: 炉口倾出的铁水在砂模沟槽里铺开，暗红的光顺槽流动，冷却后凝成一块硬物
scene: 铸工打开炉门，橙红色的金属液顺着沟槽流进砂模，空气里全是热浪。 The molten iron ran along the channel and filled the sand mould.
sceneCN: 这里 molten 指「经高温熔化后呈液态的」（第 1 个义项：因高热熔成液体，多指金属或岩石）；句意为熔化的铁水沿沟槽流下，灌满砂模。可辨识物件：炉门、铁水沟槽、砂模、热浪。

senses.title: Metal made liquid by heat
senses.definition: of metal: melted and still liquid because of intense heat
senses.definitionCN: 指金属因高温熔化而处于液态
senses.example: The molten iron ran along the channel and filled the sand mould.
senses.exampleCN: 熔化的铁水沿沟槽流下，灌满了砂模。
senses.why: molten is the old past participle of melt, and -en in broken, frozen and spoken marks a finished state, so the word describes metal that has already been liquefied, not metal that is melting now.
senses.whyCN: molten 是 melt 的古老过去分词，而 broken、frozen、spoken 中的 -en 都标记完成状态，因此这个词说的是「已经熔成液体」的金属，而不是「正在熔化」的金属。

senses.title: Rock melted underground
senses.titleCN: 地下的岩石呈熔融状态
senses.definition: of rock: liquefied by the heat of the earth, as in magma below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石因地热而熔化，如地表之下的岩浆
senses.example: Molten rock rises through cracks in the crust and feeds the volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 熔融的岩石沿地壳裂缝上升，为火山提供物质。
senses.why: the geological sense keeps the same picture but moves it underground, where pressure and heat hold rock in a liquid state that would freeze at the surface.
senses.whyCN: 地质义沿用同一幅图景，只是把它移到地下：在高压与高温下，岩石保持液态，一旦到地表就会凝固。

senses.title: Glass or other material in a furnace
senses.titleCN: 玻璃等材料在炉中熔成液态
senses.definition: of glass, wax or similar material: reduced to liquid in a furnace or crucible
senses.definitionCN: 指玻璃、蜡等材料在炉或坩埚中熔成液体
senses.example: Workers poured the molten glass into a long iron trough.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把熔融的玻璃倒进一条长铁槽。
senses.why: the participle was never limited to metals; any solid that heat turns into a pourable liquid can be called molten, and glass-making fixed the word in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词从来不限于金属；任何被高温变成可倾倒液体的固体都可以叫 molten，制玻璃的工艺把这一义项固定下来。

senses.title: Glowing with heat
senses.definition: so hot that the material glows red, orange or white
senses.definitionCN: 指温度高到发出红、橙或白色光
senses.example: The molten core of the furnace lit the whole workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 炉膛里熔融的核心照亮了整个车间。
senses.why: a liquid at such temperatures radiates visible light, so molten naturally extends from 'liquid by heat' to 'glowing because of heat'.
senses.whyCN: 处于这种温度的液体会辐射可见光，因此 molten 从「因热成液」自然延伸到「因热发光」。

senses.title: Cast from melted material
senses.titleCN: 用熔化的材料浇铸成型
senses.definition: formed by pouring melted material into a mould and letting it harden
senses.definitionCN: 指把熔化的材料倒入模具、冷却硬化而成形
senses.example: A molten bronze horse was cast in a single pour.
senses.exampleCN: 一匹熔铜的马在一次浇铸中成型。
senses.why: casting is the practical use of the participle: the material is molten at the moment of the pour, and the shape it takes is the shape of the mould.
senses.whyCN: 浇铸是这个分词的实际用途：材料在倾倒的一刻是熔融的，它得到的形状就是模具的形状。

senses.title: High-temperature liquid in chemistry
senses.titleCN: 化学中的高温熔融体系
senses.definition: of a salt or reagent: melted and used as a liquid medium at high temperature
senses.definitionCN: 指盐或试剂在高温下熔成液体并作为反应介质
senses.example: Molten salt stores heat in the plant's thermal tanks.
senses.exampleCN: 熔盐在电厂的热罐中储存热量。
senses.why: in industrial chemistry the participle becomes a technical label: a molten salt is a liquid ionic medium, not water-based and not a solution.
senses.whyCN: 在工业化学中，这个分词成了技术标签：熔盐是液态离子介质，既不是水溶液，也不是溶剂中的溶液。

senses.title: Flowing light or colour in description
senses.titleCN: 描写中流动的光或色彩
senses.definition: literary: of light or colour, glowing and fluid as if poured
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：指光或色彩如被倾倒般流动、灼亮
senses.example: The molten gold of sunset spilled across the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 落日熔金般的光铺满海湾。
senses.why: the image of poured metal gives writers a way to describe light that seems liquid, and this figurative use keeps the heat and the flow of the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 「倾倒金属」的形象给写作者提供了描写看似液态的光的办法，这一比喻义保留了原图景中的高温与流动。

senses.title: Intense, barely contained feeling
senses.titleCN: 强烈而几乎压不住的情绪
senses.definition: figurative: of anger, energy or passion, so intense that it seems to burn and flow
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：指愤怒、能量或激情强烈到仿佛在燃烧、流动
senses.example: Her molten anger frightened everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她如熔岩般的怒火让屋里所有人都害怕。
senses.why: heat and loss of shape are the two parts of the image, and both transfer to emotion: something solid has become dangerous, moving and hot.
senses.whyCN: 高温与失去形状是这幅图景的两个部分，两者都能转移到情绪上：原本稳固的东西变得危险、流动而灼热。

intro.en: Molten is the old past participle of the English verb melt, and its history is the history of that verb rather than of a Latin borrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molten 是英语动词 melt 的古老过去分词，它的历史就是 melt 这个词的历史，而不是一次拉丁语借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Meltan meant 'to melt, become liquid, dissolve' and also 'to digest' in the bodily sense; the verb is recorded in Old English before the Norman period.
items.cn: meltan 意为「熔化、变成液体、溶解」，也指身体意义上的「消化」；这个词在诺曼征服之前的古英语中已有记录。

items.en: *Meltanan is a reconstruction supported by Old Norse melta and Old High German smelzan 'to melt'; no single attested form of the root survives outside the Germanic group.
items.cn: *meltanan 是重构形式，依据古诺斯语 melta 与古高地德语 smelzan「熔化」；这个词根在日耳曼语族之外没有留存下来的单一形式。

items.en: The ending -en marks a completed state in strong past participles such as broken, frozen, spoken and molten, so the form says 'already melted' rather than 'melting'.
items.cn: 后缀 -en 在 broken、frozen、spoken、molten 这类强变化过去分词中标记完成状态，因此这一形式说的是「已经熔化」，而不是「正在熔化」。

items.en: In Middle English molten is recorded of liquefied metal, wax and ore, usually in the phrase 'molten lead' or 'molten metal'.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，molten 已用于熔化的金属、蜡与矿石，常见于「熔铅」「熔融金属」这类说法。

items.en: From the seventeenth century metallurgy fixed the word in phrases such as molten iron, and geology later applied it to magma and lava; the technical senses keep the participle's perfect meaning.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，冶金学用 molten iron（铁水）这类说法把词固定下来，地质学后来把它用于岩浆与熔岩；这些技术义都保留了分词的完成意味。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic history of *meltanan is unsettled, and the old comparison with Latin mollis 'soft' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation; any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*meltanan 在日耳曼语之前的历史没有定论，把它与拉丁 mollis「软」相比只是假说，并非已证实的派生；凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound like molten but come from other roots; group two collects words for the same physical state of matter.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音近似但词根不同的词；第二组是描述同一物态的词。

entries.definition: Means to shed feathers, hair or skin, and comes from a separate Germanic and Old French line; the resemblance to molten is only in sound and spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为脱换羽毛、毛发或外皮，来自另一条日耳曼语与古法语线索；与 molten 的相似只在音形。

entries.definition: To extract metal from ore by heating, from Middle Dutch smelten 'to melt'; it is a Germanic relative of melt rather than a form of molten itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指加热矿石以提炼金属，来自中古荷兰语 smelten「熔化」；它是 melt 在日耳曼语中的亲属，而不是 molten 本身的一个形式。

entries.definition: A hollow form for casting, or the verb to shape something; it goes back through Old French to Latin modulus 'small measure', so it is not related to melt at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指浇铸用的凹型，或「塑造」这一动词；它经古法语上溯到拉丁 modulus「小量度」，与 melt 毫无词源关系。

entries.definition: The regular past participle of melt, used for anything that has melted, from butter to snow; molten is the older form and today mostly describes metal, rock and glass.
entries.definitionCN: melt 的规则过去分词，可用于黄油、积雪等任何融化之物；molten 是较早的形式，今天多用于金属、岩石与玻璃。

entries.definition: A formal or technical word for turning a solid into a liquid, from Latin liquere 'be fluid'; it states the result without the image of a furnace.
entries.definitionCN: 使固体变成液体的正式或技术用词，来自拉丁 liquere「呈液态」；它只陈述结果，不带炉火的形象。

entries.definition: Describes an object glowing with heat, from Latin candere 'to shine'; it names the light rather than the liquid state that molten includes.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体因高温而发光，来自拉丁 candere「发光」；它命名的是光，而 molten 还包含液态这一层。

entries.definition: Means melted together into one mass, from Latin fundere 'to pour'; it stresses union, where molten stresses the liquid condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指经热熔合为一体，来自拉丁 fundere「倾倒」；它强调结合，molten 强调液态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle ending, the real word family and the fixed technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词后缀、真实的词族与固定技术搭配。

normal.en: Melt plus -en: the same ending as in broken, frozen and spoken, all marking a finished state.
normal.cn: melt 加 -en：与 broken、frozen、spoken 同一个后缀，都标记完成状态。

normal.en: The family runs melt, melting, melted, meltwater, meltdown, remelt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 melt、melting、melted、meltwater、meltdown、remelt。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the sense: molten metal, molten rock, molten glass, molten salt.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承载词义：熔融金属、熔融岩石、熔融玻璃、熔盐。

normal.en: In geology the word pairs with magma below ground and lava above ground.
normal.cn: 在地质学中，这个词与地下的岩浆、地表的熔岩配对使用。

normal.en: Metallurgy supplies the everyday picture: molten iron is poured, never hammered.
normal.cn: 冶金学提供日常图景：铁水只能浇，不能锤。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that has lost its shape but kept all its wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛失去了形状，却保留了全部的蜡。

abstract.en: Picture a winter stream freezing into one flat sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天的小溪冻成一整片平玻璃。

abstract.en: Picture an argument heated until it becomes one glowing thread.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论被加热到只剩一根发亮的线。

examples.en: The foundry pours molten steel into ingots every four hours.
examples.cn: 铸造厂每隔四小时把钢水浇进钢锭模。

examples.en: Molten rock beneath the ridge pushes the crust upward.
examples.cn: 山脊之下的熔融岩石把地壳向上顶。

examples.en: The glassblower shaped the molten glass with a long iron pipe.
examples.cn: 吹玻璃工用长铁管给熔融玻璃塑形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩（mō）+ 尔（l）+ 腾（tén）」——热到腾起来、化成液体 → 熔化的

root: 古英语 meltan「熔化」的过去分词，属日耳曼语 *meltanan（重构形式）；后缀 -en 标记完成状态。更深来源不确定，与拉丁 mollis「软」的比较仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one physical event: solid material is heated until it can flow, and then that same event is used for glowing light, for casting, for industrial chemistry and finally for emotion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个物理事件展开：固体被加热到可以流动，这个事件随后被用于发光、浇铸、工业化学，最后用于情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a furnace mouth where solid metal leaves its shape and becomes a glowing stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：炉口处，固态金属失去形状，变成一道发光的流体。

branches.en: MATERIALS THAT MELT: iron in a ladle and rock under a volcano obey the same rule.
branches.cn: 会熔的材料：勺里的铁与火山下的岩石遵守同一条规则。

branches.en: FURNACE AND PLANT: glass in a crucible and salt in a thermal tank are both molten media.
branches.cn: 炉与厂：坩埚里的玻璃与热罐里的盐都是熔融介质。

branches.en: GLOW: heat so great that the liquid itself becomes the light source.
branches.cn: 发光：热到液体本身成为光源。

branches.en: CASTING: the liquid is given a shape during the moment it can flow.
branches.cn: 浇铸：在能够流动的那一刻，液体被赋予形状。

branches.en: IMAGE TRANSFER: poured light and molten anger keep the same heat and flow.
branches.cn: 意象转移：倾倒的光与熔岩般的怒火保留了同样的热与流动。

intro.en: Molten is an English participle rather than a Latin compound, but its ending and its family are still readable morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: molten 是英语分词而非拉丁复合词，但它的后缀与词族仍可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relative is reliable here: the verb is Germanic, and Latin mollis 'soft' is only a hypothesis, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than invented.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有可靠的拉丁同族词：该动词属日耳曼语，拉丁 mollis「软」只是假说，因此拉丁条目留空，不作编造。

items.example: The snow melted before noon.
items.exampleCN: 雪在中午前融化了。

items.example: Broken glass lay on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 碎玻璃摊在地上。

items.example: The molten iron ran along the channel.
items.exampleCN: 铁水沿沟槽流下。

items.meaning: in the process of becoming liquid
items.example: The melting ice fed the stream.
items.exampleCN: 融冰补给着溪流。

items.example: Melted wax sealed the letter.
items.exampleCN: 熔蜡封住了信口。

items.meaning: water released by melting ice or snow
items.meaningCN: 冰川或积雪融化产生的水
items.example: Meltwater cut a narrow channel.
items.exampleCN: 融水切出一条窄沟。

items.meaning: a reactor accident, or a total collapse
items.example: The meltdown ruined the reactor core.
items.exampleCN: 熔毁损毁了反应堆堆芯。

items.example: The coating is meltable at low heat.
items.exampleCN: 这层涂料低温即可熔化。

items.meaning: to melt something a second time
items.example: Scrap steel is remelted in an electric furnace.
items.exampleCN: 废钢在电炉中再熔。

definition_zh: 离散的；分开的；独立的；不连续的；分段式的
definition_en: separate and distinct, existing as individual units rather than as one continuous whole
core_image: 实验台上摆着一排互不相连的方块灯，每两盏之间留着一指宽的暗缝，各自有独立的开关
scene: 实验台上摆着一排互不相连的方块灯，每两盏之间留出一道暗缝，每盏灯都有自己的开关。 Each reading comes from a discrete sensor with its own wire.
sceneCN: 这里指彼此分开、各自独立的单元（第 1 个义项：分离独立）；句意为每个读数都来自一个自带线路的独立传感器。图中可辨识物件：方块灯、暗缝、独立开关。

pos.zh: 离散的；分开的；独立的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「分开地；离散地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「离散性；分离性」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使离散化；离散处理」
由离散化动词加名词尾构成，义为「离散化」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「未分开的；不分明的」

senses.title: Separate and distinct
senses.definition: existing as a separate unit that is clearly apart from others and not merged with them
senses.definitionCN: 作为与其他事物明显分开、不被合并的独立单元存在
senses.example: The two faults are discrete and need separate repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这两处故障彼此独立，需要分别修理。
senses.why: Latin discretus meant separated or distinguished, and this plain sense of standing apart is the base of every later use; the same participle also produced the homophone discreet, the word for cautious behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「discretus」意为分开的或辨别出来的，这种「各自分开」的本义是后来一切用法的根基；同一个分词还产生了同音词「discreet」，即言行谨慎之义。

senses.title: Taking separate values
senses.definition: changing only in separate countable values rather than over a smooth and unbroken range
senses.definitionCN: 只在可数的分离数值之间变化，而不是在平滑连续的区间上变化
senses.example: A discrete variable can take only whole numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 离散变量只能取整数。
senses.why: Mathematics took the word's core idea of separate units and applied it to quantities that jump from one value to the next.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了这个词「分离单元」的核心意思，用来指从一个数值跳到下一个数值的量。

senses.title: Data kept as separate items
senses.titleCN: 以分离条目保存的数据
senses.definition: stored as individual records or categories rather than as one continuous stream
senses.definitionCN: 以一条条独立记录或类别保存，而不是作为一条连续的数据流
senses.example: The survey collects discrete data on each household.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查收集每户的离散数据。
senses.why: Once values are counted separately, the records themselves are called discrete, and computing made this sense common.
senses.whyCN: 数值一旦被分开计数，记录本身也就被称为离散的，计算机领域使这一义项流行起来。

senses.title: Divided into separate stages
senses.definition: broken into separate parts or stages with clear gaps between them
senses.definitionCN: 被切分为彼此有明显间隔的部分或阶段
senses.example: The training runs in discrete stages of four weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 培训分为每期四周的独立阶段。
senses.why: A process cut at fixed points looks like a row of separate blocks, so the word also describes anything divided into stages.
senses.whyCN: 过程在固定节点被切开，看起来就像一排分开的块，因此这个词也形容被分成阶段的事物。

senses.title: Individual and particular
senses.definition: considered one by one as a particular case, apart from the rest of its class
senses.definitionCN: 作为特定个案逐个考虑，与其同类中的其余部分分开
senses.example: Each discrete case was reviewed by a different judge.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的案例都由不同的法官审理。
senses.why: If units are separate, attention can fall on one alone; this sense stresses the single item rather than the gap between items, while discreet still keeps its own meaning of caution.
senses.whyCN: 单元既然分开，注意力就可以只落在一个上面；这个义项强调单个个体，而不是个体之间的间隔，而「discreet」仍保留谨慎这一独立含义。

senses.title: A signal defined at separate instants
senses.titleCN: 在分离时刻取值的信号
senses.definition: a signal whose value is defined only at separate moments, as in digital or sampled systems
senses.definitionCN: 只在分离时刻才有确定取值的信号，如数字系统或采样系统中的信号
senses.example: The receiver converts the wave into a discrete signal.
senses.exampleCN: 接收机把波转换成离散信号。
senses.why: Electronics borrowed the mathematical sense: a sampled wave exists as a series of separate points, not as a smooth line.
senses.whyCN: 电子学借用了数学义：采样后的波是一串分离的点，而不是一条平滑的线。

senses.title: An isolated group of one species
senses.definition: a group of organisms of one species that is separated from other groups and breeds mainly within itself
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种中与其他群体隔开、主要在群体内部繁殖的一群生物
senses.example: The valley holds a discrete population of frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷里有一个分离的蛙类种群。
senses.why: Ecology reused the notion of a bounded unit: a population with a clear edge is separate from its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 生态学沿用了「有边界的单元」这一概念：边界清楚的种群与邻近种群分开。

senses.title: A model that jumps between events
senses.definition: a computer model in which the state changes only at separate scheduled events rather than continuously
senses.definitionCN: 一种计算机模型，其状态只在分离的预定事件发生时改变，而不是连续变化
senses.example: The airport model is a discrete simulation of gate use.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机场模型是对登机口使用情况的离散模拟。
senses.why: Simulation inherited the word from mathematics and computing, because the model steps from one event to the next.
senses.whyCN: 模拟技术从数学与计算领域继承了这个词，因为模型是从一个事件跳到下一个事件。

intro.en: Discrete comes from Latin discretus, the past participle of discernere, to separate or distinguish, formed from dis-, apart, and cernere, to sift. The same participle also produced discreet, the word for cautious behaviour, so the two English adjectives are homophones with different meanings.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「discretus」，是动词「discernere」（分开、辨别）的过去分词，由「dis-」（分开）加「cernere」（筛、辨别）构成。同一个分词也演化出表示言行谨慎的「discreet」，因此这两个英语形容词同音而异义。

items.en: The prefix meant apart or away, and it marks the act of putting things at a distance from one another.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开、离开，标记把事物彼此拉开距离的动作。

items.en: The verb meant to sift, to separate and to distinguish, the image behind a sieve or a screen.
items.cn: 这个动词意为筛、分开、辨别，其意象来自筛子或筛网。

items.en: With the prefix added, the verb meant to separate apart and hence to tell one thing from another.
items.cn: 加上前缀之后，这个动词意为分开，进而指把一事物与另一事物辨别开来。

items.en: The past participle meant separated or distinguished, and it became the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为被分开的或被辨别出的，后来成为这个英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: English adopted the form for things that stand apart, especially in mathematics and later in computing.
items.cn: 英语采用这一形式表示彼此分开的事物，尤见于数学，后来又用于计算领域。

items.en: The same Latin participle also gave English discreet, meaning careful in speech or behaviour; the two words sound alike but must not be confused.
items.cn: 同一个拉丁分词还给了英语「discreet」，意为言行谨慎；两个词读音相同，但不可混淆。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that look or sound like discrete; the second group gathers words for separation and difference.
note.cn: 第一组收录在形音上与「discrete」相近的形式；第二组收录表示分开与差异的说法。

entries.definition: Careful and prudent in speech or behaviour; it sounds the same as discrete but belongs to a different sense of the same Latin participle.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话或举止谨慎小心；与「discrete」读音相同，但属于同一拉丁分词的另一义。

entries.definition: In a careful and prudent manner, with no relation to separate units.
entries.definitionCN: 指以谨慎小心的方式，与「分离的单元」无关。

entries.definition: The freedom or power to decide, and the quality of being careful about what one says.
entries.definitionCN: 指决定权或裁量权，也指说话谨慎的品质。

entries.definition: To perceive or distinguish something that is not obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 指察觉或辨别不明显的事物。

entries.definition: A difference between two things that should agree; it looks close but comes from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指本应一致的两事物之间的差异；形近但来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Apart from others, not joined or shared.
entries.definitionCN: 指与他人分开、不连接或不共有的。

entries.definition: Clearly different and easily told apart from something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指明显不同、容易与其他事物区分开的。

entries.definition: Single and considered on its own, apart from the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个的、单独看待而不计入群体的。

entries.definition: Broken off and not continuing without a gap.
entries.definitionCN: 指中断的、不能无间隔延续的。

entries.definition: Separated from something it was once connected to.
entries.definitionCN: 指与原先把连在一起的事物分开的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin sieve behind the word, the real spelling contrast with discreet, and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的拉丁筛子、与「discreet」的真实拼写差别，以及真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: Cernere is to sift: discrete things have already been sifted apart.
normal.cn: 「cernere」是筛，离散的事物已经被筛分开。

normal.en: In discrete the two e letters are separated by t, which is exactly what the word means.
normal.cn: 「discrete」里的两个「e」被「t」隔开，正好就是这个词的意思。

normal.en: In discreet the two e letters sit together, a neat sign that the word is not about separation.
normal.cn: 「discreet」里的两个「e」挨在一起，正好提示这个词与分离无关。

normal.en: Discrete data, discrete points and discrete steps are ordinary terms in statistics and computing.
normal.cn: 离散数据、离散点与离散步骤是统计与计算领域的常用说法。

normal.en: A discrete event happens at one scheduled moment, so the model jumps from event to event.
normal.cn: 离散事件在某个预定时刻发生，因此模型从一个事件跳到下一个事件。

abstract.en: A discrete thing is a bead on a string: the string is continuous, the beads are not.
abstract.cn: 离散之物像线上的珠子：线是连续的，珠子不是。

abstract.en: Separateness can be a virtue: clear units are easier to count, store and compare.
abstract.cn: 分开也可以是一种优点：清楚的单元更容易计数、保存与比较。

abstract.en: The quiet danger is the homophone: the careful adviser is discreet, the separate unit is discrete.
abstract.cn: 无声的危险在同音：谨慎的顾问是「discreet」，分开的单元是「discrete」。

examples.en: The samples fall into three discrete groups.
examples.cn: 样本分成三个彼此独立的组。

examples.en: She keeps her work and home life discrete.
examples.cn: 她把工作与家庭生活分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of lamps stands apart, each with its own switch and its own dark gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排灯各自独立，每盏都有自己的开关与暗缝。

branches.en: THE SEPARATE ITEM: one unit stands apart, and attention can rest on that single case.
branches.cn: 分开的个体：一个单元独立存在，注意力也可以落在这单个案例上。

branches.en: THE COUNTED VALUE: numbers and records exist as separate points rather than a smooth range.
branches.cn: 计数的值：数值与记录以分离的点存在，而不是平滑区间。

branches.en: THE CUT PROCESS: a whole is divided into stages with clear gaps between them.
branches.cn: 切分的过程：整体被分成有明显间隔的阶段。

branches.en: THE SAMPLED WAVE: a signal lives only at separate instants in a digital system.
branches.cn: 采样的波：信号在数字系统中只存在于分离的时刻。

branches.en: THE BOUNDED MODEL: an isolated population and a simulation that steps from event to event.
branches.cn: 有边界的模型：隔离的种群，以及逐个事件推进的模拟。

intro.en: Discrete is the adjective of a Latin verb of separating, and its family includes both the technical words and the dangerous homophone.

definition_zh: 市场竞争；市场中多个卖者或买者为争夺同一批顾客、合同与资源而相互角逐的状态；竞争政策所规范的对象
definition_en: the state in which several sellers or buyers contend for the same customers, contracts or resources, each trying to win business away from the others
core_image: 一条街上几家卖同样货品的铺子并排开着，顾客一走近便被各家招手，铺主不断改价、换招牌、添赠品，只求把人引进自己门里
scene: 同一街区里开着几家卖同样货品的铺子，顾客一走近就被各家招手，铺主不断改价、换招牌、添赠品，只为把客人引进自己门里；傍晚一算账，谁家让价让得多，谁家门口就排得长。 Market competition keeps every one of them watching the others' prices.
sceneCN: 几家同类铺子在同一条街上争夺同一批过路人，彼此盯着对方的标价不断调整。句中的 market competition 指「多个主体争夺同一批顾客的状态」（第 1 个义项：同业者为同一批买主相互角逐）。图中可辨识物件：并排的店面、手写价牌、赠品篮、排队的人。

senses.title: Several sellers chasing the same buyers
senses.titleCN: 多个卖者追逐同一批买主
senses.definition: the ordinary situation in which two or more firms offer similar goods to the same group of customers
senses.definitionCN: 两家或更多厂商向同一群顾客提供相似货物的一般情形
senses.example: Market competition forces the two chains to match each other's opening hours.
senses.exampleCN: 市场竞争迫使两家连锁店把营业时间对齐。
senses.why: competition goes back to a Latin verb for seeking the same thing together, and market names the arena, so the phrase says that several parties seek one prize in one place.
senses.whyCN: competition 上溯一个表示「共同追求同一物」的拉丁动词，market 指场所，因此这个短语是说：多方在同一场所追逐同一个目标。

senses.title: Rivalry conducted through price
senses.titleCN: 以价格手段进行的争夺
senses.definition: contention carried on by cutting prices, offering discounts or matching a rival's rate
senses.definitionCN: 通过降价、折扣或与对手同价来进行的争夺
senses.example: Market competition in the budget sector has pushed fares down for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价市场的竞争已把票价压低了十年。
senses.why: price is the fastest lever a seller can pull, so the general rivalry is often narrowed to the one instrument that shows up first on a price board.
senses.whyCN: 价格是卖者能拉动的最快的杠杆，因此笼统的角逐常被收窄为最先写在价牌上的那件工具。

senses.title: Rivalry through quality and brands
senses.titleCN: 以品质、品牌与服务进行的争夺
senses.definition: contention carried on by improving quality, design, service or advertising rather than by cutting the price
senses.definitionCN: 通过提升品质、设计、服务或广告而非降价来进行的争夺
senses.example: Where fares are fixed by law, market competition shifts to legroom and punctuality.
senses.exampleCN: 当票价由法律规定时，市场竞争便转向腿部空间与准点率。
senses.why: once price is off the table, sellers must differentiate, so the word's field extends from the price tag to everything else a buyer weighs.
senses.whyCN: 一旦价格不可动，卖者只能在别处做出区别，于是这个词的范围从价签扩展到买方所权衡的一切。

senses.title: The benchmark of many small rivals
senses.titleCN: 作为基准的充分竞争状态
senses.definition: the idealised condition in which so many sellers exist that none can influence price, used as a measuring rod
senses.definitionCN: 一种理想化状态：卖者多到无人能影响价格，常被用作衡量的标尺
senses.example: The textbook treats market competition as a benchmark against which real industries are judged.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把市场竞争当作评判现实产业的基准。
senses.why: theory needs a limiting case, so the phrase also names the pole of perfect rivalry rather than any observable market.
senses.whyCN: 理论需要一个极值情形，因此这个短语也指「充分角逐」的那一端，而非任何可观察的市场。

senses.title: The object of competition law
senses.titleCN: 竞争法所保护与规范的对象
senses.definition: the rivalry that authorities protect by blocking mergers, cartels and abuses of dominance
senses.definitionCN: 主管机关通过阻止合并、卡特尔与滥用支配地位来保护的角逐
senses.example: The case turned on whether a rebate scheme had removed market competition in the dairy aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 该案的争点在于返利方案是否消除了乳品货架上的市场竞争。
senses.why: law personifies the phrase as something that can be harmed or preserved, which is why it appears as the object of enforcement verbs.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这个短语当作可被损害、也可被保全的对象，因此它常作执法动词的宾语。

senses.title: Rivalry between regions or states
senses.titleCN: 地区或辖区之间为吸引投资而竞争
senses.definition: contention among jurisdictions that cut taxes or offer subsidies to attract the same firms
senses.definitionCN: 各辖区为吸引同一批企业而减税或提供补贴的争夺
senses.example: Market competition between cities produced a costly race of tax breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 城市之间的市场竞争演变成一场代价高昂的减税竞赛。
senses.why: the sellers in this reading are governments offering a location, so the same frame is transferred from shops to jurisdictions.
senses.whyCN: 这种读法中的「卖者」是提供落户地的政府，于是同一框架从店铺转移到了辖区。

senses.title: A selection mechanism that weeds out firms
senses.titleCN: 淘汰落后者的一种选择机制
senses.definition: the process by which inefficient sellers lose customers and exit while efficient ones expand
senses.definitionCN: 低效卖者失去顾客并退出、高效卖者扩张的过程
senses.example: Market competition drove three of the seven mills out of business within four years.
senses.exampleCN: 市场竞争使七家磨坊中的三家在四年内停业。
senses.why: rivalry does not merely set prices, it also decides who survives, so the phrase can name a sorting process rather than a state.
senses.whyCN: 角逐不仅定出价格，也决定谁存活，因此这个短语可指名一个筛选过程，而非一种状态。

senses.title: Contention inside a segment or platform
senses.titleCN: 细分市场或平台内部的争夺
senses.definition: rivalry confined to one product segment, or played out between platforms that host other sellers
senses.definitionCN: 局限于某一产品细分的争夺，或在承载其他卖者的平台之间展开的争夺
senses.example: Market competition among delivery apps now turns on who controls the rider network.
senses.exampleCN: 配送应用之间的市场竞争，如今取决于谁掌握骑手网络。
senses.why: the phrase scales down to a niche and up to a platform layer, because the contending parties can be any sellers sharing one pool of demand.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既可缩小到一个细分位，也可放大到一个平台层，因为相互角逐的可以是共享同一需求池的任何卖者。

intro.en: Market competition pairs a Latin trade noun with a Latin noun of striving. Market goes back to mercatus 'a place of trading'; competition goes back to competere, literally 'to seek together', built from com- 'together' and petere 'to seek, to head for'.
intro.cn: market competition 把一个拉丁的交易名词与一个拉丁的「力争」名词配在一起。market 上溯 mercatus「交易场所」；competition 上溯 competere，字面是「共同追求」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 petere「寻求、奔向」构成。

items.en: Petere meant 'to seek, to make for, to attack'. It is generally thought to come from a root for rushing at something, but the older form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、奔向、攻击」。一般认为它出自表示「扑向某物」的词根，但更早的形式是重构形式，而非有记录的词。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus petere produced competere, whose first sense was 'to meet, to come together, to coincide'. Only in later Latin did it take on 'to strive after the same thing, to contend'.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加 petere 构成 competere，其本义是「相遇、会合、恰好一致」。到较晚的拉丁语中，它才带上「争夺同一物、相争」的意思。

items.en: The noun competitio named the act of seeking something together, and in legal and later usage it named a claim laid by several parties to one thing, hence a dispute.
items.cn: 名词 competitio 指「共同追求某物」的行为，在法律及后世用法中指多方对同一物提出主张，因而带上争执之意。

items.en: Competition reached English through Old French in the sixteenth century, bringing the sense of rivalry between persons or traders rather than the older sense of coincidence.
items.cn: competition 于十六世纪经古法语进入英语，带来的是人与人、商人与商人之间的角逐义，而非较早的「恰好一致」义。

items.en: The full phrase became standard with industrial organization and competition policy in the twentieth century, when rivalry among sellers was named, measured and regulated as a distinct object.
items.cn: 完整短语在二十世纪的产业组织理论与竞争政策中成为标准说法，卖者之间的角逐从此被命名、测量并作为独立对象加以规范。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single citation fixes the moment when the Latin verb shifted from 'meet' to 'contend', and the pre-Latin root of petere is unsettled, so the boundary dates given here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定：没有单一书证能确定这个拉丁动词由「相遇」转为「相争」的时刻，petere 在拉丁语之前的词根亦无定论，此处给出的分界年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin striving root but names a capacity, a person or a quality instead of the contest itself; group two names neighbouring ideas in the same contest, each with a narrower reach.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁「力争」词根，但指能力、人物或性质，而非角逐本身；第二组指同一场角逐中的邻近概念，各自范围更窄。

entries.definition: The ability of a firm or country to hold its own against rivals; it is the strength brought to the contest, not the contest itself.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或国家与对手抗衡的能力；它是带入角逐的实力，而非角逐本身。

entries.definition: One of the parties doing the contending; it names a participant, whereas the target names the relation between participants.
entries.definitionCN: 参与角逐的其中一方；它指参与者，而目标短语指参与者之间的关系。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a market or a price that can win business; the target is the noun for the process the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 描述市场或价格足以赢得生意的形容词；目标短语则是该形容词所指过程的名称。

entries.definition: A continuing state of striving between two parties; it stresses duration and personal antagonism, which a market phrase does not.
entries.definitionCN: 两方持续力争的状态；强调持续性与人对人的敌意，市场短语不含这两层。

entries.definition: A contest fought only by repeated price cuts; it is a single episode inside the target, not the whole relation.
entries.definitionCN: 只靠反复降价进行的争夺；它是目标状态中的一段插曲，而非整段关系。

entries.definition: The ease with which a newcomer could enter and displace an incumbent; it measures a threat behind the contest rather than the contest.
entries.definitionCN: 新来者进入并取代在位者的容易程度；它衡量角逐背后的威胁，而非角逐本身。

entries.definition: The body of law that protects rivalry; it is the policy instrument aimed at the target, not the target.
entries.definitionCN: 保护角逐的法律体系；它是指向目标状态的政策工具，而非目标状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb 'to seek together', real relatives and real phrases from competition policy.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词「共同追求」、真实同族词，以及竞争政策中的真实说法。

normal.en: Competition rests on competere, com- 'together' plus petere 'to seek': two parties seeking one thing is already the whole picture.
normal.cn: competition 基于 competere，即表示「共同」的前缀加 petere「寻求」：两方共追一物，画面已然完整。

normal.en: The old sense was 'to meet or coincide', which is why the same root also gives competent, a word about fitting the case.
normal.cn: 旧义是「相遇、相合」，同一词根因此也给出 competent，一个表示「合于其事」的词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the intensity: intense market competition, fair market competition, shielded from market competition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出强度：激烈的市场竞争、公平的市场竞争、受保护而免受市场竞争。

normal.en: Policy vocabulary travels with the phrase: competition policy, antitrust enforcement, a merger review.
normal.cn: 政策词汇与这个短语同行：竞争政策、反垄断执法、合并审查。

normal.en: The phrase is also a benchmark, so textbooks set it beside monopoly and oligopoly on the same scale.
normal.cn: 这个短语同时是一个基准，因此教科书把它与垄断、寡头放在同一标尺上。

abstract.en: Picture several shopkeepers on one street all watching the same passer-by and stepping forward at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上几个店主盯着同一位过路人，并在同一刻一起迎上前去。

abstract.en: Picture a price board rewritten every morning by each shop, then compared with the board across the road.
abstract.cn: 想象每家铺子每天早上重写价牌，然后与对街那家的价牌相比。

abstract.en: Picture a race in which the finish line is the customer's hand reaching for one counter out of several.
abstract.cn: 想象一场赛跑，终点线是顾客的手在几个柜台之间伸向其中一个。

examples.en: Intense market competition has cut the average price of a solar panel by more than half in a decade.
examples.cn: 激烈的市场竞争使太阳能板均价在十年间下降了一半以上。

examples.en: The regulator blocked the merger on the ground that it would remove market competition in two regional routes.
examples.cn: 监管机构阻止该合并，理由是它将消除两条区域航线上的市场竞争。

examples.en: Where a service is shielded from market competition, providers tend to answer to budgets rather than to users.
examples.cn: 当某项服务免受市场竞争时，提供者往往对预算负责，而非对使用者负责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「market（市场）+ competition（比赛）」——把集市当成一场比赛：几家铺子同抢一批客人，谁价低、谁货好，谁就得分。

root: 拉丁 mercatus「市场、交易」← mercari「做买卖」← merx（属格 mercis）「货物」；拉丁 competere「共同追求」= 表示「共同」的前缀 + petere「寻求、扑向」，晚期拉丁转为「相争」，名词 competitio 经古法语 competition 入英语；短语为二十世纪产业组织与竞争政策术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold from one Latin verb meaning to seek the same thing together: first many sellers chase one crowd, then they chase it by price, then by quality, then the chase is idealized into a benchmark, protected by law, transferred to cities, read as a weeding-out process and finally confined to a segment or a platform.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个意为「共同追求同一物」的拉丁动词展开：先是多个卖者追同一群人，继而以价格追、以品质追，随后这场追逐被理想化为基准、被法律保护、被移用到城市之间、被读成淘汰过程，最后被限定在某个细分或某个平台之内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several shops on one street stepping forward at the same moment toward the same customer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上几家铺子在同一刻朝同一位顾客迎上前去。

branches.en: THE BASE AND THE FIRST LEVER: many sellers share one pool of buyers, and the quickest way to pull them over is the price board.
branches.cn: 基本局面与第一根杠杆：多个卖者共享一个买主池，而把人拉过来最快的办法是价牌。

branches.en: THE SECOND LEVER AND THE LIMIT: with price fixed, rivalry moves to quality, and pushed to its limit it becomes the theorist's benchmark.
branches.cn: 第二根杠杆与极值：价格被固定时，角逐转向品质；把它推到极值，便成了理论家的基准。

branches.en: GUARDED AND RELOCATED: the law treats the contest as a thing to protect, and the same frame is then moved from shops to cities.
branches.cn: 被守护与被移用：法律把这场角逐当作需要保护之物，同一框架随后从店铺移到了城市。

branches.en: THE SORTING: beyond prices, the contest decides which sellers stay and which close their doors.
branches.cn: 筛选：除定出价格之外，角逐还决定哪些卖者留下、哪些关门。

branches.en: THE NARROW ARENA: the same chase can be scaled down to one niche or up to a platform that hosts the sellers.
branches.cn: 更窄的场地：同一场追逐可缩小到一个细分位，也可放大到承载卖者的平台。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two nouns, and its second half is itself a Latin verb plus a prefix and a noun suffix, so the whole can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词合成，后半部分本身又是一个拉丁动词加上前缀与名词后缀，因此整体可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- and petere build competere, competitio and the English family compete, competitor, competitive; mercatus supplies market and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀与 petere 构成 competere、competitio，以及英语词族 compete、competitor、competitive；mercatus 提供 market 与 merchant。

items.example: The prefix marks two parties acting on one object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记两方作用于同一对象。

items.structure: Latin verb, third conjugation, 'to seek, head for'
items.meaning: to seek, to make for, to attack
items.example: The verb supplies the striving at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供这个词核心处的「力争」。

items.meaning: to seek together, then to contend
items.example: Competere first meant to meet, and later to strive against.
items.exampleCN: competere 最初意为相遇，后来意为相争。

items.structure: Latin suffix forming a noun of action
items.meaning: the act or process of doing
items.example: Competere plus the suffix yields the noun of striving.
items.exampleCN: competere 加这个后缀构成表示「力争」的名词。

items.example: Competition entered English with the sense of rivalry.
items.exampleCN: competition 带着「角逐」之义进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 有胜出倾向的；竞争性的
items.example: A competitive price is one that can take business from a rival.
items.exampleCN: 有竞争力的价格是能从对手那里抢走生意的价格。

items.example: Each competitor watches the others' moves.
items.exampleCN: 每个竞争者都盯着其他人的动作。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to contend
items.meaningCN: 能够角逐的性质；竞争力
items.example: The index ranks countries by competitiveness.
items.exampleCN: 该指数按竞争力给各国排名。

items.example: An uncompetitive price loses the contract.
items.exampleCN: 无竞争力的价格会丢掉合同。

items.meaning: a place of trade, and demand itself
items.meaningCN: 交易场所，也指需求本身
items.example: Market supplies the arena in which the contending happens.
items.exampleCN: market 提供角逐发生的场所。

definition_zh: 减少；削减；降低；还原；（数学）约简；（烹饪）收汁
definition_en: the act of making something smaller or simpler, or the amount by which it is made smaller
core_image: 一块厚布被两边慢慢拉紧，最后缩成一小片
scene: 家里换了新锅炉之后，暖气费账单明显薄了一截。 The new boiler led to a twenty percent reduction in fuel use.
sceneCN: 这里 reduction 指「用量下降的幅度」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度变小）；句意：新锅炉使燃料用量减少了百分之二十。图中可辨识物件：旧锅炉、新锅炉、下降箭头、用量表。

pos.zh: 减少；削减；降低；（化学）还原；（数学）约简；（烹饪）收汁
