senses.title: A decrease in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量减少：总量或程度变小
senses.definition: the act or result of making an amount, rate or level smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使数量、比率或水平变小的动作或结果
senses.example: The new boiler led to a twenty percent reduction in fuel use.
senses.exampleCN: 新锅炉使燃料用量减少了百分之二十。
senses.why: Reduction comes from Latin reducere 'to lead back'; the modern 'make smaller' sense grew from leading something down to a lower level.
senses.whyCN: reduction 出自拉丁 reducere「带回」；现代「使变小」义由「把某物带到更低水平」发展而来。

senses.title: A price cut
senses.definition: a lowering of price, often offered as a discount
senses.definitionCN: 价格的调低，常作为折扣给出
senses.example: The store advertised a fifty-dollar reduction on the jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 商店宣传这件夹克降价五十美元。
senses.why: Commerce applies the physical image of lowering to money: the price is brought down, and the amount is called a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 商业把「降低」的物理意象用于金钱：价格被带下来，降下的数额就叫 reduction。

senses.title: Chemical reduction
senses.titleCN: 化学还原：物质得到电子
senses.definition: in chemistry, the process in which a substance gains electrons and its oxidation state falls
senses.definitionCN: 化学中物质获得电子、氧化态降低的过程
senses.example: Iron ore is turned into metal by chemical reduction in a furnace.
senses.exampleCN: 铁矿石在炉中经化学还原变成金属。
senses.why: Chemists kept the 'lowering' idea: the oxidation number is brought down as electrons are added, so the reaction is a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 化学家保留了「降低」的观念：加入电子后氧化数被带低，因此该反应称为还原。

senses.title: Mathematical simplification
senses.titleCN: 数学约简：把式子化到更简形式
senses.definition: in mathematics, the rewriting of an expression or problem into a simpler equivalent form
senses.definitionCN: 数学中把表达式或问题改写为更简单的等价形式
senses.example: Reduction of the fraction 18/24 gives 3/4.
senses.exampleCN: 把分数 18/24 约简得到 3/4。
senses.why: The 'lead back' sense survives here: a complex expression is led back to its simplest equivalent.
senses.whyCN: 「带回」义在此留存：复杂表达式被带回其最简单的等价形式。

senses.title: Cooking down a sauce
senses.titleCN: 烹煮收汁：水分蒸发使汤汁变浓
senses.definition: in cooking, the evaporation of liquid so that a sauce becomes thicker and more concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 烹饪中液体蒸发、使酱汁变稠变浓的过程
senses.example: A slow reduction concentrates the flavour of the stock.
senses.exampleCN: 慢火收汁使高汤的味道更浓缩。
senses.why: The kitchen borrows the volume sense literally: the liquid is reduced in quantity while the flavour remains.
senses.whyCN: 厨房直接借用了体积义：液体数量变少，而风味保留。

senses.title: Lowering in rank
senses.titleCN: 降级：职位或地位被调低
senses.definition: the act of moving someone to a lower rank, position or status
senses.definitionCN: 把某人调到更低职级、职位或地位的行为
senses.example: His reduction from captain to private was announced at roll call.
senses.exampleCN: 点名列队时宣布他从上尉降为列兵。
senses.why: This sense is the oldest direction of ducere: a person is led back down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项最贴近 ducere 的原始方向：人被沿着等级序列带回下方。

senses.title: Data reduction
senses.titleCN: 数据简化：把原始数据压缩成可用摘要
senses.definition: the process of summarizing or simplifying large sets of raw data into usable measures
senses.definitionCN: 把大量原始数据汇总或简化为可用指标的过程
senses.example: Data reduction turned thousands of sensor readings into one daily average.
senses.exampleCN: 数据简化把数千条传感器读数变成一个日均值。
senses.why: The word is applied to information rather than matter: detail is brought down to a manageable summary.
senses.whyCN: 该词被用于信息而非物质：细节被压到可处理的摘要层级。

senses.title: Reductio ad absurdum
senses.titleCN: 归谬：把命题推到荒谬以反驳它
senses.definition: in logic, the method of disproving a claim by showing that its consequences are absurd
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中通过显示某主张的推论荒谬来反驳它的方法
senses.example: The proof proceeds by reduction to absurdity.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明通过归谬法推进。
senses.why: The Latin phrase reductio ad absurdum means 'a leading back to the absurd': the argument leads the claim back to a contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语 reductio ad absurdum 意为「带回到荒谬」：论证把该主张带回矛盾之处。

intro.en: Reduction comes from Latin reductio, the noun of action from reducere 'to lead back'. The English word first meant a bringing back, and later narrowed toward 'making smaller'.
intro.cn: reduction 出自拉丁 reductio，即 reducere「带回」的动作名词。英语词最初意为「带回」，后来收窄为「使变小」。

items.en: Latin ducere meant 'to lead, draw, conduct'. Its family includes conduct, produce, induce, introduce and reduce.
items.cn: 拉丁 ducere 意为「引导、拉、带领」，其词族包括 conduct、produce、induce、introduce、reduce。

items.en: Reducere joined re- 'back' to ducere, meaning 'to lead back, bring back'. It could be used for troops, for a price, or for a written argument.
items.cn: reducere 把 re-「回」加到 ducere，意为「带回、领回」，可用于军队、价格或书面论证。

items.en: The Latin action noun reductio named the act of leading back. In logic, reductio ad absurdum named a proof that leads a claim back to contradiction.
items.cn: 拉丁动作名词 reductio 指「带回」的行为。逻辑中的 reductio ad absurdum 指把主张带回到矛盾的证明。

items.en: English reduction entered in the sixteenth century, first as a bringing back or restoration, then as a lowering or diminishing.
items.cn: 英语 reduction 于 16 世纪进入，最初指带回或恢复，后指降低或减少。

items.en: Chemistry, mathematics, cooking and data processing each fixed a specialized sense of the lowering or simplifying action.
items.cn: 化学、数学、烹饪与数据处理各自固定了「降低」或「简化」动作的专门义项。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of Latin ducere is generally discussed only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；拉丁 ducere 的更深来源通常只能作为重构来讨论。

note.en: The first group separates the reduce family from near-looking forms; the second gives near-synonyms that stress amount, cut or simplification.
note.cn: 第一组区分 reduce 词族与形近形式；第二组给出强调数量、削减或简化的近义词。

entries.definition: To make smaller or simpler; reduction is the act or the resulting amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变小或变简单；reduction 是动作或由此得到的量。

entries.definition: Describing something that simplifies, often with disapproval. It is not the noun for a cut.
entries.definitionCN: 形容简化的，常带贬义；不是表示「削减量」的名词。

entries.definition: The theory that complex things can be explained by simpler parts. It is not a decrease in quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 指复杂事物可由更简单部分解释的理论，并非数量减少。

entries.definition: Logical inference from general to specific, from Latin deducere 'lead away'. The prefix changes the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一般到具体的逻辑推理，出自拉丁 deducere「带走」；前缀改变了方向。

entries.definition: A general fall in amount. Reduction often implies a deliberate act by someone.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指数量下降；reduction 常暗示有人有意采取行动。

entries.definition: An often sudden or politically decided lowering, especially of budgets or staff. It is more informal than reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 常指突然或政治上决定的削减，尤指预算或人员，比 reduction 更口语。

entries.definition: A gradual worsening or falling off. It usually happens over time rather than by a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐恶化或下降，通常随时间发生，而非由单一行动造成。

entries.definition: The act of making something easier to understand. It stresses clarity, not size.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物更易理解，强调清晰而非规模。

entries.definition: A specific lowering of price. It overlaps sense 2 but names the commercial offer, not the general act.
entries.definitionCN: 特指价格下调，与第 2 个义项重叠，但命名的是商业优惠而非一般行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + ducere 'lead' + -tion: leading something back down.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ ducere「引导」+ -tion：把某物带回低处。

normal.en: The family runs reduce, reductive, reducer, reductionism, irreducible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reduce、reductive、reducer、reductionism、irreducible。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: cost reduction, emission reduction, data reduction, reduction to absurdity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：成本削减、减排、数据简化、归谬法。

normal.en: Chemistry says reduction when electrons are gained and the oxidation number falls.
normal.cn: 化学中，得到电子、氧化数下降就叫还原。

normal.en: deduction leads away; reduction leads back. The prefix decides the direction.
normal.cn: deduction 带走，reduction 带回；前缀决定方向。

abstract.en: Picture a thick cloth pulled tight from both sides until it shrinks to a small patch.
abstract.cn: 想象一块厚布被两边拉紧，最后缩成一小片。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of papers whittled down to a single summary card.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞文件被削成一张摘要卡。

abstract.en: Picture a sauce simmering until the surface drops and the colour deepens.
abstract.cn: 想象酱汁慢煮到液面下降、颜色加深。

examples.en: The policy aims at a thirty percent reduction in plastic waste by 2030.
examples.cn: 该政策目标是到 2030 年将塑料废物减少三成。

examples.en: Reduction of the oxide with carbon yields iron and carbon dioxide.
examples.cn: 用碳还原氧化物会生成铁和二氧化碳。

examples.en: After data reduction, the team kept only the four most stable variables.
examples.cn: 经过数据简化，团队只保留四个最稳定的变量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ duct（引导）」——把数量往回带 → reduction 减少、削减

root: 拉丁 ducere「引导」→ reducere「带回、领回」→ reductio「带回」；英语 reduction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower something: an amount, a price, an oxidation state, an expression, a sauce, a rank, a data set, or a claim driven back into contradiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在「把某物带低」：数量、价格、氧化态、表达式、酱汁、职级、数据集，或被带回矛盾的命题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick cloth drawn tight until it shrinks to a patch.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚布被拉紧，缩成一小片。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND PRICE: something is brought down, whether a quantity or a tag.
branches.cn: 数量与价格：被带低的东西，或是一个量，或是一个标价。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: electrons are added and the oxidation number falls.
branches.cn: 化学：加入电子，氧化数下降。

branches.en: SIMPLIFICATION: expressions and raw data are led back to manageable forms.
branches.cn: 简化：表达式与原始数据被带回可处理的形式。

branches.en: KITCHEN: liquid volume falls while flavour concentrates.
branches.cn: 厨房：液体体积下降，风味浓缩。

branches.en: RANK AND LOGIC: a person is led down the hierarchy, or a claim is led back to absurdity.
branches.cn: 职级与逻辑：人沿等级被带下，或主张被带回到荒谬。

intro.en: Reduction is a Latin action noun in -tio laid onto the verb reducere, which joins 'back' to 'lead'. English keeps both the physical and the figurative directions.
intro.cn: reduction 是加在动词 reducere 上的拉丁 -tio 动作名词，该动词把「回」与「引导」结合。英语同时保留其物理与比喻方向。

latinIntro.en: The ducere family is large: conduct, produce, induce, introduce, deduce, reduce, educate and seduce all contain the 'lead' root, but each prefix sets a different direction.
latinIntro.cn: ducere 词族庞大：conduct、produce、induce、introduce、deduce、reduce、educate、seduce 都含「引导」词根，但各前缀设定不同方向。

items.example: The reduction in hours improved safety.
items.exampleCN: 工时减少改善了安全状况。

items.meaning: to bring down or make smaller
items.example: The factory reduced water use by half.
items.exampleCN: 工厂把用水量减少了一半。

items.example: The review called the argument reductive.
items.exampleCN: 评论称该论证过于化约。

items.meaning: a device or substance that lowers something
items.meaningCN: 使某物降低的装置或物质
items.example: A pressure reducer sits before the valve.
items.exampleCN: 阀门前装有一个减压器。

items.meaning: cannot be made simpler or smaller
items.meaningCN: 不能进一步简化或缩小的
items.example: The problem is irreducible to one cause.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题无法化约为单一原因。

items.example: The deduction follows from the two premises.
items.exampleCN: 该推论由两个前提推出。

items.meaning: to lead into; to bring about
items.example: Warmth induces the seeds to sprout.
items.exampleCN: 温度促使种子发芽。

items.example: Copper conducts heat well.
items.exampleCN: 铜导热良好。

definition_zh: 由……组成；由……构成；由（材料）制成；由（人员）组成；含有（化学成分）；由（地层）构成；由（部分）构成；由（词汇、物种）构成
definition_en: to consist of particular materials, parts, members or elements that together make up the whole
core_image: 一只陶罐被轻轻敲开，断口露出三层颜色不同的泥料，每一层都能单独叫出名字
scene: 修复师把碎陶片按颜色和颗粒分成几堆，摆在白纸上，再一层层拼回罐身，最后指出它由三种泥料烧成。 The ancient jar can be composed of three distinct clay layers.
sceneCN: 修复师在案上拼合陶片（第 1 个义项：由材料组成）；句意为这只古罐可能由三层不同的泥料构成。图中可辨识物件：陶片、白纸、放大镜、颜色标签。

pos.zh: 由……组成；由……构成；由（若干部分）组成

collocations.phrase: be composed of carbon and hydrogen
be composed of stone and timber

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「componere」经法语「composer」而来，义为「组成；创作」
加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「构成；作品；作文」
加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「作曲家」
由同一拉丁词干而来，义为「组成部分；部件」
由同一拉丁分词而来，义为「复合的；复合材料」

senses.title: Made of materials
senses.definition: to be made from particular materials that are mixed or combined
senses.definitionCN: 由若干被混合或结合起来的特定材料制成
senses.example: The mortar can be composed of sand, lime and water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种砂浆可以由砂、石灰与水组成。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to place things together, so the phrase begins with material laid beside material.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为把东西放在一起，因此该短语从材料与材料并排摆放开始。

senses.title: Parts forming a whole
senses.definition: to consist of separate parts that together make one complete structure
senses.definitionCN: 由若干分开的部分组成，这些部分合起来构成一个完整结构
senses.example: The roof can be composed of six prefabricated panels.
senses.exampleCN: 这个屋顶可以由六块预制板构成。
senses.why: Placing parts together is the literal picture, and the finished structure is the result of that placement.
senses.whyCN: 把部件放在一起就是字面画面，而完成的结构正是这种摆放的结果。

senses.title: People forming a body
senses.titleCN: 人员组成团队或委员会
senses.definition: to consist of named members who together form a team, board or committee
senses.definitionCN: 由指明的成员组成，他们合起来构成团队、董事会或委员会
senses.example: The review board can be composed of five independent experts.
senses.exampleCN: 评审委员会可以由五位独立专家组成。
senses.why: A committee is a whole assembled from people, so the same verb that builds objects also builds bodies.
senses.whyCN: 委员会是由人装配成的整体，因此造物的动词也用来造组织。

senses.title: Chemical composition
senses.definition: to consist of chemical elements or compounds in fixed proportions
senses.definitionCN: 由按一定比例存在的化学元素或化合物构成
senses.example: The mineral can be composed of calcium carbonate and traces of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物可以由碳酸钙与微量铁构成。
senses.why: Chemistry lists ingredients the way a recipe does, and the phrase names that list.
senses.whyCN: 化学像食谱一样列出成分，这个短语指的就是这份清单。

senses.title: Layered rock or strata
senses.definition: to consist of beds or layers stacked in a definite order
senses.definitionCN: 由按确定次序叠置的层或岩层构成
senses.example: The cliff face can be composed of alternating shale and sandstone beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这处崖面可以由页岩与砂岩层交替构成。
senses.why: Geology reads a cliff as a stack of placed layers, which is the Latin verb taken literally.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把崖壁读成一叠摆放好的层，这正是那个拉丁动词的字面用法。

senses.title: Structure of a work
senses.definition: to consist of sections or movements arranged into a larger artistic whole
senses.definitionCN: 由若干段落或乐章排列成一个更大的艺术整体
senses.example: The symphony can be composed of four contrasting movements.
senses.exampleCN: 这部交响曲可以由四个对比鲜明的乐章构成。
senses.why: To compose music and to compose a whole use the same arranging gesture, so structure and creation share the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 谱写音乐与组合整体使用同一个排列动作，因此结构与创作共用这个短语。

senses.title: Words forming a corpus
senses.definition: to consist of texts or words collected into a body of language data
senses.definitionCN: 由收集起来构成语言数据总体的文本或词语组成
senses.example: The learner corpus can be composed of essays written by secondary students.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学习者语料库可以由中学生撰写的文章构成。
senses.why: A corpus is a body built from many texts, and the phrase treats each text as a placed piece.
senses.whyCN: 语料库是由许多文本建成的整体，这个短语把每篇文本当作摆放进去的一块。

senses.title: Members of an ecological community
senses.definition: to consist of species or populations that together form a community
senses.definitionCN: 由若干物种或种群组成，它们合起来构成一个群落
senses.example: The reef community can be composed of corals, algae and grazing fish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个珊瑚礁群落可以由珊瑚、藻类与食草鱼类组成。
senses.why: An ecosystem is an assembly of living parts, so the phrase extends the placed-together image to species.
senses.whyCN: 生态系统是活体部件的装配，于是该短语把「放在一起」的画面扩展到物种。

intro.en: Compose comes from Latin componere, to put together, from com-, together, and ponere, to place. Its past participle compositus passed through French composer into English, and the passive frame be composed of was added later.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「componere」「组合」，由「com-」「一起」与「ponere」「放置」构成。其过去分词「compositus」经法语「composer」进入英语，后来再加上被动框架「be composed of」。

items.en: Ponere meant to place, put or set something down, and it supplied the core of the verb.
items.cn: 「ponere」意为放置、放下或安置，是该动词的核心。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together or with, and it took the form com- before a p.
items.cn: 前缀「com-」意为一起或共同，在「p」之前取「com-」这一形式。

items.en: Putting com- before ponere produced componere, to place things together and so to arrange or compose.
items.cn: 把「com-」放在「ponere」前得到「componere」，意为把东西放在一起，进而指排列或组合。

items.en: The past participle compositus meant put together or arranged, and English took that shape for the adjective composed.
items.cn: 过去分词「compositus」意为已组合的、已排列的，英语的形容词「composed」就取了这个形状。

items.en: The verb passed through French composer, which still meant to put together and also to produce a work.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语「composer」传入，仍指把东西放在一起，也指创作作品。

items.en: English compose covers making up a whole, writing a text and writing music, all from the same placing-together image.
items.cn: 英语「compose」既指构成整体，也指写作与作曲，都来自同一个「放在一起」的画面。

note.en: The first group looks like compose and shares its root; the second group contrasts three ways of linking things: composed of names the parts that make a whole, characterized by names the mark that identifies it, and associated with reports only a statistical or accompanying link.
note.cn: 第一组与「compose」形近且同源；第二组对照三种连接方式：「composed of」指出构成整体的各个部分，「characterized by」指出识别事物的标志，「associated with」只表示统计或伴随的联系。

entries.definition: To make up a whole, to arrange parts, or to write a text or a piece of music.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成整体、排列部分，或写作、作曲。

entries.definition: The act of putting parts together, the resulting structure, or a written work.
entries.definitionCN: 指把部分组合起来的行为、由此形成的结构，或一篇作品。

entries.definition: A person who writes music, one who arranges parts into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指创作音乐的人，即把部分排列成整体的人。

entries.definition: One of the parts that together make up a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指合起来构成更大整体的部件之一。

entries.definition: Made of separate parts combined into one, or such a combined material.
entries.definitionCN: 指由分开的部分合成一体的，也指这样的合成材料。

entries.definition: To be made up of parts; it comes from a different Latin verb meaning to stand, so it is not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 指由部分组成；它来自另一个意为「站立」的拉丁动词，并非同一词源。

entries.definition: To include or be made up of; it comes from a Latin verb meaning to grasp together, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 指包含或由……构成；它来自一个意为「抓在一起」的拉丁动词，词源不同。

entries.definition: To be formed from parts, the plain everyday version of the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指由部分组成，是同一意思的日常平实说法。

entries.definition: To be linked to something, often statistically; it does not say what the thing is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某事物相联系，常是统计上的；它并不说明事物由什么构成。

entries.definition: To have a defining mark; it names an identifying feature, not the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有定义性标志；它说明识别特征，而非组成部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal placing-together picture and the many wholes the phrase can inventory.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用字面上「放在一起」的画面，以及该短语能清点出的各种整体。

normal.en: Com- means together and ponere means to place, so compose is literally to place together.
normal.cn: 「com-」意为一起，「ponere」意为放置，因此「compose」字面上就是把东西放在一起。

normal.en: Composition, composer, component and composite all keep the same placed-together picture.
normal.cn: 「composition」「composer」「component」「composite」都保留着同一个「放在一起」的画面。

normal.en: A committee is composed of members, a cake is composed of layers, and a poem is composed of lines.
normal.cn: 委员会由成员组成，蛋糕由层组成，诗由行组成。

normal.en: Be composed of names the parts; it does not name the mark that identifies them.
normal.cn: 「be composed of」点出部分，并不点出识别这些部分的标志。

normal.en: Consist of and comprise are close in meaning but come from different Latin verbs.
normal.cn: 「consist of」与「comprise」意思接近，却来自不同的拉丁动词。

abstract.en: A whole is a promise that its parts can be listed, and the phrase keeps that promise.
abstract.cn: 整体是一种承诺，承诺它的部分可以被列出来，而这个短语兑现了这份承诺。

abstract.en: The same word builds a jar from clay, a board from people and a reef from species.
abstract.cn: 同一个词用陶土造罐、用人组成委员会、用物种组成珊瑚礁。

abstract.en: Composition is neither a feature nor a statistical link; it is the inventory of what is inside.
abstract.cn: 构成既不是特征，也不是统计联系；它是内部东西的清单。

examples.en: The wall can be composed of local stone and lime mortar.
examples.cn: 这面墙可以由本地石料与石灰砂浆构成。

examples.en: The committee can be composed of teachers, parents and doctors.
examples.cn: 这个委员会可以由教师、家长与医生组成。

examples.en: The atmosphere can be composed of several layers with different temperatures.
examples.cn: 大气可以由若干温度不同的层构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 康剖兹德 欧夫」——把几块料放进一只罐里，再数清里面有几样：由……组成

root: 拉丁语「com-」「一起」加「ponere」「放置」构成「componere」「组合」，过去分词「compositus」，经法语「composer」进入英语，再加被动框架「be composed of」。要注意：它与「comprise」（来自「comprehendere」「抓在一起」）和「consist」（来自「sistere」「站立」）形近而来源不同，不可混为一谈。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same inventory: material, parts, members, elements, layers, movements, texts and species are all counted as what the whole contains.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项遵循同一份清单：材料、部件、成员、元素、岩层、乐章、文本与物种都被算作整体所含的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jar is broken open and three coloured clay layers are counted one by one inside the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶罐被敲开，罐壁里三层颜色不同的泥料被一层层数出来。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL MIX: clay, sand or chemical elements named as what the thing contains.
branches.cn: 材料配比：陶土、砂石或化学元素，用来说明事物含有什么。

branches.en: THE LAYERED WHOLE: prefabricated panels or rock beds stacked into a structure.
branches.cn: 层叠整体：预制板或岩层叠合成一个结构。

branches.en: THE MEMBER BODY: a board of people or a community of species that fills the whole.
branches.cn: 成员整体：由人组成的委员会，或由物种组成的群落。

branches.en: THE BUILT WORK: movements of a symphony arranged into a larger composition.
branches.cn: 构建的作品：交响曲的乐章排列成更大的作品。

branches.en: THE WORD INVENTORY: a corpus filled by essays from many writers.
branches.cn: 词汇清单：由众多作者的文章填充起来的语料库。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin verb of placing, fitted with an English passive frame; its parts are com-, ponere and the participle ending.
intro.cn: 这个短语是一个表示「放置」的拉丁动词，装上英语被动框架；其构件是「com-」「ponere」与分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ponere, com- and componere with its participle compositus; French passes the verb on, and English adds compose and its family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「ponere」「com-」与「componere」及其分词「compositus」；法语把动词传下来，英语再加上「compose」及其同族词。

items.example: The verb names the act of laying something in position.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把某物放在某一位置的动作。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of several things meeting.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上若干事物会合的意思。

items.structure: Latin verb from com- and ponere
items.example: The verb places parts side by side into one thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把部件并排摆成一个东西。

items.example: The participle describes the finished whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述已完成组合的整体。

items.example: The English verb covers both structure and creation.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语动词既指结构，也指创作。

items.meaning: the way parts are put together
items.example: The noun names the arrangement and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指排列方式及其结果。

items.example: The ending names the person who arranges the parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指排列部件的人。

items.structure: English noun from the same stem
items.meaning: a part of a larger whole
items.example: Each component can be named separately.
items.exampleCN: 每个部件都能单独命名。

items.example: The word describes a whole built from separate pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述由分开的块件建成的整体。

items.example: It names a substance made by combining others.
items.exampleCN: 它指由其他物质结合而成的物质。

definition_en: relating to or produced by a volcano, or, of a mood or situation, ready to explode like one
core_image: 一座锥形山体顶端喷出灰柱，黑色熔岩顺坡流下，冷却成坚硬的石
scene: 海边的小村旁，黑色砂粒在浪里翻滚，孩子弯腰捧起一把，掌心留下细小的黑色颗粒。 The black sand under our feet is volcanic, worn from old lava by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 volcanic 是形容词「由火山物质形成的」（第 2 个义项：火山岩、火山灰等喷出物构成的）；句意为脚下的黑沙是火山物质，由古老熔岩被海水磨碎而成。

pos.zh: 火山的；火山造成的；火山岩的；火山土的；（比喻）一触即发的

senses.title: Relating to a volcano
senses.definition: relating to a volcano or to the fire, ash and rock it produces
senses.definitionCN: 与火山或与其产生的火、灰、岩石有关的
senses.example: The island's volcanic peaks rise straight from the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛上的火山峰从海面直直升起。
senses.why: the adjective simply marks belonging: volcanic scenery, volcanic origin, volcanic island all attach the noun to the fire mountain.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只标记归属：火山地貌、火山成因、火山岛，都是把名词挂到那座火之山上。

senses.title: Rock and ash from a volcano
senses.definition: made of or consisting of material thrown out by a volcano, such as lava, ash or pumice
senses.definitionCN: 由火山喷出的物质（如熔岩、火山灰或浮石）构成或组成的
senses.example: Layers of volcanic ash lie between the coal seams.
senses.exampleCN: 煤层之间夹着层层火山灰。
senses.why: geology uses the adjective for the material itself, so a rock can be called volcanic without naming a particular mountain.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个形容词指材料本身，因此一块岩石可以被称为火山的，而不必指明某座具体的山。

senses.title: Volcanic activity or eruption
senses.definition: caused by or showing the action of a volcano, including eruptions, tremors and gas release
senses.definitionCN: 由火山作用引起或表现出的，包括喷发、颤动与气体释放
senses.example: Volcanic activity increased sharply before the evacuation.
senses.exampleCN: 撤离之前，火山活动急剧增加。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the place to the process, naming an event rather than a mountain or a stone.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「地点」转到「过程」，指事件而非山体或石头。

senses.title: Fertile volcanic soil
senses.definition: describing soil formed from weathered volcanic material, which is often rich in minerals and very productive
senses.definitionCN: 描述由风化火山物质形成的土壤，常富含矿物质且十分肥沃
senses.example: Farmers prize the deep volcanic soil for its minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 农民看重深厚的火山土，因为它富含矿物质。
senses.why: the destructive mountain leaves a gift behind, and the adjective carries that unlikely pairing of fire and fertility.
senses.whyCN: 毁灭性的山体留下了一份礼物，这个形容词就承载着「火与肥沃」这种出人意料的组合。

senses.title: Volcanic glass
senses.definition: a natural glass formed when lava cools too quickly to crystallize, as in obsidian
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩冷却过快、来不及结晶时形成的天然玻璃，如黑曜岩
senses.example: Volcanic glass forms when lava cools too fast to crystallize.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩冷却得太快、来不及结晶时就形成火山玻璃。
senses.why: the adjective names the origin of the material, while glass names its structure, so the phrase combines a source and a texture.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指明材料的来源，玻璃指明其结构，因此这个短语把来源与质地组合在一起。

senses.title: Volcanic winter
senses.definition: a period of global cooling caused by ash and sulfur aerosols from a very large eruption blocking sunlight
senses.definitionCN: 极大规模喷发产生的灰与硫气溶胶遮挡阳光、造成全球降温的一段时期
senses.example: A large eruption can cause a volcanic winter that cools the whole planet.
senses.exampleCN: 一次大喷发可能引发火山冬天，使整个行星降温。
senses.why: climate science extended the adjective from the mountain to the planet, because the effects of an eruption travel far beyond the cone.
senses.whyCN: 气候科学把这个形容词从山体扩展到行星，因为喷发的影响会远远超出火山锥。

senses.title: Volcanic arc
senses.definition: a curved chain of volcanoes formed above a descending tectonic plate at a subduction zone
senses.definitionCN: 在俯冲带、位于下沉板块之上形成的一列弧形火山链
senses.example: The islands form a volcanic arc above the subducting plate.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿在俯冲板块之上构成一条火山弧。
senses.why: plate tectonics needed a term for a whole line of volcanoes, and the adjective turned a single mountain into a geographic pattern.
senses.whyCN: 板块构造学需要一个指整条火山链的术语，这个形容词把单座山变成了地理格局。

senses.title: Ready to explode, of temper or tension
senses.titleCN: 比喻：脾气或局势一触即发
senses.definition: extremely explosive, violent or unstable, used of a person's temper or of a tense situation
senses.definitionCN: 极其易爆、猛烈或不稳定的，用于人的脾气或紧张的局势
senses.example: His volcanic temper emptied the meeting room in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 他那火山般的脾气几秒钟内就让会议室空了。
senses.why: the metaphor is almost too easy: a volcano gives warning, then erupts, and so does a temper that has been held down too long.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻几乎太顺理成章：火山先有预兆再喷发，被压抑太久的脾气也是如此。

intro.en: Volcanic is volcano plus the adjective suffix -ic. Volcano reached English through Italian from Latin Volcanus, also spelled Vulcanus, the Roman god of fire and metalworking. The suffix -ic came from Greek -ikos by way of Latin -icus.
intro.cn: volcanic 是在表示火山的那个英语名词上加形容词后缀 -ic 构成。那个名词经意大利语来自拉丁 Volcanus（亦作 Vulcanus），即罗马的火与冶金之神。后缀 -ic 由希腊 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus 进入英语。

items.en: Volcanus was the Roman god of fire and the forge. His name was also given to burning ground and to the fire itself, which is why a mountain that burns bears it.
items.cn: Volcanus 是罗马的火与锻造之神。他的名字也被用于燃烧的地面与火本身，因此一座会燃烧的山沿用此名。

items.en: Italian vulcano named a burning mountain, and English borrowed the word as volcano, generally in the seventeenth century, through Italian or French.
items.cn: 意大利语中的火山之名本指「燃烧的山」，英语一般在十七世纪经意大利语或法语借入这个词，成为表示火山的名称。

items.en: The suffix -ic entered English from Latin -icus, itself from Greek -ikos, meaning belonging to or connected with; it turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 由拉丁 -icus 进入英语，而 -icus 又出自希腊 -ikos，意为「属于……的、与……有关的」；它把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.en: Volcanic was formed on volcano in the late eighteenth century, first describing rocks and terrain produced by fire, then widening to the whole subject.
items.cn: volcanic 于十八世纪后期在火山这一名词上构成，最初描述火造成的岩石与地貌，随后扩展到整个主题。

items.en: Geology added volcanic arc, volcanic glass and volcaniclastic; climatology added volcanic winter. All keep the original image of a mountain that burns.
items.cn: 地质学增添了火山弧、火山玻璃与火山碎屑等说法；气候学增添了火山冬天。它们都保留着「会燃烧的山」这一原初意象。

items.en: Two tiers of doubt: the origin of the god's name is uncertain, with an Etruscan source often suggested but never proved, a root question; the first date of the rock sense is only approximate, a dating question.
items.cn: 来源不确定，分两档：火神之名的来源不确定，常有人提出源自伊特鲁里亚语，但从未得到证实，属词根存疑；岩石义的首见年代只是约数，属年代存疑。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the volcano family; group two holds near neighbours that describe fire, rock and eruption.
note.cn: 第一组是建于火山这一词族之上的词；第二组是描述火、岩石与喷发的近义词。

entries.definition: The mountain itself, from which volcanic is formed by adding -ic; the direction is noun to adjective, never the reverse.
entries.definitionCN: 指山体本身；volcanic 是在它之上加 -ic 构成的形容词，方向是名词到形容词，绝非反向。

entries.definition: The whole set of processes by which magma reaches the surface; it names the activity, not a single mountain.
entries.definitionCN: 岩浆到达地表的整套过程；它指活动，而非单座山。

entries.definition: The scientific study of volcanoes and volcanic phenomena, built with the study suffix -logy.
entries.definitionCN: 研究火山与火山现象的科学，由表示「学科」的后缀构成。

entries.definition: In a volcanic manner or by volcanic action, as in a volcanically active region.
entries.definitionCN: 以火山的方式或由火山作用地，如「火山活动活跃的地区」。

entries.definition: Relating to rock solidified from magma or lava; broader than volcanic, because it also covers rock that cooled deep underground.
entries.definitionCN: 指由岩浆或熔岩固结而成的岩石；比 volcanic 更广，因为它也包括地下深处冷却的岩石。

entries.definition: Relating to an eruption or tending to burst out suddenly, used of volcanoes, skin rashes and tempers alike.
entries.definitionCN: 与喷发有关的，或倾向于突然爆发的，火山、皮疹与脾气都可用。

entries.definition: Made of fragments of hot rock and ash thrown out by an eruption, a narrower technical term than volcanic.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷发抛出的炽热岩石碎片与灰构成的，是比 volcanic 更窄的术语。

entries.definition: Burning or glowing like fire, or intensely passionate; it shares the heat image but not the geological meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 像火一样燃烧或发光的，或极其炽烈的；它共享「热」的意象，但没有地质含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin name, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁名称、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Volcan- is the fire god's name, so the root already contains a mountain that burns.
normal.cn: volcan- 就是火神的名字，因此词根本身已经含着一座会燃烧的山。

normal.en: The suffix -ic makes an adjective of belonging: relating to the fire mountain.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ic 造出表示归属的形容词：与那座火之山有关的。

normal.en: Volcanic describes origin and material; the noun names the mountain. Keep the direction straight.
normal.cn: volcanic 描述来源与材料，名词则指山本身；要把构词方向记牢。

normal.en: Each science borrows the adjective for its own object: winter, glass, arc, soil.
normal.cn: 每门学科都借这个形容词指自己的对象：冬天、玻璃、弧、土。

normal.en: The figurative use keeps the eruption: a volcanic temper erupts, it does not simmer.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留喷发的意象：火山般的脾气是爆发，而不是慢炖。

abstract.en: Picture a pressure cooker whose lid lifts before anyone expects it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只压力锅，锅盖在谁都没预料到的时候被顶起。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom silent because one person's anger fills it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室鸦雀无声，只因一个人的怒气充满了整个空间。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside green with vines growing on old ash.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山坡绿意盎然，藤蔓长在陈年的火山灰上。

examples.en: Volcanic ash grounded flights across the region.
examples.cn: 火山灰使整个地区的航班停飞。

examples.en: The vineyard thrives on volcanic soil.
examples.cn: 这片葡萄园在火山土上长势旺盛。

examples.en: He has a volcanic temper that shows up without warning.
examples.cn: 他有一种毫无预兆就爆发的火暴脾气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「volcan（火神）+ ic」——火神的山一喷就炸 → 火山的、火山岩的、一触即发的

root: 拉丁 Volcanus（罗马火神，亦作 Vulcanus）经意大利语进入英语，成为表示火山的那个名词；本词是在该名词上加希腊来源、经拉丁而来的形容词后缀 -ic 构成，方向是名词加后缀，而非反向派生。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one source: a mountain that opens and pours out fire, ash and stone. The adjective first marks the mountain, then its material, its activity, its gifts to soil, glass and climate, its geography, and finally an explosive human mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个源头展开：一座裂开并喷出火、灰与石的山。这个形容词先标记山体，再依次标记其材料、活动、对土壤与玻璃与气候的馈赠、其地理格局，最后落到人的爆发性情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mountain that opens and pours fire, ash and black glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座裂开、喷出火、灰与黑色玻璃的山。

branches.en: THE MOUNTAIN ITSELF: the plain adjective of belonging, with no special object yet.
branches.cn: 山体本身：最朴素的归属形容词，尚未挂上特定对象。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND PROCESS: what comes out of the mountain, and the act of it coming out.
branches.cn: 材料与过程：山喷出的东西，以及它喷出的那个动作。

branches.en: PRODUCTS ON LAND: the same material becomes fertile soil or natural glass.
branches.cn: 陆地上的产物：同一种材料变成肥沃的土或天然的玻璃。

branches.en: PLANETARY SCALE: one eruption reaches the climate, many eruptions make an arc.
branches.cn: 行星尺度：一次喷发触及气候，许多次喷发连成一道弧。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE FIRE: a person or a situation that holds pressure until it blows.
branches.cn: 比喻之火：一个人或一种局势积压着压力，直到炸开。

intro.en: Volcanic is a noun of place turned into an adjective by one suffix, and that same root supports a whole vocabulary of fire, rock and study.
intro.cn: volcanic 是由地名名词经一个后缀变成的形容词，而同一词根支撑起整套关于火、岩石与研究的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin Volcanus, the fire god, and the Greek-origin suffix -icus give volcanic and its relatives volcano, volcanism and volcanology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Volcanus（火神）与希腊来源的后缀 -icus 构成本词及其同族词，包括表示火山的那个名词、火山作用与火山学。

items.example: The stem volcan- names the fire god and his mountain.
items.exampleCN: 词干 volcan- 指火神与他的山。

items.example: The volcano rises from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 那座火山从海面升起。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns a noun of place into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把指地点的名词变成形容词。

items.example: The island has a volcanic origin.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛有火山成因。

items.example: The ridge was volcanically active for ages.
items.exampleCN: 这条山脊长期处于火山活动之中。

items.example: Volcanism shaped the whole plateau.
items.exampleCN: 火山作用塑造了整个高原。

items.example: Volcanology combines geology and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 火山学结合了地质学与化学。

items.example: The volcanologist measured the swelling of the cone.
items.exampleCN: 火山学家测量了锥体的膨胀。

items.example: The sediment is volcanogenic, not river-borne.
items.exampleCN: 这种沉积物是火山成因的，而非河流搬运的。

items.example: The cliff is built of volcaniclastic layers.
items.exampleCN: 这处崖壁由火山碎屑层构成。

latinEntries.meaning: the same god, the spelling behind the Italian name for a burning mountain
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一位火神的另一种拼写，也是意大利语火山之名的来源拼写

definition_zh: 外国市场；境外市场；他国需求与交易环境
definition_en: a market in a country other than one's own, seen from the standpoint of a home-based seller
core_image: 一道海关线把地图分成两半，本国的工厂在线的这一侧，线的另一侧是挂着不同旗子的店铺
scene: 出口部门的会议上，经理摊开地图，指着海外的几座城市说下一年要先去那里试销。 The team chose three foreign markets for the first year of sales.
sceneCN: 这里指「本国之外的市场」，对应第 1 个义项：相对于本国而言的其他国家市场；句意为团队选定了三个外国市场作为第一年的销售目标。画面要点：摊开的地图、海关线、不同旗帜的店铺标记。

pos.zh: 外国市场；境外市场（可数，复数 foreign markets）

derivatives.zh: 外国人（foreign 加表示人的后缀，语义从「境外的」转为「境外之人」）
陌生感；异域性（foreign 加名词后缀，指不属于本地的性质）
在国外出生的（foreign 加 born 构成的复合形容词）
市场；推销（短语的另一半，语义为交易场所或交易行为）
营销（market 加动名词后缀，语义从「市场」转为「开拓市场的工作」）

senses.title: A market outside one's own country
senses.definition: a market located in another country, considered in contrast to the home market
senses.definitionCN: 位于另一国的市场，与本国市场相对而言
senses.example: The team chose three foreign markets for the first year of sales.
senses.exampleCN: 团队选定了三个外国市场作为第一年的销售目标。
senses.why: Foreign comes from Latin foris 'outside', so a foreign market is literally the market outside the gate of one's own country.
senses.whyCN: foreign 出自拉丁 foris「门外」，因此外国市场字面上就是本国大门之外的市场。

senses.title: The market of one specific country
senses.titleCN: 某一个具体国家的市场
senses.definition: the market of a named country, with its own buyers, rules and habits
senses.definitionCN: 某个具名国家的市场，有其自身的买方、规则与习惯
senses.example: The German foreign market proved harder to enter than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 德国这一外国市场比预想的更难进入。
senses.why: The phrase can be counted, so each national market becomes a separate foreign market with its own features.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以计数，于是每个国家市场都成为一个具有自身特点的外国市场。

senses.title: Foreign demand for a product
senses.definition: the demand for a product that comes from buyers in other countries
senses.definitionCN: 来自他国买方对某产品的需求
senses.example: Foreign market demand for the vaccine outstripped supply.
senses.exampleCN: 境外市场对这种疫苗的需求超过了供给。
senses.why: Market also means the buyers themselves, so foreign market demand is demand located beyond the border.
senses.whyCN: market 也可指买方本身，因此境外市场需求就是位于边界之外的需求。

senses.title: The act of entering a foreign market
senses.titleCN: 进入外国市场这一动作
senses.definition: the process of establishing sales in a country other than one's own
senses.definitionCN: 在本国之外的国家建立销售的过程
senses.example: Foreign market entry usually begins with a local partner.
senses.exampleCN: 进入外国市场通常从本地伙伴开始。
senses.why: From a firm's viewpoint the market is a door, and the phrase becomes a stage in an expansion plan.
senses.whyCN: 从企业视角看，市场是一道门，这个短语于是成为扩张计划中的一个阶段。

senses.title: Share held in markets abroad
senses.titleCN: 在境外市场所占的份额
senses.definition: the portion of sales in other countries held by a firm or country
senses.definitionCN: 某企业或某国在他国销售中所占的部分
senses.example: The brand holds a tenth of the foreign market in cosmetics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌在化妆品境外市场中占十分之一。
senses.why: Share language turns the market into a pie, and the foreign adjective marks which pie is being divided.
senses.whyCN: 份额说法把市场变成一块饼，foreign 这个形容词标明被分的是哪一块饼。

senses.title: The rules and conditions abroad
senses.titleCN: 境外的规则与经营条件
senses.definition: the legal, tariff and commercial conditions that govern trade in another country
senses.definitionCN: 管束他国贸易的法律、关税与商业条件
senses.example: Tariffs and labelling rules shape each foreign market differently.
senses.exampleCN: 关税与标签规则使每个外国市场各不相同。
senses.why: A market is not only buyers but also the rules around them, so the phrase often appears beside regulation and risk.
senses.whyCN: 市场不只是买方，还包括围绕他们的规则，因此这个短语常与监管、风险并置。

senses.title: Foreign buyers as a customer group
senses.titleCN: 作为客户群的境外买方
senses.definition: the group of customers abroad that a seller treats as one audience
senses.definitionCN: 境外被卖方当作一个客户群体对待的买方
senses.example: The catalogue was rewritten for a foreign market.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产品目录为外国市场重新编写。
senses.why: Marketing treats the foreign market as an audience with shared tastes, which is why catalogues and campaigns are adapted.
senses.whyCN: 营销把外国市场当作有共同口味的受众，因此目录与推广都要改写。

senses.title: Any unfamiliar arena outside one's own
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：自己圈子之外的陌生场域
senses.definition: an unfamiliar external setting in which one must compete or prove oneself
senses.definitionCN: 必须在其间竞争或证明自己的陌生外部场域
senses.example: For a local painter, the capital was a foreign market in every sense.
senses.exampleCN: 对一位本地画家来说，首都在任何意义上都是一个陌生的外部市场。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops trade and keeps only outsideness: any field where one is an outsider qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉贸易，只保留「在外」：任何自己是外人的领域都符合。

intro.en: Foreign market joins foreign, from Latin foris 'outside', with market, from Latin mercatus 'trade'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: foreign market 把出自拉丁 foris「门外」的 foreign，与出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」的 market 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Foris meant 'outside, out of doors', and it built adjectives about what lies beyond a boundary.
items.cn: foris 意为「在外、门外」，构成一批表示「边界之外」的形容词。

items.en: Foranus 'outside, exterior' passed through Old French as forain, giving English foreign in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: foranus「外部的、外面的」经古法语 forain 传入，在 15 世纪形成英语 foreign。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise'.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或市场，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「货物」。

items.en: English borrowed market through Latin and French, and it soon covered both the place and the demand found there.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁语与法语借入 market，很快既指地点，也指那里出现的需求。

items.en: Foreign market became standard in export practice, usually in contrast with the home or domestic market.
items.cn: foreign market 在出口实务中成为标准说法，通常与本国市场或国内市场相对。

note.en: The first group shares the outside root or looks close to it; the second group names markets that differ by whose viewpoint is taken.
note.cn: 第一组共享「在外」词根或与之外形相近；第二组是按立场区分的不同市场。

entries.definition: A person from another country; the root describes outsideness, but the word names a human, not a market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自另一国的人；词根表示「在外」，但这个词指人，不指市场。

entries.definition: A large wooded area, from medieval Latin forestis silva 'the wood outside', built on foris; it shares the root but means woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 大片林地，出自中世纪拉丁 forestis silva「外面的林子」，由 foris 构成；同根但指树林。

entries.definition: To lose something as a penalty, from foris 'outside' plus facere 'do', originally to do something outside the law.
entries.definitionCN: 因受罚而失去某物，出自 foris「在外」加 facere「做」，原指做了法外之事。

entries.definition: A public square or debate setting, from Latin forum; it looks like foreign but has no connection to foris.
entries.definitionCN: 公共广场或讨论场所，出自拉丁 forum；它与 foreign 形近，却与 foris 无关。

entries.definition: A market across the sea from the seller's country; foreign market is wider because a neighbour across a land border also counts.
entries.definitionCN: 从卖方国家隔海相望的市场；foreign market 范围更宽，因为陆上邻国也算。

entries.definition: The foreign market viewed as a destination for exports; it stresses the trade flow rather than the market itself.
entries.definitionCN: 作为出口目的地看待的外国市场；它强调贸易流向，而不是市场本身。

entries.definition: Trade conducted across national borders; it is neutral, while foreign market is always seen from one country's side.
entries.definitionCN: 跨国家进行的贸易；它保持中性，而 foreign market 始终从某一国的立场看。

entries.definition: The market where currencies are traded; it contains the same adjective but the trade is money, not goods or services.
entries.definitionCN: 交易货币的市场；它带同一个形容词，但交易对象是货币，不是货物或服务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the outside root, the trade root and real export phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「在外」词根、交易词根与真实出口搭配。

normal.en: Foreign means outside the gate; market means trade; the phrase is trade beyond one's own gate.
normal.cn: foreign 意为大门之外，market 意为交易，短语就是本国大门之外的交易。

normal.en: The two halves have separate Latin sources: foris for outside, mercatus for trade.
normal.cn: 两半各有拉丁来源：foris 表「在外」，mercatus 表「交易」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: enter a foreign market, foreign market share, foreign market entry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：进入外国市场、境外市场份额、外国市场进入。

normal.en: The phrase always implies a viewpoint: a market is foreign only relative to somebody's home.
normal.cn: 这个短语始终隐含一个立场：市场只有相对于某人的本国才叫外国市场。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with the currency market, which uses the same adjective but trades money.
normal.cn: 不要与货币市场混淆，后者带同一个形容词，却交易金钱。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a map with a gate in it, and the shops on the far side fly other flags.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着一条线，线上有一道门，线那侧的店铺挂着别的旗子。

abstract.en: Picture a merchant who must learn a new language before he can read the price tags.
abstract.cn: 想象一位商人必须先学会一门新语言，才看得懂价签。

abstract.en: Picture an artist whose own town is small, so every larger city feels like another country.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家，自己的镇子很小，于是每座大城都像另一个国度。

examples.en: The firm opened a branch to serve the foreign market directly.
examples.cn: 这家公司开设分公司，直接服务外国市场。

examples.en: Local tastes forced a redesign for each foreign market.
examples.cn: 本地口味迫使公司为每个外国市场重新设计。

examples.en: Foreign market sales now exceed domestic ones.
examples.cn: 境外市场销售额如今超过了国内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门外的集市」——foris 是门外，market 是集市，本国门外的集市就是外国市场

root: foreign 出自拉丁 foris「门外」，经 foranus、古法语 forain 进入英语；market 出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」。合指「本国之外的市场」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all take a viewpoint: a market outside the home country, one named country's market, its demand, the act of entering it, a share of it, its rules, its buyers as an audience, and finally any unfamiliar arena.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都带一个立场：本国之外的市场、某一国的市场、其需求、进入它的动作、在其中所占份额、它的规则、作为受众的买方，最后是任何陌生的外部场域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line with shops on the far side flying other flags.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界线，线那侧的店铺挂着别的旗子。

branches.en: BASE OUTSIDENESS: the market lies beyond one's own border.
branches.cn: 基础的外在性：市场位于本国边界之外。

branches.en: NAMED AND COUNTED: each country is a market, and its buyers are demand.
branches.cn: 具名与计量：每个国家都是一个市场，其买方构成需求。

branches.en: FIRM ACTION: the market is entered, then measured by share.
branches.cn: 企业行动：先进入市场，再用份额衡量。

branches.en: RULES AND AUDIENCE: tariffs govern it, and buyers form an audience.
branches.cn: 规则与受众：关税管束它，买方构成受众。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any unfamiliar arena can be called foreign.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何陌生的场域都可以被称为「外国」。

intro.en: Foreign market is a phrase of two free words, one about outsideness and one about trade, each with its own Latin line.
intro.cn: foreign market 是由两个自由词构成的短语，一个讲「在外」，一个讲交易，各有拉丁线索。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris 'outside' gives foreign, foreigner and forest; Latin mercatus 'trade' gives market, marketing, marketplace and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foris「门外」衍生 foreign、foreigner 与 forest；拉丁 mercatus「交易」衍生 market、marketing、marketplace 与 merchant。

items.example: The element marks what lies beyond a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分标出边界之外的事物。

items.example: They studied foreign languages.
items.exampleCN: 他们学习外语。

items.example: A foreigner opened the shop.
items.exampleCN: 一位外国人开了这家店。

items.example: The accent gave a mild foreignness.
items.exampleCN: 这口音带来一丝异域感。

items.example: The forest lay beyond the river.
items.exampleCN: 森林在河的那一边。

items.meaning: a place or system of trade
items.example: The market opens early.
items.exampleCN: 市场开得早。

items.example: Marketing costs rose.
items.exampleCN: 营销成本上升了。

items.example: The marketplace was crowded.
items.exampleCN: 市场里很拥挤。

items.example: The merchant sold cloth.
items.exampleCN: 这位商人卖布。

items.example: They entered a foreign market.
items.exampleCN: 他们进入了一个外国市场。

latinEntries.structure: foris (adverb and ablative plural of fores, door)

definition_zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地；法律文书开头陈述的事实；以……为前提预先提出
definition_en: a statement accepted as true and used as the basis of an argument, or (in the plural) a building and its land
core_image: 长桌的四条桌腿先稳稳立住，桌面上才摆得下一层层叠起的论证卡片
scene: 辩论开始前，主持人提醒双方先确认共同接受的基本判断，否则后面的推论都无处落脚。 The whole argument rests on a premise that nobody has tested.
sceneCN: 这里指论证所依据的基本判断（第 1 个义项：作为论证基础的前提命题）；句意为整个论证都建立在一个无人检验过的前提上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地
以……为前提预先提出（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地；营业场所」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学中的另一种拼写，义同「前提」
由「前提」与「基于」复合而成，义为「以前提为基础的」

senses.title: A proposition that supports an argument
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true so that a conclusion can be drawn from it
senses.definitionCN: 作为真实陈述提出、以便从中推出结论的命题
senses.example: The main premise of the essay is that prices reflect information.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的主要前提是价格反映信息。
senses.why: The Latin word meant something sent before, and this sense places the statement ahead of the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本义是「事先送出之物」，这一义项把它放在结论之前。

senses.title: An assumption taken without proof
senses.titleCN: 未加证明就接受的假设
senses.definition: a belief that a study or person accepts as true without testing it
senses.definitionCN: 研究或个人未经检验就当作真实的信念
senses.example: The model works only if its premise about human rationality holds.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当模型关于人类理性的假设成立时，它才有效。
senses.why: What is put before an argument is often simply granted, which is how a premise becomes an assumption.
senses.whyCN: 放在论证之前的东西常被直接认可，「前提」由此变成「假设」。

senses.title: The major premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the general statement from which a syllogism begins, before the minor premise is applied
senses.definitionCN: 三段论起始的一般性陈述，在其后接上小前提
senses.example: The major premise says all mammals are warm-blooded.
senses.exampleCN: 大前提说所有哺乳动物都是温血的。
senses.why: Logic gave the word a fixed slot: the general claim sits first, and the specific case is placed under it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学给这个词一个固定位置：一般性主张坐第一，具体事例被置于其下。

senses.title: The minor premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the specific statement that brings a particular case under the general one
senses.definitionCN: 把具体事例归入一般陈述之下的特定陈述
senses.example: The minor premise states that this animal is a mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提陈述这只动物是哺乳动物。
senses.why: The second slot in the syllogism is also called a premise, since both statements must be granted before the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 三段论中的第二个位置同样称为前提，因为两个陈述都必须先被认可，结论才成立。

senses.title: A building and its land
senses.definition: the buildings and the ground belonging to a business or an owner, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 属于某企业或业主的建筑物与土地，用复数形式
senses.example: The inspectors walked through the factory premises.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员走遍了工厂的场地。
senses.why: Legal deeds opened by describing the property set before the reader, and that list of property became the buildings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律契约开头先描述摆在读者面前的财产，这份财产清单后来就指建筑物本身。

senses.title: The property recited in a deed
senses.titleCN: 法律文书开头陈述的财产
senses.definition: the opening part of a legal instrument that sets out the facts and property concerned
senses.definitionCN: 法律文书开头说明相关事实与财产的部分
senses.example: The lease recites the premises before stating the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约在说明租金之前先陈述标的财产。
senses.why: The word names what is placed in front of the operative clauses, so it labels that opening recital.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指放在操作性条款之前的内容，因此用来指开头的陈述部分。

senses.title: A condition treated as given
senses.titleCN: 模型中当作给定的条件
senses.definition: a condition that a model or calculation accepts as fixed before it begins
senses.definitionCN: 模型或计算在开始之前就当作固定条件的设定
senses.example: The estimate rests on the premise that fuel prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这一估算建立在燃料价格持平的假设之上。
senses.why: A model must fix something before it can move, and whatever is fixed is literally placed in front.
senses.whyCN: 模型必须先固定某些东西才能运转，被固定者正被摆在最前面。

senses.title: A claim a debate must grant
senses.titleCN: 辩论中须先接受的主张
senses.definition: a statement that one side asks the other to accept before the exchange can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 一方要求另一方在交锋开始前先接受的主张
senses.example: The judge asked whether both sides shared that premise.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人问双方是否共有那个前提。
senses.why: Debate is an argument built in public, so it needs a floor of agreed statements under it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论是当众搭建的论证，因此需要一层公认陈述作地板。

senses.title: To state something beforehand
senses.definition: to set something out in advance as a basis for what follows
senses.definitionCN: 事先把某内容摆出来，作为后续论述的基础
senses.example: Let me premise my answer with one condition.
senses.exampleCN: 请允许我先以一个条件作为回答的前提。
senses.why: The verb kept the Latin sense of sending something ahead, and English uses it rarely, mostly in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「事先送出」的意思，英语中很少用，多见于正式书面语。

intro.en: Premise comes from Latin praemissa, things sent before, from praemittere, to send ahead. Logic took the word for the statements placed before a conclusion, and law took it for the property described at the start of a deed; the plural then became the buildings themselves.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」，出自动词「预先送出」。逻辑学用它指放在结论之前的陈述，法律用它指契约开头描述的财产，其复数随后就指建筑物本身。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go, and it stands behind words of sending, such as mission and transmit.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「送、放出」，英语中表示发送的词多出自它。

items.en: The prefix prae- added «in front», so the verb meant to send something ahead of what follows.
items.cn: 前缀加上「在前」，于是动词意为把某物先于后续内容送出去。

items.en: The neuter plural named the things set before a conclusion, and logic adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 中性复数指放在结论之前的内容，逻辑学把它采用为术语。

items.en: Translations of Aristotle fixed major and minor premise as the two statements above and below the conclusion.
items.cn: 对亚里士多德著作的翻译固定了「大前提」与「小前提」，即结论之上与之下的两个陈述。

items.en: Deeds opened by reciting the property, and the plural premises came to mean that property and then the buildings on it.
items.cn: 契约开头先陈述财产，复数形式便指该财产，随后又指其上的建筑物。

items.en: The building sense now lives almost entirely in the plural, while the logic sense keeps the singular; the split's exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 建筑物义如今几乎只存在于复数，逻辑义则保留单数；两者分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root or looks close; the second group names other starting points of reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根或形近；第二组指推理的其他起点。

entries.definition: The plural noun for a building and its land, from the property clause of a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指房屋及场地，来自契约中的财产条款。

entries.definition: Based on a stated assumption; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某陈述假设为基础的，是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: The older spelling used in logic for a stated proposition.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑学中指前提命题的旧拼写。

entries.definition: First in rank; it belongs to the Latin word for first, not to sending ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位最高的；属于拉丁语「第一」，与「预先送出」无关。

entries.definition: A bonus or an insurance payment; it comes from the word for reward.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖金或保险费；来自表示报酬的词。

entries.definition: A declaration that one will do something; its root is to send forth a word, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示将做某事的声明；其词根是「送出话语」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true without evidence, often silently.
entries.definitionCN: 指无证据而被接受为真的东西，常是默许的。

entries.definition: A belief that must already hold for a statement to make sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个陈述要成立就必须先已存在的信念。

entries.definition: A statement that can be judged true or false.
entries.definitionCN: 指可判断真假的陈述。

entries.definition: A tentative explanation offered for testing, not merely granted.
entries.definitionCN: 指提出来供检验的暂时解释，而不只是被认可。

entries.definition: A principle accepted without proof as a starting point.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需证明即被接受作为出发点的原理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the table-leg picture, the syllogism slots, the legal deed and the everyday plural.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用桌腿画面、三段论的两个位置、法律契约与日常复数用法。

normal.en: A premise is sent before the conclusion, just as a table leg is placed before the table top.
normal.cn: 前提先于结论送出，正如桌腿先于桌面立好。

normal.en: The major premise is the wide statement; the minor premise puts one case under it.
normal.cn: 大前提是宽的一般陈述，小前提把一个事例放到它下面。

normal.en: Premises in the plural are buildings, from the property clause at the head of a deed.
normal.cn: 复数形式指建筑物，来自契约开头的财产条款。

normal.en: A false premise makes a valid argument reach a wrong conclusion.
normal.cn: 前提错了，形式有效的论证也会得出错误结论。

normal.en: On the premise that is the everyday phrase that carries the logic sense into ordinary writing.
normal.cn: 「以……为前提」是把逻辑义带入日常写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: A premise is a floor that nobody looks at until the argument falls through it.
abstract.cn: 前提是一块地板，直到论证掉了下去，才有人低头看它。

abstract.en: Every model stands on statements it never proves, and that silence is what makes it usable.
abstract.cn: 每个模型都站在它从不证明的陈述上，正是这份沉默让它可用。

abstract.en: The same word can name a sentence and a building, because both are things set in front of you.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指一句话，也能指一栋楼，因为两者都是摆在你面前的东西。

examples.en: The study rests on the premise that memory declines with age.
examples.cn: 这项研究建立在记忆随年龄衰退这一前提上。

examples.en: If the premise is false, the conclusion cannot stand.
examples.cn: 如果前提错误，结论就站不住。

examples.en: Visitors must not smoke anywhere on the premises.
examples.cn: 访客不得在场地内任何地方吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞密斯」——「普」通人先「密」密接受的那句话，就是推理的前提

root: 拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」← praemittere「预先送出」= prae-「在前」+ mittere「送、放」。逻辑学经中世纪翻译固定「大前提、小前提」，法律契约开头的财产陈述引申出「房屋及场地」。十五世纪起见于英语；两义分化的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from logic to property: a supporting proposition, an untested assumption, the major and minor premises, buildings and land, a deed recital, a fixed model condition, a debated claim, and the rare verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从逻辑延伸到财产：支撑命题、未验证假设、大前提、小前提、房屋场地、契约陈述、模型条件、辩论主张，以及少用的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four legs are set down first, and only then can the stacked cards of argument rest on the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：先放下四条桌腿，论证的卡片堆才放得上桌面。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT FLOOR: the proposition that must be granted before debate can proceed.
branches.cn: 论证的地板：辩论开始前必须先被认可的那个命题。

branches.en: THE UNPROVED GRANT: assumptions that a person or a model simply accepts.
branches.cn: 未经证明的认可：人或模型直接接受的假设。

branches.en: THE TWO LOGIC SLOTS: the general statement and the case placed under it.
branches.cn: 逻辑的两个位置：一般陈述与置于其下的事例。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PROPERTY: the recited property and the buildings standing on it.
branches.cn: 法律上的财产：契约陈述的财产及其上的建筑物。

branches.en: THE RARE VERB: to send a condition ahead as a basis.
branches.cn: 少用的动词义：事先把一个条件送出作为基础。

intro.en: Premise is a Latin participle turned noun, and the same root that sends things ahead also produced words of mission and transmission.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的名词，同一个「预先送出」词根也产生了「使命」「传送」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies praemittere and praemissa; the logic and property senses both grew from the idea of things placed in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「预先送出」与「事先送出之物」；逻辑义与财产义都从「摆在前面之物」长出来。

items.example: It marks what is sent ahead.
items.exampleCN: 它标出事先送出的东西。

items.example: The root of mission and transmit.
items.exampleCN: 这是「使命」与「传送」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是该名词的直接来源。

items.example: It became the logic term for a premise.
items.exampleCN: 它成为逻辑术语「前提」。

items.example: It marks the rare English verb premise.
items.exampleCN: 它标明这个少用的英语动词。

items.example: The legal sense moved into everyday property talk.
items.exampleCN: 法律义进入日常财产用语。

items.meaning: a statement set before a conclusion
items.example: The everyday singular that carries the logic sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是承载逻辑义的日常单数形式。

items.example: It survives chiefly in British academic prose.
items.exampleCN: 它主要保留在英国学术写作中。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地」
加已然词尾，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学旧拼写，义为「前提」
复合形容词，义为「以前提为基础的」

definition_zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；细胞核的
definition_en: relating to a nucleus, especially the atomic nucleus or the cell nucleus
core_image: 一个极小的中心，周围绕着一圈电子或一层膜
scene: 这个国家大部分电力来自核电站。 The country gets most of its electricity from nuclear power plants.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear 指「核能的」（第 2 个义项：由原子核反应释放能量的）；句意：该国大部分电力来自核电站；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；核武器的；细胞核的；核心家庭的

derivatives.zh: 核；原子核；细胞核
核动力的
无核的
具备核能力的
核工程学（少用）

senses.title: Of the atomic nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 与原子核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear size is measured in femtometres.
senses.exampleCN: 原子核的尺度以飞米计。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun nucleus to atomic physics, where the centre of the atom is the object of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把 nucleus 直接接到原子物理上，那里研究的对象就是原子的中心。

senses.title: Nuclear energy
senses.definition: describing energy released by changes in atomic nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 指由原子核变化释放的能量
senses.example: Nuclear power supplies a fifth of the country's electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 核电供应全国五分之一的电力。
senses.why: Because the energy comes from the nucleus rather than from chemical bonds, the adjective names the source of the power.
senses.whyCN: 因为能量来自原子核而不是化学键，这个形容词命名的就是能量的来源。

senses.title: Nuclear weapons
senses.definition: describing weapons whose explosive force comes from nuclear reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指爆炸力来自核反应的武器
senses.example: The treaty limits the number of nuclear warheads.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约限制核弹头的数量。
senses.why: The same source of energy, released deliberately and instantly, yields a weapon, so the adjective marks the mechanism of the blast.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能量来源若被有意瞬间释放，就成为武器，因此这个形容词标出爆炸的机制。

senses.title: Nuclear physics
senses.definition: relating to the branch of physics that studies nuclei and their reactions
senses.definitionCN: 与研究核及其反应的物理分支有关
senses.example: Nuclear physics grew out of radioactivity research.
senses.exampleCN: 核物理学从放射性研究中发展出来。
senses.why: A discipline named after its object takes the adjective as a fixed modifier, as in nuclear physics or nuclear chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 以研究对象命名的学科会把形容词作为固定修饰语，如 nuclear physics 或 nuclear chemistry。

senses.title: Of the cell nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of a living cell
senses.definitionCN: 与活细胞的细胞核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear DNA is separated from the cytoplasm by a membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 核 DNA 由一层膜与细胞质隔开。
senses.why: Biology uses the same adjective for the cell's centre, and compounds such as nuclear envelope keep the two senses distinct by context.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用同一个形容词指细胞的中心，nuclear envelope 等复合词靠上下文把两个义项区分开。

senses.title: Nuclear family
senses.definition: describing a household of parents and their dependent children
senses.definitionCN: 指由父母与其未成年子女组成的家庭
senses.example: The survey compared nuclear and extended households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了核心家庭与大家庭。
senses.why: Social science borrowed the image of a small centre with close members, contrasting it with the wider extended family.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学借用「小核心加紧密成员」的意象，用来与更宽的扩展家庭相对照。

senses.title: Nuclear medicine
senses.definition: describing medical techniques that use radioactive substances
senses.definitionCN: 指使用放射性物质的医学技术
senses.example: Nuclear medicine scans reveal how an organ is working.
senses.exampleCN: 核医学扫描能显示器官的工作状况。
senses.why: Radioactive tracers are read by their nuclear emissions, so the medical branch is named after the physical process.
senses.whyCN: 放射性示踪剂靠其核辐射被读取，因此这个医学分支按物理过程命名。

senses.title: Nuclear envelope
senses.definition: describing the membrane that surrounds the cell nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 指包围细胞核的那层膜
senses.example: The nuclear envelope breaks down during mitosis.
senses.exampleCN: 核膜在有丝分裂过程中解体。
senses.why: An anatomical compound uses the adjective to say which structure the membrane belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学复合词用这个形容词说明这层膜属于哪个结构。

senses.title: Figurative extreme option
senses.definition: in politics, describing an extreme measure reserved as a last resort
senses.definitionCN: 政治语境中指留作最后手段的极端措施
senses.example: Both sides avoided the nuclear option in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在谈判中都避免使用极端手段。
senses.why: The destructive power of nuclear weapons supplies a metaphor for any step that would end the game.
senses.whyCN: 核武器的破坏力为任何「一出手就终结局面」的步骤提供了比喻。

intro.en: Nuclear is the adjective of nucleus, formed with -ar; its history splits between atomic physics and cell biology.
intro.cn: nuclear 是 nucleus 的形容词，由 -ar 构成；它的历史分为原子物理与细胞生物学两条线。

items.en: Nucleus, diminutive of nux 'nut', meant a kernel. English borrowed the noun in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 是 nux「坚果」的指小形式，意为果仁。英语在 17 世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective nuclear is recorded in the 19th century in general senses such as 'relating to a kernel or centre'. The precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 nuclear 在 19 世纪有「与果核或中心有关的」这类一般义。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Robert Brown's nucleus gave biology its own central body, and nuclear later described the structures around it.
items.cn: Robert Brown 的 nucleus 为生物学提供了自己的中心小体，nuclear 后来用于描述它周围的结构。

items.en: Rutherford's model placed nearly all atomic mass in a tiny nucleus, and nuclear physics was born around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福的模型把原子几乎全部质量放进一个极小的核，核物理学约在 1911 至 1912 年诞生。

items.en: The nuclear age fixed the word in public language through weapons and power stations, adding figurative uses such as the nuclear option.
items.cn: 1945 年之后的核时代通过武器与电站把这个词固定进公共语言，并增加了「极端手段」这类比喻用法。

note.en: The first group separates nuclear from the noun and from near-looking words; the second separates its atomic sense from its biological and social senses.
note.cn: 第一组把 nuclear 与名词及形近词分开；第二组把它的原子义与生物、社会义分开。

entries.definition: The central body itself; nuclear is the adjective used in nuclear power, nuclear physics or nuclear envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 指中心小体本身；nuclear 是用于 nuclear power、nuclear physics、nuclear envelope 的形容词。

entries.definition: A structure inside the cell nucleus, not the nucleus; it is a noun and never replaces nuclear as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内的一个结构，不是细胞核本身；它是名词，不能像 nuclear 那样作修饰语。

entries.definition: Used almost only in nucleic acid; it refers to the chemistry of nuclei, not to nuclear energy.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎只用于 nucleic acid；它指核的化学，而不是核能。

entries.definition: Relating to atoms as wholes; atomic energy can mean energy from the atom generally, while nuclear pins it to the nucleus.
entries.definitionCN: 指与整个原子有关的；atomic energy 可泛指原子能，而 nuclear 明确限定在原子核。

entries.definition: Describing unstable nuclei that emit radiation; a material can be radioactive without being part of a nuclear reactor.
entries.definitionCN: 指不稳定的核发出辐射；某种材料可以具有放射性，却与核反应堆无关。

entries.definition: Located at the middle; it is the everyday word for position and never means atomic or cell nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于中间，是表示位置的日常词，从不指原子核或细胞核。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus + -ar: the adjective of the kernel.
normal.cn: nucleus + -ar：果核的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs nucleus, nuclear-powered, nuclear-free and nucleonics.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nucleus、nuclear-powered、nuclear-free、nucleonics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: nuclear power, nuclear weapon, nuclear family, nuclear envelope.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：核能、核武器、核心家庭、核膜。

normal.en: Context decides whether the nucleus is in an atom or in a cell.
normal.cn: 上下文决定这个核是在原子里还是在细胞里。

normal.en: The nuclear option is a metaphor borrowed from the bomb.
normal.cn: nuclear option 是从核弹借来的比喻。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny sun with a nucleus at the centre and electrons in orbit.
abstract.cn: 原子像一颗微型太阳，原子核在中心，电子在轨道上。

abstract.en: A nuclear family is a small core with a clear boundary, like a nucleus with its membrane.
abstract.cn: 核心家庭像一个有清晰边界的小核心，如同带膜的细胞核。

abstract.en: The nuclear option is the move that ends the game, like a bomb in a board game.
abstract.cn: 极端手段是终结整局棋的那一步，就像棋盘游戏里的炸弹。

examples.en: Nuclear power produces electricity without burning coal.
examples.cn: 核能发电不燃烧煤炭。

examples.en: The nuclear envelope separates the cell's DNA from the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 核膜把细胞的 DNA 与细胞质隔开。

examples.en: The country expanded its nuclear medicine programme.
examples.cn: 该国扩大了核医学项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus（核）+ -ar」→ 跟核有关的 → 原子核的、核能的、细胞核的

root: 拉丁语 nux「坚果」→ nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；加形容词后缀 -ar 构成 nuclear。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide into three families: atomic physics and its power and weapons, cell biology and its envelope, and social or figurative cores such as the nuclear family and the nuclear option.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分成三族：原子物理及其能量与武器，细胞生物学及其核膜，以及核心家庭、极端手段这类社会或比喻性的核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny centre with electrons or a membrane wrapped around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个极小的中心，外面绕着一圈电子或一层膜。

branches.en: ATOMIC SCIENCE: the nucleus as an object of study and the discipline built around it.
branches.cn: 原子科学：作为研究对象的原子核，以及围绕它建立的学科。

branches.en: ENERGY AND MEDICINE: power from the nucleus, weapons from the same source, and radioactive tracers.
branches.cn: 能量与医学：来自核的能量，同源的武器，以及放射性示踪剂。

branches.en: CELL BIOLOGY: the nucleus of a living cell and the membrane around it.
branches.cn: 细胞生物学：活细胞的细胞核及其周围的膜。

branches.en: SOCIAL CORE: the small household built around parents and children.
branches.cn: 社会核心：围绕父母与子女建立的小家庭。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the destructive force of the bomb becomes a last-resort political move.
branches.cn: 比喻：核弹的破坏力变成政治上最后才用的手段。

intro.en: Nuclear adds the Latin adjective ending -ar to nucleus; the word then multiplies in compounds.
intro.cn: nuclear 在 nucleus 后加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ar；随后在复合词中大量增殖。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and nucleus supply the root; -ar comes from Latin -aris. Compounds such as nuclear-powered and nuclear-free are English formations.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 与 nucleus 提供词根；-ar 来自拉丁语 -aris。nuclear-powered、nuclear-free 等复合词是英语构造。

items.example: Nuclear reactions change the identity of atoms.
items.exampleCN: 核反应改变原子的身份。

items.example: The nucleus is the cell's control centre.
items.exampleCN: 细胞核是细胞的控制中心。

items.example: A nuclear-powered submarine can stay under for months.
items.exampleCN: 核动力潜艇能在水下停留数月。

items.example: The zone was declared nuclear-free.
items.exampleCN: 该区域被宣布为无核区。

items.example: Nucleonics covers reactors and isotopes.
items.exampleCN: 核工程学涵盖反应堆与同位素。

items.example: Atomic theory predates nuclear physics.
items.exampleCN: 原子论早于核物理学。

items.example: Radioactive waste needs long storage.
items.exampleCN: 放射性废料需要长期储存。

items.example: The nuclear envelope has pores.
items.exampleCN: 核膜上有孔。

items.example: Nuclear fission releases heat.
items.exampleCN: 核裂变释放热量。
